# An Efficient Student Relationship Automation Using Multimodal Temporal Convolution Networks and Ranked Resolving Computations

S. Muruganandam,^([^(15)](#fn15))

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-18](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-18)

## Abstract

Organizational process optimization is critical to meet the challenges of today, especially in educational institution environments, where information flow is very rapid, and the actors involved are different in their decision-making approach. Use of various communication mediums like phone calls or emails is highly diversified which may lead to missing important notifications from both the students and the placement cell. Most of the currently used real-time platforms are either third- party specific or don’t provide an exemplary performance. Most of the existing solutions make use of only chat-based workflow that doesn’t involve any filtering capabilities. Thus, we develop an extensive novel approach to increase the productivity of an organization, to consolidate the entire process into a single thread using the Ranked resolver approach and deep learning techniques.

Keywords: Temporal Convolution Networks, Ranked resolver model, Transfer model, Dual Authority, Cloud computing Storage, Integrity, Authentication

## Introduction

Any organization, anywhere in the globe, must prioritize the management and resolution of queries. Each day, an educational institution may have to deal with tens of thousands of inquiries from students reporting a variety of issues. The primary necessity to cope with bottleneck circumstances is for the institution to be able to respond to inquiries promptly. This gives the institution a competitive advantage. Human experts are frequently grouped into expert groups with the knowledge to handle particular kinds of issues in order to manage query resolution successfully. The sorts of reported issues vary as systems and third-party apps get more complicated.

## Related Work

The management of communications is essential to how businesses interact with their clients. A company that wishes to promote a message must first determine who its target market is and what makes them unique. Then, one should consider the quickest and most reliable way to reach that audience.

By initially identifying these factors, a communications specialist can more effectively personalize a message for a particular target. It’s important to keep in mind while assessing communication needs that a company must maintain healthy growth in order to gain input from both employees and clients. This approach, referred to as “open communication,” is widely applied.

A company should focus on the easiest ways for audiences to provide feedback and then design techniques to make it happen rapidly. Likewise, due to the multitude of channels of communication prevalent in the digital age, authorities in communications management must quickly adapt to new breakthroughs to ensure their audiences are being addressed.

The front-end area’s sole goal was to generate problems and send them to the appropriate problem-handling department. For instance, they offer a section for electrical issues. The company’s troubles with ticket distribution led them to adopt a machine learning algorithm to categorize the tickets as they entered the system. For the best result, they combined Random Forest and Support Vector Machine ([Fuchs et al., 2022](#ch18.xhtml#ref18_1)). In order to visualize the application of the ticketing system, this article suggests gathering all the data from employees’ ticketing systems.

Additionally, they determine priorities to address system entry tickets in accordance with SLA ([Aglibar & Rodelas, 2022](#ch18.xhtml#ref18_3)). The technical issues addressed are with the cloud, the wasteful resource distribution, and an introduction to new technologies like Alops for ticketing systems are discussed ([Chen et al., 2020](#ch18.xhtml#ref18_4)). [Adiyanto & Nurasiah (2019)](#ch18.xhtml#ref18_5) address in this paper, to create of a ticket system for customer relationship management to increase the organization’s statistics and performance. It was developed in order to save money and time for customer conflicts. It can manage large amounts of data but requires internet connectivity all the time.

In the context of network event monitoring, alerts are useful notifications that provide IT management employees with information regarding incidents. Because they are often generated automatically by network equipment and monitoring systems, they frequently only contain technical information that is accessible to the systems producing them.

But in this circumstance, ticketing systems serve a different purpose.

Tickets are a representation of incidents from a business standpoint. They are often developed by human activity and contain more semantic information about both the present and the past. The main premise of this study is that including ticketing data in the alert correlation process will enhance the timeliness, correctness, and comprehensiveness of incident descriptions throughout the incident resolution lifecycle ([Gohil & Kumar, 2019](#ch18.xhtml#ref18_6); [Salah et al., 2018](#ch18.xhtml#ref18_7)).

A model utilizing expert profiles and social profiles to provide recommendations for the tickets to be sent to the appropriate experts to be resolved. They conducted several experiments to determine the model’s efficacy, and they found that the suggested model had a lot of promise (Xu & He, 2018). A classification scheme to send the ticket to the appropriate division (Kormpho et al., 2018). They chose to create a deep neural network model to rank each ticket as it entered the system. If a ticket contained a lot of redundant terms, it could not be effectively classified ([Baral et al., 2017](#ch18.xhtml#ref18_10)).

The ticket is word-by-word extracted when it enters the system, labeled appropriately, and then attached to the appropriate cluster. The algorithm used by this system is Agglomerative clustering analysis which is used for incident categorization depending on the variables involved. The approach of the ticketing system with the help of another machine learning algorithm known as K Nearest Neighbor, this algorithm is not only used just for classification but it has also used in ticket resolving redundant tickets which continuously enter the system (Zhou et al., 2015).

To enhance the incident management procedure, an appropriately structured incident ticket system is created. We offer a general concept for ticket classification here. ## 3\. Proposed System Architecture

Initially, here in the paper with the usage of an educational institution database, an instance of a query is created. The generated query is sent to the server of the organization’s console. Thus, generated queries are classified with the use of deep neural networks and a matching score which can be deliberated using the ranked resolver and routing methods. The matching score further filters out the queries with respect to the subdivisions. The classified and clustered tickets are reconciled and resolved by the respective departments and the stored queries are further used for the learning of the system.

### Database and enumerated preprocessing

The process of gathering datasets from diverse sources is referred to as data collection. It’s possible for the collected raw data to be labelled or not. Manual labelling must be done if the item is not labeled. When an object is encountered

in data without a label, data labeling enables a learning model to recognize that particular class. Data labeling entails adding labels to raw picture data that describe the class to which the object belongs. The organization’s data collection process was adopted because it already had a database of the clients it served. The construction of this work makes use of a database from an educational institution. As only dominating and conspicuous features are required for the verification of just integral processes, only specified preprocessing is carried out. With the highest certainty, the data were retrieved from the institution.

### Temporal Convolutional Network

An input layer, hidden layers, convolutional layers between them, and output layers make up the foundation of CNN’s architecture. Secret layers come together. Intermediate results are consolidated and aggregated using pooling layers. A nonlinear function that defines a mapping of input values to outputs is attempted to be derived using fully connected layers. TCN, like RNN, has a cost or loss function that it aims to reduce in order to reduce prediction error.

![Fig. 2. Temporal Convolutional Network](images/fig18_2_C.jpg)

Fig. 2. Temporal Convolutional Network

An operation in integral calculus is convolution. Convolution determines the integral of the product of two functions, one of which is the inverse and transposed. The convolution function describes how two functions interact to change one’s shape.

Convolution analyses the similarity between two series or sequences, much like cross- correlation does. In computer vision, the input to a certain node is referred to as a receptive field or patch. Each node in the network receives information from a small portion of its previous layer, called the node’s receptive field.

**Input:** A sequence of inputs X with length T and number of features F, kernel size K, number of filters F’, and output dimension 0.

**Output:** A sequence of outputs Y with length T’ and dimension 0.

Initialize weights W with random values. For each time step tin the input sequence:

1.  Extract the input slice of length K centered at time t, resu lting in a tensor of shape (K, F).
2.  Perform a convolution operation on the input slice with the weights W, resulting in a tensor of shape (F’,).
3.  Apply an activation function (e.g., ReLU) to the output of the convolution.
4.  Append the resulting tensor to the output sequence Y.

Apply a fully connected layer with weights W\_ fc and bias b\_fc to the output sequence Y, resulting in a tensor of shape (T’, 0).

Apply a softmax function to the output tensor to obtain class probabilities.

TCN makes causal convolution certain. Only values found earlier in the input sequence should be used to determine an output value. The receptive field of a node is widened through diffusion in TCN to encompass more historical eras.

### Routing based on the ranked resolution

In this study, the routing system and ranked resolver together enhance efficiency, reliability, and resolution time while also helping to locate the matching score and permitting queries to reach the

proper subdivisions. The process that decides the path that data will take to move from one point to another is known as a routing algorithm. One of the major benefits of the method is the efficient management of Web traffic, which they promote. A data packet can choose from a number of paths after exiting its source to go to its destination. The routing algorithm formulae is as follows

  
$$\\begin{matrix} & {Pa\_{i} = \\lbrack P(k\_{1} \\mid a\_{i}),P(k\_{2} \\mid a\_{i}),} \\\\ & {P(k\_{3} \\mid a\_{i})\\ldots\\ldots..P(k\_{n} \\mid a\_{i})\\rbrack^{9}} \\\\ \\end{matrix}$$  

where P refers to the probability with a as the words mentioned in the queries and k are the keywords used by various teams.

### System of Aristotelian Logic

The approach of using inductive reasoning to transfer a given input to a result is known as Aristotelian logic. The mapping then creates a foundation for making decisions and spotting trends. Fuzzy inference is the process of using vfuzzy logic to transform an input into an output. The mapping then provides a basis for making decisions and spotting trends.

In this research, the specific type of material is connected to the appropriate classification strategy using a fuzzy inference model. The output of the classifier serves as its input. The implementation of various fuzzification techniques is facilitated by a fuzzification unit, which transforms the crisp input into fuzzy information. A knowledge base, which consists of a compilation of rule bases, is generated once precise information is converted into fuzzy input. The defuzzification unit’s fuzzy input is subsequently transformed into crisp value which is the output.

## Proposed Algorithm

This involves using convolutional layers to extract features from the data and then passing the features through a temporal layer to model the temporal dependencies in the data. The output of the temporal layer is then passed through a fully connected layer for classification, which determines the appropriate group for routing the query.

In conclusion, our study demonstrates the effectiveness of using complex algorithms, such as temporal convolutional networks, to consolidate queries from a large number of people and consumers.

![Fig. 3. Efficiency chart](images/fig18_3_C.jpg)

Fig. 3. Efficiency chart

## Conclusions

In this study, we have analyzed the performance of a technological software that consolidates queries from a large number of people and consumers. We have done so in a comprehensive manner, taking into account the expansion and development of human and technological processes, which has led to a significant increase in data and communication.

To address this issue, we have implemented a complex algorithm that uses temporal convolutional networks to efficiently route queries to the appropriate group.

Our results show that our implementation, Specifically, our algorithm improves the accuracy and speed of query routing, thereby reducing the response time for students and increasing satisfaction.

To further improve the performance of our algorithm, we suggest adding more classification-focused algorithms. This could potentially enhance the accuracy and efficiency of query routing, especially for complex or ambiguous queries. In terms of the algorithm used, we have implemented a temporal convolutional network to process sequential data, such as queries.

# Data Privacy Preservation with Optimization Technique for Effective Multi-Cloud Storage and Security

K. H. Vani^([^(16)](#fn16))

Corresponding Author Email Id: [vanikh524@gmail.com](mailto:vanikh524@gmail.com)

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-19](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-19)

## Abstract

Data volume has rapidly increased from a trillion bytes to a petabyte since the big data era began. Data needs high availability and scalability while storing and accessing it. Thanks to cloud storage presents the idea of a practically endless pool of storage resources. However, there are dangers associated with single cloud-based data storage, including dealer lock-in, privacy leaks, and unreliability. With geologically spreading cloud storage providers, multi-cloud storage could reduce these risks. Cost-effective with high availability user data is a significant need for the storage strategy. This paper presents the architecture for multi-cloud storage. Erasure coding is currently being used with several cloud security and providers in storage to expand failure tolerance and minimize vendor lock-in, among other benefits. In real fact, choosing providers and erasure coding parameters is the key to optimizing storage of multi-cloud and is also utilized for the privacy preservation model. Extensive tests on several cloud storage providers (CSPs) in the authentic world demonstrate the model’s efficacy. Finally, the performance study of the proposed Muddy Soil Fish Optimization Algorithm (MSFOA) based Multi-Objective Data-Privacy-Preservation-Tech

Keywords: Multi-cloud storage, Erasure coding, sanitization, security, restoration.

## Introduction

Since cloud storage-based services offer profitable architectures, the usage of remote storage systems is growing in popularity. In a pay-per- use business model, these infrastructures support the transmission, storage, and computationally expensive processing of outsourced data ([Aceto et al., 2013](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_1)). Commercial businesses and governmental agencies looking for more robust and cost-effective solutions are mostly to blame for the increased interest in cloud storage services. In a time when information technology services are more responsive, effective, and efficient, to put it another way, the advantages of using the cloud are quite real. Therefore, there is no longer a need to invest a lot of money on high-end hardware or pricey application software that they might never use again.

In a cloud network context, data security is crucial ([Singh & Chatterjee, 2017](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_2)). Cloud data contains a list of various security concerns, including those related to security applications, access and identity management, physical and audit planning, key and encryption management, and user access control (Li & Wang, 2018).These days, a variety of encryption algorithms are used to encrypt data. These algorithms have the power to transform text into an innovative structure called cipher text.

The security components of data processing and data storage make up privacy maintenance in cloud environments. In terms of data storage security, there are issues with guaranteeing user data privacy when this data is stored in a data center ([Gao et al., 2018](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_4); [Choi & Lee, 2015](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_5)). The challenges of maintaining user confidentiality during runtime on a virtual cloud platform are part of data processing security.

Unauthorized users cannot read this form of encrypted plain text input since it is encrypted. Similarly, by employing a different key, the algorithm to decode the data is generated by the encrypted data, which can then provide the authorized user with the original text.

The data sanitization and restoration processes make up the two key stages of the data privacy preservation paradigm ([Vani & Balamurugan, 2022](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_19)). Here, a unique meta-heuristic algorithm called MSFOA performs the optimal key creation based on the suggested sanitization method.

For better privacy data preservation, a sanitization and also restoration model that can find out the objective parameters like Hiding Failure rate (HR), Information Preservation rate (PR), False Rules generation rate (FR), Degree of Modification (DM), Compression Ratio (CR), tampering, and Low Pass Filter (LPF). An ideal key is developed during sanitization and restoration called Genetic Algorithm with Crow Search Algorithm ([Navale & Mali, 2019](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_21)) (GA- CSA) utilizing a hybrid module. Furthermore, the authorizer connected with the accepting end has restored the sensitive data successfully.

Alternatively, the authentication process is ineffective. For its users, cloud storage can offer practically infinite storage space. There has been a tendency of many businesses, organizations, government agencies, etc. to put their data in the cloud ([Computer sciences corp, 2015](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_6)).

However, employing a single CSP increases the risk of vendor lock-in and single-point failures ([Abu-Libdeh et al., 2010](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_7); [Chen et al., 2014](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_8)). As a result, recent works use multi-cloud storage, which depends on many CSPs to keep data at a particular level of redundancy ([Abu-Libdeh et al., 2010](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_7); [Chen et al., 2014](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_8); Mu et al., 2012). It can deliver greater servicing quality by preventing vendor lock-in and enhancing fault tolerance. Any

kind of application that should maintain a lot of data, namely document archiving, health records in electronic storage, or backup for data, might greatly benefit from these qualities.

Erasure coding ([Pless, 2011](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_10)), which can minimize the cost significantly in comparison to full replication of data storage ([Wu et al., 2013](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_11)), is typically used in these situations for additional improvement. It is also possible to minimize the whole data that needs to be carried across the network. Each data item in erasure coding is split into k equal blocks, and these types of blocks are then utilized to create encoded (total n blocks, n > k), (n-k) as data blocks. This is referred to as the parameters of erasure coding (n, k). These n blocks of data will be transferred to n various cloud storage providers, all of which will retain a single data block. Reproducing the original data object is possible using any k blocks from the available n ones. Erasure coding is a natural fit for multi-cloud storage.

The foremost contributions are as explained below.

*   To concentrate on developing a sanitizing procedure effectively for concealing the sensitive rules provided by various experts and users in multi-cloud storage.
*   To optimize by means of erasure coding, data is placed in many cloud storage systems.
*   To partition the coding as inner and outer coding, this is optimized twice using a new optimizer. This leads to dual utilization of optimizer.
*   To lessen the four sanitization obstacles of modification degree, information loss, hiding failure, and incorrect rule generation. • To propose multi-cloud storage and security
*   utilizing a Muddy Soil Fish Optimization Algorithm (MSFOA) combines with erasure coding.
*   To restore the original data effectively using this approach without error code.
*   To compare this approach with the relevant process and to provide better outcomes in their accessing time and latency comparisons after the evaluations of an optimizer.

## Related Works

Better characteristics like availability and scalability may be offered via multi-cloud storage. Current research uses erasure coding and several CSPs to minimize vendor lock-in and boost up fault tolerance, among other benefits. These efforts, however, only make sporadic use of multi-cloud storage, and none of them take the optimization issue generally into account. In actuality, choosing providers and erasure coding parameters wisely is the key to optimizing storage in multi-cloud progress. The data placement should also meet the needs of system or application developers. Such complicated necessity optimization cannot readily be fulfilled by ad hoc methods since developers frequently demand that many objectives be optimized simultaneously. This study introduces Triones, a methodical approach in multi-cloud storage that uses erasure coding to properly express the placement of data.

However, a lot of earlier works ((Mu et al., 2012; [Tang et al., 2022](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_25); [Saini & Kaur, 2022](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_28)) only employed multi-cloud storage with an erasure-coding foundation to accomplish a few capabilities. Erasure coding parameter (n, k) and cloud storage providers (n) make up a data assignment formation in multi-cloud storage. A further criterion for the optimization progress included in multi-cloud storage model is that it be sufficiently broad to take into account any future changes in variables and specifications. This is significant since cloud storage technology is currently evolving quickly.

### Single Cloud vs. Multi-Cloud Storage

Most works have utilized multi-cloud storage to set up the systems or apps in order to evade the drawbacks of single-cloud storage ( (Abu- Libdeh et al., 2010; Mu et al., 2012; [Saini & Kaur, 2022](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_28)). They disperse data across numerous CSPs situated in various sections. By doing so, it is possible to ensure improved fault tolerance, data durability, increased service availability, and vendor lock-in. Erasure coding is used in these situations to drastically minimize the quantity of data that needs to be saved in comparison to full replication ([Wu et al., 2013](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_11)), but it has a cost in latency (Mu et al., 2012). On the other hand, application (system) creators can put up with overhead in order to maintain a lot of data for less cost.

## Methodology

Information Collection in Cloud Storage is used to gather data on CSPs from Cloud Harmony, a website for gathering and tracking information of a third-party about cloud service offerings such as costs, features, and availability.

### Multi-cloud storage system

Even though multi-cloud storage offers the aforementioned advantages, the trade-off among data availability, retrieval costs, and storage costs is a significant challenge ([Elkordy et al., 2023](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_27)). It is a serious issue since high-availability CSPs place a significant financial burden on the customer for storage and retrieval. The answer to this problem is how to pick the best CSPs and erasure coding settings in order to maximize data availability while minimizing storage and retrieval costs.

[Figure 1](#ch20.xhtml#fig20_1) is an example of how users might save their data across many clouds. Statistics of User Demand, Collection of Cloud Storage Information, Retrieving Data, and Hosting are the four parts. Data demand statistics compile user needs, such as data size, necessary data availability, and frequency of data access. The framework contains two primary components are data retrieval and data hosting. Clouds in which the data should be set up by choosing data hosting. Data Retrieving selects the clouds from which a user’s data will be retrieved. For confirming high availability, two types of these components utilize erasure coding, which is frequently employed in storage systems ([Zhang et al., 2015](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_12)). Erasure coding could be utilized to divide the data item into equal-sized parts, and differences between the chunks could be encoded using data chunks. The primary benefit of erasure coding is the ability to reconstruct the input data from any data chunks (m) ([Weatherspoon & Kubiatowicz, 2002](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_13)). Data chunks from CSPs can be utilized to retrieve the original data in erasure coding.

Fig. 1\. Outline of Multi-cloud storage

*Data unavailability:* The availability of a service is the primary barrier to the growth of cloud computing ([Armbrust et al., 2010](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_14)). Another sign that users are most worried about is data accessibility. Despite stringent Service Level Agreements (SLAs) for their services, CSPs may experience unplanned service interruptions. These unforeseen occurrences include server outages, natural disasters, power outages, and other things.

*Data privacy leakage:* Users prefer to stay away from unreliable CSPs since data is held with a third party. Users’ data is exposed to CSP if they utilize just one cloud provider, which greatly increases the risk of data leakage.

*Vendor lock-in:* This is a big obstacle to the hypothesis of cloud computing ([Opara-Martins et al., 2016](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_15))and results from a lack of standards. User vulnerability to a price increase, availability decline, or even provider insolvency is known as the vendor lock-in issue in this cloud storage.

Cloud usage can be divided into the top three types of deployment models. One is public clouds similar to those offered by Google, Amazon, Microsoft, IBM, and others. A shared green virtual instance is possible to share as a resource by individuals and businesses in the public cloud with the help of SLA (Service Level Agreement). The succeeding model is private clouds, which are more secure and open source

### Erasure Coding

The complete document is separated into several blocks by erasure coding ([Dhinakaran et al., 2020](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_16); [Datta & Oggier, 2022](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_26)) , and while the input is distributed into blocks for security reasons, the output is still provided in the input’s original format. When storing a lot of data, erasure coding is helpful ( ([Lin & Tzeng, 2012](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_17)). Erasure is frequently used when storing big amounts of data on the cloud, where TPA is used to store all of the data. Data has been divided into simple to reassemble blocks using erasure coding ([Patil et al., 2012](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_18)). Triones, a systematic model, is suggested ([Su et al., 2015](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_20)). It formulates and optimizes placing data stored in a multi-cloud system under difficult constraints using non- linear programming. The objective function is built utilizing geometric space abstraction and the measuring of Euclidean distance, which assists in getting the ultimate ideal data placement topologies. In Triones, single- and multi-objectives are possible to successfully handle optimization progress.

### Proposed Method

The proposed study outlines the procedure for securing data via online erasure coding in a green cloud. Data encoding and decoding are being worked on in the online coding approach. The mechanism of proposed erasure coding is shown in [Figure 2](#ch19.xhtml#fig19_2). New users can complete the registration process in the first phase of this model’s user module, which contains personal information, email, and validation of mobile number with one-time password (OTP). After entering their credentials, users can access the dashboard to check the status of their cloud instances and applications. The user’s next move is to upload data that has been broken up into blocks, each of which has a different dynamic optimal key. The user can execute the following operations after uploading the document: append, remove, insert, and update the data that is already available in the cloud atmosphere, in which the consumer will be given complete protection for his workload. Since only the user can have the ability to add, update, or remove the available data occurring in the green cloud, only the user can do so.

![Fig. 2. Architectural diagram proposed system in multi-cloud storage environment](images/fig19_2_C.jpg)

[Fig. 2\. Architectural diagram proposed system in multi-cloud storage environment](#ch19.xhtml#R_fig19_2)

The dynamic key is uniquely created in the second phase. The key that has been generated and optimized using the muddy soil fish optimization approach is verified using third- party authentication (TPA). Every time an operation like a delete or append is made, it communicates that key to the administrator. Another distinct dynamic key will also be created and optimized at the same time. If the operation is being carried out with the aid of the key, it should be validated by the TPA and each block is capable of carrying out any one of the operations. The admin operator will compare the optimized keys that the TPA has validated with the created keys while the cloud admin module will keep an eye on the TPA. In between the user and the TPA, admin serves as a mediator. Administrator checks keep track of both the user as well as the TPA, when the optimized keys are validated by the TPA following the activities carried out by the user. The administrator keeps an eye on the entire cloud service procedure.

### Optimized Erasure Coding

[Figure 3](#ch19.xhtml#fig19_3) illustrates the inner and outer encoding processes. These procedures are well-optimized individually with the help of MSFOA. They are performed during the various phases of erasure coding. Outer encoding is the process of breaking up an input file into several data block pieces that are transparent to consumers and that will satisfy their needs. It is very challenging to determine how many fragments are present in a given file because all of them are fragments in the outer encoding.

![Fig. 3. Overall Coding Process](images/fig19_3_B.jpg)

[Fig. 3\. Overall Coding Process](#ch19.xhtml#R_fig19_3)

Inner encoding uses the compound message to generate numerous check blocks with a hash function to handle various encrypted fragment naming conventions. The attackers cannot Figure out the order of each fragment under these circumstances. It is necessary to perform decoding not only inner but also in the outer channel. After completing the inner type decoding, which depends on a secured dynamic key, the outer type decoding will merge all of the message blocks before reconstructing the original document. The procedure of inner and outer encoding is reversed during the decoding.

  
$$\\begin{matrix} & {Sr = Gm^{\\ast}\\text{Fr}} \\\\ & {Fr = \\left\\{ Fr\_{\\text{i}} \\mid 1 \\leq i \\leq k \\right\\}} \\\\ & {Sr = \\left\\{ Sr\\text{i}\_{\\text{i}} \\mid 1 \\leq i \\leq n \\right\\}} \\\\ \\end{matrix}$$  

where Gm is a generator matrix for online erasure coding *(n, k),* and Fr[i] and *Sr[i]* are the associated row of the vector fragment of *Fr* and *Sr,* respectively.

**Algorithm for optimized progress in erasure coding**

Input: Input data

 1: n, no. of Message Block data (M)

 2: Method of Outer Encoding — XOR function of every message block using an optimizer

 3: Inner Encoding progress using the same optimizer

A message check block has the group of all (XOR) message from data. The Random Message (M) Block Distribution is

  
$$\\sum\\limits\_{u = 1}^{n}(M = u) = 1$$  

U is a collection of every conceivable message block *(1 to* n) present in the input file.

 4: Inner Decoding progress - a dynamic secure file with private key.

 5: Progress of Outer Decoding - XOR of every message blocks decoded

Output: Retrieve Original/input File.

The above steps are developed effectively with all these steps. These are experimentally verified with the Triones approach ([Su et al., 2015](#ch19.xhtml#ref19_20)) to estimate their latency and time consumption throughout the progress.

## Conclusions and Future Work

If consumers store all of their data in a single cloud, some dangers may occur in the data security or privacy. Multi-cloud data hosting is emerging as a new development trend. One of the most crucial concerns is developed in multi-cloud systems to accomplish optimization in multi-objectives by striking a balance among diverse aspects. Therefore, the architecture for multi-cloud storage is provided first in this work. This work proposes a methodical strategy that uses MSFOA and erasure coding to plan and optimize the location of data storage in a multi-cloud system. The suggested method enables users to decide the most beneficial cloud for everyone and transfer more data to it. For better privacy data preservation, an updated sanitization and restoration model is presented that takes into account objective functions like HR, FR, DM, PR, and assaults like KPA, KCA, and CPA. The suggested MSFOA method was used to generate a key for sanitization and restoration in the greatest probable way. Furthermore, the end user who has been given permission successfully recovered the sensitive data. The suggested technique protects data from insider attacks on cloud storage. To speed up data transfer via multi-cloud storage, the suggested study used a slicing procedure depending on the cloud upload, parameters, and access latency. By keeping various data slices on multiple cloud storage, the investigation findings offer data transfer efficiency estimation. One needs to incorporate bandwidth effectiveness into the optimization parameters, especially for massive data, in our future work. The demand for high bandwidth for data transmission over several clouds of storage grows as file sizes get bigger. The cloud instance type optimization will also be taken into account when choosing between single and many providers.

# A Framework for Real-Time Prediction of Inappropriate Content

N. Suraj,^([^(17)](#fn17))

E-mail: [asurajn6501@gmail.com](mailto:asurajn6501@gmail.com); [varunrishwandh2001@gmail.com](mailto:varunrishwandh2001@gmail.com); [thuhinkhanna01@gmail.com](mailto:thuhinkhanna01@gmail.com); [dpriya.vijay@rajalakshmi.edu.in](mailto:dpriya.vijay@rajalakshmi.edu.in)

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-20](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-20)

## Abstract

The sudden growth and scale of the internet make it impossible to have a central authority to control the content being shared. Internet platforms have community guidelines for policing the content uploaded to their site. However, this is restricted to their respective platforms, and the internet is much broader. While other forms of media like television have a clearly defined system for censorship, there is a vacuum in the tech world in protecting users from being exposed to sensitive content. The work proposes to build a deep learning model that classifies the contents of a webpage as Safe or Not safe for work (NSFW) using techniques such as image classification and sentiment analysis. NSFW content is anything deemed inappropriate in a public setting, including age-restricted content. The end product would be a cross-browser web extension that can detect and classify content as safe or NSFW in real time and redact the said content from being displayed in the client’s browser. A web extension would be a universal and easy-to-use solution for the user to protect themselves from sensitive content on the internet. Thus, the work intends to solve the problem of censorship of sensitive content on the internet.

Keywords: Deep Learning, Natural Language Processing, Web Scraping, Content Filtering, Image Classification

## Introduction

The amount of data present on the internet is estimated to be around 64 Zettabytes where 1 Zettabyte is equivalent to a trillion Gigabytes. Hugely popular websites such as Facebook, and Twitter have their community guidelines and their policies on what type of content is appropriate. But the same cannot be said for all the other websites, which would have no filter on the content that a user could post on that website. Content that the viewer might not wish to consume or see in a public, formal, or controlled environment is termed to be NSFW or Not Safe For Work. It is incredibly difficult to avoid sensitive content due to the various ads, pop-ups, etc. Even during a simple internet search, people find it hard to trust the websites after the first page of search results. Children these days are exposed to the internet at a very young age. Even though child-safety mechanisms are available, it is still effortless for them to access a website containing content they shouldn’t be exposed to.

The main objective of this work is to redact text and images present on the website the user is currently viewing, that are deemed to be inappropriate or sensitive. This objective is achieved through a series of processes including scraping data and images, pre-processing the data acquired, and applying classification models to the data to classify them as safe or unsafe for the user.

## Related Works

### Data Collection and Web Scraping

Moaiad Ahmad Khder ([Khder, 2021](#ch20.xhtml#ref20_1)) has described the acquisition of data as the first phase in any data science study and development and has drawn comparisons between APIs and web scraping while arguing that APIs cannot be depended on to acquire data at all times, unlike web scraping. He has laid out three approaches to web scraping using Python namely Beautiful Soup, Regular Expressions, and LXML, and has compared them in terms of criteria such as performance and ease of use. Amani Alswailem *et.al \[* *\]* have outlined the use of real-time data scraping to analyze the content of web pages. They have proposed ways to crawl the internet and scrape data from web pages. He has also used techniques like OXPath and computer vision analyzers to extract data from any kind of web page.

### Text Classification and Hate Speech Detection

Text classification or categorization is the process of assigning pre-determined labels to sentences or excerpts of text data. A wide range of techniques has been developed over the years to classify text. Text classification begins with encoding words as numerical vectors and then classifying them in either supervised or unsupervised learning.

### Supervised Text Classification

#### Bag of Words

A Bag of Words or BoW is another technique of encoding text as a numerical vector in Natural Language Processing. The BoW starts with a large vocabulary of words compiled for the task and each word in the sentence is encoded as a count of each word in the vocabulary. This means that for each word in a sentence, a vector of the size of the entire vocabulary is generated.

The Bag of Words technique is limited by the size of the vocabulary for the task at hand. As the vocabulary size increases, the length of each word vector increases, and the space complexity of encoding text becomes too huge to handle.

### Tf-Idf

Term Frequency - Inverse Document Frequency or TF-IDF is a statistical way of representing text as numerical vectors. TF-IDF uses a logarithmic score based on the frequency of the words in the documents to represent each word or token. Using TF-IDF we can identify the most important words in the document, the higher the score associated with the word, the more important it is. TF-IDF has been used to train several supervised NLP models for text classification and sentiment analysis.

### Attention-Based Techniques for Text Classification

The Attention mechanism was introduced in 2017 by researchers at Google and led to the development of the Transformer architecture which has spun into a wide range of models which are state-of-the-art in text generation and classification. Several pre-trained attention-based models are being used every day in several NLP tasks and applications.

### BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers)

**BERT** is an unsupervised technique used to pre-train language representations. BERT was also developed by Google and is based on the Transformer architecture. Unlike its predecessors, BERT can capture the context of the text excerpt by looking at words both to the left and right of a given word in a sentence.

BERT is preferred for so many state-of-the-art models because of its provision for fine-tuning specific datasets for the task being focused on. BERT large has been trained with over 345 million parameters and with a vocabulary of 3.3 billion words taken from sources on the internet, books, and Wikipedia articles.

### GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer)

GPT developed by OpenAl is another state- of-the-art unsupervised NLP model based on the Transformers architecture used in various functions such as language generation, text classification, question answering, and translation. GPT differs from BERT in the way that BERT is a bidirectional model and GPT is unidirectional which means that it can only work in the conventional left-to-right direction. Because of this GPT is the preferred model for language generation tasks, unlike BERT which is used in instances where the model needs to understand the context of the text data in hand.

Depending on the size of the model GPT- 3 implementations can have from 125 million to 170 billion parameters trained on a huge training set of data collected from books, web pages from the internet, Wikipedia articles, and much more.

### Hate Speech Detection

[Mohaouchane et al., (2019](#ch20.xhtml#ref20_3)) have proposed a system to detect Arabic hate speech in social media posts with the intent to regulate the type of content that is being posted on these forums. His work has used classification deep learning methods such as LSTM and Bi-LSTM to classify text. The work analyzed over 15000 comments from YouTube’s comment sections.

Nobata et al., (2019)have proposed a way to identify the linguistic features such as the size of each word, punctuations, and so on to detect hate speech using techniques such as word2vec and comment2vec. The work analyzed over 25000 comments from Yahoo Finance comment sections.

[Pamungkas et al., (2022](#ch20.xhtml#ref20_5))have created a benchmark corpus called SWAD, which is made up of English Tweets and includes manual word- level annotations of abusive profanity. They have identified the BERT model to provide the highest

accuracy while automatically classifying words as abusive and not-abusive.

### Image Classification

Image classification refers to the categorization of images under various labels or the probability of the image being part of the label. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN, or ConvNet) is a specific type of multi-layer neural network created to identify visual patterns in pixel images. CNN typically contains three layers namely, the Convolutional Layer where the kernel performs the convolution operation on the matrix, the Pooling Layer which reduces the amount of computing power required for processing the data by reducing the dimensionality and the Fully Connected Layer where the actual learning takes place and each input is coupled to every neuron.

### VGGNet - 16

There are 16 layers in the VGGNet-16 architecture, comprising 13 convolutional layers and 3 fully linked layers. Using rectified linear unit (ReLU) activation functions, the convolutional layers employ 3 x 3 filters with a stride of 1. The 2 x 2 filters with a 2 stride are used in the pooling layers.

The input image is processed and basic features like edges and corners are extracted using the network’s first two layers. The following layers progressively raise the level of abstraction and pick up increasingly intricate details.

### ResNet

ResNet is a deep neural network architecture that makes use of residual connections to support the training of extremely deep neural networks. Several convolutional layers are spread throughout several residual blocks, followed by batch normalization and activation functions. The vanishing gradients issue that can arise in very deep networks is lessened by the residual connection in each block, which allows the input to “skip” some of the layers and be fed directly to the output.

Each residual block in ResNet is made up of two or three convolutional layers, batch normalization, and a ReLU activation function after each. The input of the block is then added to the output of the final convolutional layer, and the sum is then run through another activation function.

#### NSFW Images Classification

[Kelly et al., (2018](#ch20.xhtml#ref20_6))have experimented with various techniques involved in skin detection in images using ML and neural networks. They have proposed a system in which the skin content would be analyzed by color histograms and feature extraction.

[Deselaers et al., (2018](#ch20.xhtml#ref20_7)) have proposed a system using the Bag of Visual Words (BOVW) models in identifying sensitive images. They assert that the development of a flexible content filter surpasses cutting-edge algorithms in such jobs and can be easily adapted to the user’s demands.

[Zhelonkin & Karpov (2019](#ch20.xhtml#ref20_8))have presented a scheme on how to prepare highly accurate and fast CNN for detecting NSFW images. The novel approach in this work is identifying NSFW pictures with nudity not only in images with real humans but also in other drawn pictures including cartoons containing obscene content.

**Proposed Work**

The proposed work aims to detect and redact NSFW content on the web pages that a user on the internet might visit. The work takes advantage of image and text classification models and architectures to perform such a task. The work consists of numerous processes divided mainly into three modules, which separate the work into three distinct computing modules as depicted in [Fig. 1](#ch20.xhtml#fig20_1)

![Fig. 1. System architecture diagram representing the proposed system.](images/fig20_1_B.jpg)

[Fig. 1. System architecture diagram representing the proposed system.](#ch20.xhtml#R_fig20_1)

The data collection process for the work includes the identification of labels for the training process and the collection of data that would adequately represent the training labels. By building a dataset for this work the model is trained to be exposed to the kind of data that would be encountered in the running of the application.

The data collection process is followed by pre- processing the text and image data. Pre-processing is necessary to make the scraped data suitable for training and validation as web data might not be in the right format to be used directly without cleaning. Pre-processing data from internet sources often involves dealing with internet-specific terms, HTML tags, CSS data, etc. While there exist many libraries and packages for web scraping, regular expressions provide the necessary tools and speed to scrape data by simply matching patterns of text that need to be removed.

There can be any number of solutions for text and image classification including state-of-the-art pre-trained models which can produce the best results. In the task of making real-time predictions speed is a much more important characteristic of the model than space or time complexity. Models need to be trained to achieve a trade-off between these characteristics. The models built on the labeled dataset need to be validated against real user data and conversational data from Internet sources. In such cases, it is important to understand the context of the text excerpt when performing sentiment analysis and this warrants the need for deep- learning text classification models. Architectures like Bi-LSTM and **BERT** are examples of models that can gainfully understand the context of the textual data and assign labels to it.

The final module of the proposed work is the application with which the user or client device interacts. The scraping part of the module is designed to function on the client side entirely in the device of the user in the form of a browser extension. This design choice was made to preserve the user’s content’s privacy. The browser extension also carries out the task of redacting the NSFW content on the web page after their detection/classification. The scraped data is sent to the cloud instance hosting the backend server which performs the actual classification task. The requirement of the task to provide real-time accurate prediction often relies on hardware that can be efficient and fast, since the client’s devices may be engaged in any number of processes at that time, a cloud instance is best suited for the classification task.

## Conclusion

The proposed work provides a suitable framework to redact NSFW content from the user’s screen through a browser extension using various deep learning algorithms. There is a tonne of fascinating stuff on the internet, some of which may or may not be suitable for consumption. Limiting young users to a small number of websites may stifle their desire to learn and explore new things. This work can be used as a real-time child safety system to prevent children from accessing inappropriate content online. The system is designed to be elegant and user-friendly. The proposed system also provides a way of implementing text and image classification algorithms in making real- time predictions on actual user-generated data. The proposed system once implemented and deployed will be able to effectively reduce the number of encounters with NSFW content on the internet for any user.

# Statistical and Algorithmic Color Normalization and Stain Separation Methods: A Brief Study

Lourdu Rayappan^([^(18)](#fn18))

E-mail: [abyssrayappan@gmail.com](mailto:abyssrayappan@gmail.com), [dr.r.parameswari16@gmail.com](mailto:dr.r.parameswari16@gmail.com)

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-21](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-21)

## Abstract

Staining and color standardization are a significant steps in the computer-aided analysis of digital pathological images. Blood cells contain a wide range of phenotypic details, which is essential for predicting changes in the pathological characteristics of blood tissues. Lately, advancements in deep learning techniques have contributed to the imaging, assessment, and interpretation of pathological details supported by computational methods, but this process presents several challenges. The complexity of Color and stain variations calculation due to the application of different scanners with various features regarding the source of light, objective lens, camera resolution utilized to capture the image, the application of other color dyeing techniques, varying chemical agents, and various magnification levels reduce predictive accuracy of results. This paper presents a brief study associated with multiple color normalization techniques used in pathological image analysis.

Keywords: Color Normalization, Pathology Stain Separation, color disparity, pre-processing, deep learning

## Introduction

Histopathology is the study of the characteristics of invasive or minimally invasive abnormal cells under a microscope. Pathologists examine the distribution, regularity of shape, and geometrical features of tissue structure to determine whether the image is benign or cancerous. A blood smear is stained to separate the nucleus, cytoplasm, and connective tissue of the cellular components to identify benign or malignant tissues ([Rashmi et al., 2021](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_1)). Next, malignancy is discovered by examining changes in morphological features such as shape, size, and color of the region of interest (ROI). However, manual analysis is subjective, inconsistent, tedious, time-consuming, and prone to human error ([Rashmi et al., 2021](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_1)).

Also, due to human error and different standards of equipment used, the interpretation of results in the lab may be inconsistent. Therefore, quantitative analysis of pathological images from an objective diagnostic point of view ([Gurcan et al., 2009](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_2))is also essential to free pathologists from the task of concentrating on difficult-to-diagnose cases. Color changes are essential in pathology. Images of tissues are translucent, and the colors they reveal are due to the transmission of light with scattering. Uneven lighting, unbalanced camera sensitivity, or artifacts can upset the color channels and display unreasonable colors. One can tell the difference by staining the blood smear on the same day or a different day ([Clarke & Treanor, 2016](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_3)). Techniques like GEM ENFPs used to detect a change in color space, noise, and distribution ([Hwang et al., 2006](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_4); [Bejnordi et al., 2014](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_5)). Various staining techniques are used in digital pathology to emphasize the structure of cells and tissues. Hematoxylin and e’osin (H & E) are standard stains for histological examination of blood tissue, where cells at the initial stage usually have a blue cytoplasm, turn gradually from blue to purple, then to pink as cells mature ([Cross, 1998](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_6)).

Our core issue is worth repeating here. The performance of image analysis techniques depends on the quality of the stained tissue and the influence of image characteristics, which are determined by many factors, on the study results. Many pre-processing methods apply the colors of one image to another ([Reinhard et al., 2001](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_7)), convolutional neural networks for color and stain normalization and augmentation, analysis or measurement of domain shifts, and variability analysis( ([Zheng et al., 2021](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_8); [Salvi et al., 2020](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_9); [Anghel et al., 2019](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_10); [Zanjani et al., 2018](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_11); [Stacke et al., 2021](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_12); [Grabel et al., 2021](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_13); [Vasiljevic et al., 2021](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_14); [Tellez et al., 2018](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_15); [Tellez et al., 2019](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_16)) . This article explores the proposed stain and color normalization, enhancement methods, and various approaches to explain the results.

## Various Schemes of Pre-Processing Pathological Images.

### Stain Separation

Digital pathological images captured for human interpretation and automated analysis were originally stained with various chemicals to contrast the morphological features of tissues visually. Unfortunately, the images need to be standardized for automated analysis. The approach to capturing the biological structure of tissue by dye separation is to examine the density map of each dye and understand the relationship between the RGB channels and the dye density of each pixel. ([Tadrous (2010)](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_17) proposed a de-colorization algorithm that allows the selection of RGB single maximum contrast color channel, inversion of each pixel intensity value is subtracted from the top image value and repeated for all channels increase. Then transfer the contrast from the red channel vector to the other two channels. In H & E images, red is the high-contrast channel, and bleaching red channels other than the predominant red-blue channel reduces Hematoxylin staining. At the same time, the dark-stained brown-only algorithm yields brighter results ([McCann et al., 2014](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_18)).From the optical density matrix, the contrast of the H & E channels is adjusted to produce a separate vector for H and E to obtain a single maximum for a single vector decomposition. Another method- independent component analysis ([Trahearn et al., 2015](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_19)) shows that the computational complexity of the monitored stain separation method is significant and the failure to preserve characteristics of the source image.

### Color Normalization

Color shifts in pathological images make it difficult to obtain reliable results. Differences in the color of pathological images are due to differences in raw materials, scanners, and laboratory procedures. By reducing color changes, one can reduce complexity and improve predictions. Color normalization can be generalized to two statistical and algorithmic approaches. The statistical method ( [Reinhard et al., 2001](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_7)) transfers the color features of the reference image to the input image based on the mean and standard deviation to improve the image’s appearance. [Salvi et al., (2020](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_9))proposed a new fully automated approach to color separation and normalization by enhancing the contrast between tissue and background by preserving the color of the local structure. [Bautista et al., (2014](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_20))performed global color standardization by converting non-linear RGB channels to linear channels, performing linear RGB color correction, and then converting to images. Instead of standardizing the partial causes of color changes [Li & Plataniotis (2015)](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_21), use intensity comparison algorithms and spectral normalization modules to handle imaging and staining changes. Statistical approach Global color normalization is a non- linear process that fails to preserve source information, and the transformation is applied globally. The pixel-to-pixel mapping model relies only on a single reference image and does not

perform the change accurately and smoothly. Deep learning algorithms quickly solve conversion problems with a complex network structure that can learn color properties from the entire dataset and convert values at the pixel level. Most neural structured color normalization focused on high- performance models rather than disproportionate data. Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) normalize the source image to the target image and the set normalized image as the training ground truth [Anghel et al., (2019](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_10)). Have a generalized CNN approach to standardize colors without using template images trained in histopathology and cytopathology datasets ([Kang et al., 2021](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_22)).

## Domain and Color Augmentation

Data augmentation techniques include geometry and color conversion, random erasing, adversarial training, style transfer, and more. Affine transformations are applied to manipulate data by mirroring, rotating, cropping, enlarging, reducing, or creating duplicates of distorted images. Color

augmentation is performed by separating the RGB color channels and manipulating them with matrix operations to increase or decrease the brightness, reduce the image’s brightness, or change the illumination using intensity values. [Vasiljevic et al., (2021](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_14)) proposed a pixel space and feature space approach to color augmentation to change the features of the input image. [Tellez et al., (2019](#ch21.xhtml#ref21_16))showed that color normalization combined with a color enhancement approach to address color inhomogeneity improves generalization. The robust data augmentation framework such as GAN or Cycle-GAN allows unsupervised augmentation of images from small datasets for training and style transfer.

## Conclusion

This study presented a few staining and color normalization and augmentation practices in the context of histopathological imaging. We have identified computerized analysis of pathological images with various supervised and unsupervised methods in global and subspace for color and stain separation, normalization, and enhancement and have shown different results. The statistical approach does not preserve the source image information. Stain findings are not good with large numbers of dark and bright pixels. Source and destination domains expect similar statistics, coloring is applied globally, and in most circumstances, color is preserved. The algorithmic approach holds the functionality of the source and target domains, and the unsupervised method reduces annotation time, produces more types of staining variability, and is more sophisticated. In contrast, the algorithmic approach computational complexity and memory consumption of deep learning networks are high, and the quality and quantity of balanced training datasets affect the interpretability of the model. A fully automated algorithmic approach may not be agile or provide the flexibility to address different staining techniques and focus on the area of interest.

A summary of the statistical and algorithmic techniques studied is given in [Table 1](#ch21.xhtml#tab21_1). Each technique studied used different image datasets containing several different types of dyes, but most H & Es focused on a particular disease. Most studies used a single dye instead of a different dye in the experiment, and in most scenarios, both the statistical and algorithmic approaches used curated datasets in the research. This multidimensional variability makes it challenging to compare techniques with their results. Using pre-processing methods, stain separation, and subsequent color and stain normalization, the color variability of the synthesized dataset shows significantly improved outcomes. Future work will focus on color and domain augmentation approaches.

# Classification of Malware Infected API Call Sequences With Ensemble Learning

Bhavith Chowdary,^([^(19)](#fn19))

E-mail: [19113071@student.hindustanuniv.ac.in](mailto:19113071@student.hindustanuniv.ac.in), [19113084@student.hindustanuniv.ac.in](mailto:19113084@student.hindustanuniv.ac.in), [lindaj@hindustanuniv.ac.in](mailto:lindaj@hindustanuniv.ac.in)

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-22](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-22)

## Abstract

The privacy and security of users’ information is seriously threatened by the steady rise in malware. Consequently, efficient, and effective techniques are required for classifying malicious malware. This research proposes a technique for classifying malware using ensemble learning. As a result, malware classification is important and necessary to stop malware attacks. API call patterns are extremely useful sources of knowledge for identifying malware behavior. API call sequences are used as classifier inputs in the suggested malware classification algorithms presented in this study. Call sequences for APIs are effective at capturing characteristics for malware categorization. The approach suggested in this study for the malware classification of the API Calls uses ensemble learning based on Maximum voting ensemble classifier. Algorithms used in the paper are Decision tree K-Nearest Neighbor and Random Forest Classification methods. These algorithms act as base learners. The model proposed performs malware variant classification model based on the majority voting method. Finally, the results were compared to find the model with high accuracy.

Keywords: Malware, Ensemble Learning, Machine Learning, API Calls

## Introduction

In accordance with the Symantec Threat Report ([Symantec, 2016](#ch22.xhtml#ref22_1)), malware attacks significantly increased in 2016 by 286% and by 600% in 2017. A rise in malware attacks of roughly 217.5% was noted in 2018, according to SonicWall (2019 )Cyber Threat Report. In the first half of 2020, 1.8 million additional dangerous programs were identified by experts at the AV-TEST Inst. (2020). According to a McAfee report, the number of malware attacks in 2015 exceeded nine million per year, particularly against Google’s Android operating system. A dangerous program called malware is created with the express purpose of stealing data or undermining infrastructures and systems. They are highly developed programs that may greatly dodge and delay malware detection technologies. Similar methodologies are predicated based on the assumption that malware may make great use of system calls, calling them in a random order compared to clean malware([Zhang et al., 2015](#ch22.xhtml#ref22_4)). Furthermore, computer virus snippets sometimes use certain API calls far more frequently than is typical. On the other hand, the total number of APIs invoked is rather small compared to these API calls. Additionally, hackers remove, swap out, and introduce false API calls that have no bearing on the malicious code’s original function and activity in order to confuse malware detectors.

It is essential to create a malware detection method that identifies malware with increased accuracy based on API call sequences. The issue with current malware detection techniques is that they rely heavily on signature-based data. Signature-based identification is based on the recognition of distinct fingerprints for each malware. This method is incapable of detecting novel malware variants. As a result, machine learning has lately been suggested as a solution to this problem.

Machine learning techniques have been demonstrated to be capable of recognizing new malware strains and typically focus on discovering and mining relationships in observed data. As a result, several API call-based techniques based on sequence have been suggested in the paper for identifying and categorizing malware. These methods fundamentally work by evaluating similarities between the patterns that have been gathered that signify malicious actions and the sequence of API calls that characterizes the evaluated applications. When it comes to improving classification performance, using a collection of classifiers performs better than using a single classifier. A single accurate classifier is created using the ensemble learning technique, which integrates multiple algorithms rather than just one. The drawbacks of single-model-based approaches can be addressed by developing an ensemble learning approach. In this research, we employ the majority voting mechanism, to get better results than the previous methods. We defined API calls as the techniques through which computer applications. Each species of malware may have distinct API call patterns; hence, system call sequences may be classified. Three categorization models are investigated using the suggested approaches, which include Decision Tree, K-Nearest Neighbor, and Random Forest Classification.

Thus, the organization of the research is carried out. Section 2 presents an overview of some literature we have referred in this work. The proposed system and modules are illustrated and discussed in Section 3. In Section 4, we provide the experimental results and testing of the proposed system. Finally, paper is concluded and draws our limitations, and discusses some possible future works in Section V.

## Proposed Model

### Overview

Based on machine learning techniques, the proposed malware categorization methodology is provided in this section. This system offers an ensemble learning architecture for malware classification.

Algorithm :

In Step 1, we execute the malware samples in a sandbox, gather the results of the dynamic analysis, and then extract the API call sequences in accordance with those results.

In Step 2, feature extraction is performed on the extracted API call sequences.

In Step 3, we train a dataset and apply three different classification models to it.

In step 4, A technique of ensemble learning called majority voting classifier is applied to obtain the model with high accuracy in detecting malware.

In step 5, the performance of each algorithm is evaluated using various measurement metrics.

### API Call

Application programming interfaces (APIs) allows one software to communicate with another. API calls are the means via which they communicate. An API call, also known as an API request, is a message delivered to a server that requests that an API offer a service or information. In fact, the program’s function, whether benign or malicious, is mostly accomplished through organized API calls. Furthermore, the majority of malware is derived from innocuous software that has been infected by malware such as viruses.

## Methodology

### Dataset

First, using the free source software cuckoo sandbox (Cuckoo [Sandbox, 2019](#ch22.xhtml#ref22_19)), which includes numerous malwares including roughly 23,150, the malware-based API call sequences dataset is collected. malware API call sequences categories include Adware, Backdoors, Downloaders, Droppers, Spyware, Trojans, Viruses, Worms, and others that are divided into different families. Send the executable samples to a sandbox for automated investigation of suspect files, such as Cuckoo Sandbox. A report is produced in the sandbox in a supervised virtual setting.

The program’s start and end times are then extracted, together with the API call sequences and calling time.

### Preprocess

The pre-processing of the dataset comes next. In this instance, the dataset underwent preprocessing and was split into training and testing datasets to facilitate evaluation. By eliminating permissions that aren’t necessary for categorization, these techniques reduce dataset sizes.

### Feature Selection Method

In the third step, the malware traits are extracted. Feature extraction methods can help to improve classification accuracy by utilizing key characteristics that define the dataset’s distinctive properties Machine learning algorithms may have repeated or irrelevant properties, leading to a variety of issues. It benefits the model by changing the number of features and bringing them within a range. It is critical to follow this procedure if we are using algorithms that are sensitive to the size of the values, We can scale the characteristics using standardization, and normalization scaling. To detect, a suitable feature selection strategy must be used. We adopted min-max scaling and a

label encoder for the extraction of features from the dataset.

In min-max, the numbers of a feature range are re-scaled from -1 to 1. It is the ratio of subtracting each observation and the mean from the highest and lowest value of that feature.

\[X - mean(X)\]/\[max(X) - min(X)\] (1) Label encoding is the process of turning labels into a numeric shape that is machine-readable. Machine learning systems can then better determine how those identifiers should be used. It is an essential pre-processing stage for the organized dataset in supervised learning.

### Classifier

Ensemble learning methodology is used throughout the training phase. We employ three separate classifiers: decision trees, k-nearest neighbor, and random forest classifier. All three are part of supervised machine learning, which involves training and testing each classifier individually.

### Ensemble Learning Model

Ensemble learning integrates predictions from various models to increase predictive performance. Machine learning ensemble techniques integrate information from multiple learning models to make more accurate and better choices. The main causes of mistakes in learning models are noise, variance, and prejudice. Machine learning ensemble techniques ([Natani & Vidyarthi, 2014](#ch22.xhtml#ref22_20)) help to reduce these error-causing variables, guaranteeing the precision and reliability of the machine learning (ML) algorithm.

### Majority Voting Classifier

An ensemble of several machine learning models is used to train an Ensembled voting classifier, which then predicts an outcome (a class) based on the likelihood that the output would most likely belong to the chosen class. It simply combines the classification results from each classification that are input into the voting-based classifier and forecasts the outcome based on the majority of the votes. We use a single model that trains numerous specialized models and predicts output based on the sum of their votes for each out. The training

phase employs an ensemble learning technique. We use three distinct classifiers, namely decision trees, k-nearest neighbor, and random forest all of which pertain to the supervised machine learning method and are trained and then evaluated. On top of ensemble learning, we apply a majority voting classifier.

## Conclusion

This study investigated the ensemble technique for malware detection in the context of supervised learning classification.

In comparison to other feature selection strategies, we adopted five different features. Good accuracy was obtained by performing classification by adopting various algorithms. The outcome also demonstrated the great accuracy of the K-Nearest Neighbour classifier. This demonstrates how this kind of classifier may deliver the optimal outcome with a high degree of accuracy. There are still some issues that need to be resolved even if our suggested ensemble-based learning architecture is efficient at identifying and categorizing the various malware variants and families.

The suggested machine learning-based ensemble learning performs poorly when categorizing unknown malware and when identifying Linux APIs that have been compromised by malware. In our upcoming work, we intend to use this in real time, while working with datasets that contain different kinds of data.
