# Real-Time Over-The-Air-Programming (OTAP) for Wireless Sensor Network: Implementation and Analysis Using SENSEnuts IoT Platform

Chakravarthi Harshitha, Tallavalasa Venkatesh, and Jayavignesh Thyagarajan

School of Electronics Engineering, Vellore Institute of Technology Chennai, India

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-32](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-32)

## Abstract

Numerous smart remote monitoring applications pertaining to the environment (specific to panchaboothas namely monitoring air {quality, gas concentration, pollution, etc}, fire, water, land, sky), habitat, military, surveillance, intrusion/border detection, health, etc.) focus on Internet of Things (IoT) based Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) solutions. The IoT sensor nodes are constrained in terms of resources namely computing, storage and battery and are programmed to perform tasks such as sensing, processing and wirelessly transmitting the monitored event as packets over low data rate networks and switch to sleep state when inactive to preserve battery power. In such remote monitoring locations that are restricted or limited in physical access, these constrained IoT devices are deployed in random or installed in regular manner. To support large-scale deployment of monitoring for such applications, it becomes highly essential to remotely control these IoT sensor nodes. OTAP provides remote connectivity to remotely monitor the devices and reprogram the devices when required. This enables to remotely flash the sensor nodes simultaneously and also displays the real-time gathered sensor data results for different applications. In this paper, we have implemented & tested OTAP using SENSEnuts Embedded IoT platform to remotely program the IEEE 802.15.4 compliant sensor mote and analyzed for different use cases. Also, challenges involved of flashing the firmware (compiled binary) over the air via the PAN coordinator are highlighted.

Keywords: SENSEnuts, Protocol, IoT node, OTAP, WSN

## Introduction

Over The Air Programming (OTAP) has been widely adopted in mobile smartphone handsets to transmit firmware updates through wireless technology(WiFi/4Getc),In a pandemic-driven world, OTA Phasa huge impact and importance in IoT based WSN that demands more of remote monitoring and control. IoT based WSN consists of several sensor nodes, each node comprising of sensor(s) interfaced with a micro-controller and radio transceiver capture and wirelessly transmit information about the region of interest and perform actuation or control action appropriately. OTAP enables to dynamic flash of the program code over the air on the remotely deployed Internet.

of Things (IoT) networks. This gives the flexibility to enable re-programming over the air, to add new features to the existing code, fix the bugs or resolve the security vulnerabilities.

This work focuses on the remote monitoring of greenhouses. A greenhouse is a closed structure that provides optimal conditions for plant growth by controlling the indoor and outdoor environments. The walls of the greenhouse are made with transparent materials such as glass or plastic. To achieve optimal plant growth, several key parameters must be considered, including soil moisture, humidity, atmospheric and soil temperature, sunlight availability, and the concentration of carbon dioxide in the air. This work specifically focuses on two parameters: temperature and humidity, which affect plant growth. Using the SENSEnuts IoT platform, we test sensor nodes at different locations inside the greenhouse under varying conditions. We also propose over-the-air programming in greenhouse monitoring to remotely reprogram the SENSEnuts nodes as needed. The paper is structured as follows: WSN architecture, Literature Survey, Proposed System, Methodology, Results obtained under various test conditions, and Conclusion.

## Literature Survey

In previous works ([Sangeeth et al., 2016](#ch32.xhtml#ref32_1); [Ramesh et al., 2013](#ch32.xhtml#ref32_7)), the OTAP approach has been implemented in a remote-triggered laboratory, enabling real-time video streaming of results without requiring physical connections between the nodes and the system. According to an evaluation, SO% of students rated the performance as excellent, and 41% rated it as very good. The next phase of development involves integrating compression algorithms into the OTAP method.

According to [Lata et al., (2020](#ch32.xhtml#ref32_2)), SENSEnuts wireless sensor nodes were utilized in conjunction with a wireless sensor network to monitor the temperature and humidity within a miniature greenhouse laboratory model. The system was subjected to various testing scenarios and was found to have low power consumption, low cost, and a user-friendly approach for real-time monitoring of climatic conditions within a greenhouse.

In a comprehensive overview of OTAP, including discussions of the latest OAP protocols utilized in WSN applications and the test-bed implementations ( ([Qandour et al., 2012](#ch32.xhtml#ref32_6); [Ramesh et al., 2013](#ch32.xhtml#ref32_7); [Steyn & Hancke, 2011](#ch32.xhtml#ref32_8); [Hellbruck et al., 2011](#ch32.xhtml#ref32_9); [Doddavenkatappa et al., 2011](#ch32.xhtml#ref32_10)), presented in these works (Q[uadri et al., 2014](#ch32.xhtml#ref32_3)). Over-the-air programming is a crucial process for resolving bugs, updating codes, and managing changes in application requirements.

The project ([Frisch et al., 2017](#ch32.xhtml#ref32_4)) aims to create a reliable and robust system for ESP8266 microcontrollers by developing and releasing encrypted firmware updates. Additionally, efforts are underway to expand and improve the functionality and security of the system, with the latest developments focusing on enhancing security features.

An article ([Kilaru et al., 2022](#ch32.xhtml#ref32_5))discusses the utilization of wireless sensor networks (WSN) and weather forecasting to automate agriculture. It explains how the Internet of Things (IoT) and cloud integration can automate irrigation and enhance security in farming. Moreover, the system can be adapted to create a sensor-cloud-based environment control system to cultivate vegetables and flowers in greenhouse farming during the off-season. The authors of the paper suggest that their system can be a valuable tool for improving the efficiency and productivity of farming.

## IoT Based WSN Architecture

WSN involve deploying a large number of sensor nodes throughout a specific area, which can range from hundreds to thousands of nodes. WSN involves deploying a large number of sensor nodes throughout a specific area, which can range from hundreds to thousands of nodes. The sensor node typically comprises units such as sensor(s), processing unit, and communication unit as shown in [Fig. 1](#ch32.xhtml#fig32_1). The gateway node (sink) acts as PAN coordinator to coordinate and collect data from the sensor nodes. The WSN employs the Zigbee protocol compliant with IEEE 802.15.4 specifications

## Proposed System and Methodology

The proposed WSN system comprises several SENSEnuts IoT nodes developed by Eigen Technologies and deployed in the region of interest. Each SENSEnuts node is modular hardware platform stacked with Temperature and Light sensors and interfaced with JN5168 32 bit IEEE 802.15.4 compliant radio microcontroller that operates in the 2.4 GHz ISM frequency band. The sensor(s) in each node are tasked to transmit the data as packets under few test conditions such as single-hop (direct transmission) and multi-hop (via intermediate relay nodes to reach gateway) as shown in [Fig. 2](#ch32.xhtml#fig32_2). The sensor nodes can also be re-flashed (reprogrammed) to change the data collection frequency etc using OTAP.

![Fig. 2. Test Deployment scenario](images/fig32_2_C.jpg)

[Fig. 2. Test Deployment scenario](#ch32.xhtml#R_fig32_1)

The TL (Temperature, Light) interfaced sensor node is deployed to monitor a particular zonewise area. Sensor nodes have been strategically placed at varying distances, and in order to test the OTAP for SENSEnuts motes. The gateway node is flashed and programmed with the PAN coordinator code to collect data from the deployed sensor nodes at specified time intervals. The gateway module is utilized for programming all sensor nodes, as well as interfacing with the PC and network. The TL sensor can collect data from the TMP102 temperature sensor, which has a range sensitivity of —250 °C to 800 °C and a resolution of 12 bits.

The SENSEnuts gateway node, depicted in [Fig. 3](#ch32.xhtml#fig32_3) of the Greenhouse Monitoring System that utilizes Over The Air Programming (OTAP), comprises a radio IEEE 802.15.4 module and a USB gateway module. The node is battery-powered and equipped with two 1.5V AA batteries, housed within the protective plastic case to shield it from environmental conditions.

![Fig. 3. Gateway module and TL stacked radio module](images/fig32_3_C.jpg)

[Fig. 3. Gateway module and TL stacked radio module](#ch32.xhtml#R_fig32_3)

The compiled binary i.e the new program code (firmware) to be flashed onto the sensor devices is transmitted as several packets of fixed size of 64 bytes wirelessly over the air by the PAN coordinator (gateway node) until the complete binary file is received (i.e. all packets are successfully transferred and received by the sensor node error free i.e. individual packets are acknowledged and checksum validated). As the Over the Air (OTA) Layer is enabled in each sensor node (i.e coordinator devices), where the node is tasked to check if the flash memory is free, flush the memory, and once the compiled program code (binary file) is received completely it is stored in flash memory and command is sent to reboot with the new firmware (i.e program code). The methodology is two-step process:

*   **Step 1**: The compiled new program binary file (OTA code) is split as packets of 64 bytes each and transmitted via wire (USB) to program serially the PAN coordinator (Gateway node) initially. Each packet transmitted is acknowledged and checksum verified and once the complete binary file is transferred, the new firmware gets flashed in PAN coordinator.
*   **Step 2**: The PAN coordinator now starts searching the network and scans for the sensor devices (coordinator) connected in the network and starts programming the sensor nodes one by one by transmitting the compiled binary file as packets of 64bytes

## Implementation

OTAP enables the programming of nodes by transmitting as data packets over the wireless network, allowing each node to program itself with the received data packets, without requiring a constant connection to PC. The received data packets put together are stored in the mote’s EEPROM. When a command is tasked to the PAN coordinator to modify or change a particular code, the starting address page is traced and cached to processor memory from the flash memory. The coordinator node is rebooted then automatically with the newly flashed program code.

For every data transfer, 64 bytes of data are sent and received from the PAN co-ordinator, providing an acknowledgment to the PC indicating whether the data was received or not as shown in [Fig. 5](#ch32.xhtml#fig32_5).

## OTA Flashing Time

If we need to wirelessly flash these nodes which are deployed at a larger separation distance, The flashing time has the potential to increase further due to the need for packet retries, which are necessary to compensate for packets lost as a result of poor channel quality. This phenomenon is depicted in [Fig. 7](#ch32.xhtml#fig32_7) (OTA Flashing Network Setup Time for Different Network Sizes), where theoretical calculations outline the comprehensive time required to flash nodes within the network. For instance, consider a scenario with a total of 10 nodes. In this case, the cumulative packets transferred within the network amount to 5580 for the broadcast app code. The total time taken to flash these 10 nodes is approximately 11.16 seconds, assuming a fixed data transfer rate of 25KB. As the number of nodes increased, the time required to complete the flashing process increases linearly. This linear increase in flashing time with larger network sizes imposes limitations on scalability. Consequently, there arises a necessity to optimize the flashing time in order to accommodate the expansion of the network.

![Fig. 7. Total packets transferred for OTA flash updates vs total number of nodes deployed in greenhouse](images/fig32_7_C.jpg)

## Conclusion

In this paper we implemented Over The Air Programming (OTAP) based WSN test bed implementation using SENSEnuts embedded IOT platform in LINUX to reprogram sensor motes wirelessly. The paper highlights the main challenges presented when we scale the size of the deployed WSN, the setup and reprogramming time will increase linearly. Due to the limitations of IEEE802.15.4 standard such as limited bandwidth (256Kbps), power and storage constraints, the flashing of binary files (firmware) wirelessly takes time and due to varying channel conditions, the complexity increases. The future work includes optimization of the flashing time and implementation of the remotely reprogramming in Greenhouse Monitoring Application.

# Mobile-Based Cloud Detection Model for Skin Cancer Using Machine Learning

K. Devi, B. Muthusenthil,^([^(25)](#fn25))

E-mail: [devii.jeya@gmail.com](mailto:devii.jeya@gmail.com)

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-33](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-33)

## Abstract

A recent development in the field of deep learning has taken the spotlight for creating rich applications. Computer-based applications in medicine are the upcoming projects, which are wide-spreading the advancement of the IT industry. This paper takes the readers and researchers on an expedition across the cloud-based approach to detecting skin cancers in people. We are aware that skin cancer is a fatal condition, and that improving the likelihood of effective survival depends on early identification. Deep learning approaches have shown up their strengths in terms of performance like sensitivity, accuracy, and precision. So, in this paper, we are using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in experimenting with image recognition and image classification to detect skin cancer. We are also deploying the application in a cloud platform so that anyone can use this with the help of the internet.

Keywords: Convolutional Neural Network, Image Classification, Skin Cancer, Cloud Computing, Deep Learning, Image Recognition, Transfer Learning

## Introduction

Skin cancer is merely subjected to ultraviolet (UV) radiation causing contagious disease among people ([Vijayalakshmi, 2019](#ch33.xhtml#ref33_1); Vedanti Chintawar & Jignyasa Sanghavi) . Early diagnosis is the initial possible measure reducing the risks of extending the disease to the next level ([Vijayalakshmi, 2019](#ch33.xhtml#ref33_1); Yuexiang li & Linlin Shen, 2018) .

Insights reports concede that there has been a 53% expansion in the melanoma cases analyzed every year (Esteva et al., 2017; (World Health Organization, n.d.). Multiple individuals kick the bucket because of skin disease each hour in the U.S. The death rate is under 14% on the off chance that it is analyzed in later stages ([Erkol et al., 2005](#ch33.xhtml#ref33_6); [Zorman et al., 1997](#ch33.xhtml#ref33_7)). Likewise, the endurance rate is over 97% in case it is analyzed in the beginning phases ([Siegel et al., 2018](#ch33.xhtml#ref33_8)). This tells us early detection helps us to easily overcome this disease.

Yet, the dermatologist’s expertise has a significant impact on precise determination. It has been noted that the top dermatologists struggle to effectively diagnose skin malignant growths with an accuracy rate of under 80% ([Marks, 2000](#ch33.xhtml#ref33_9)). Besides, talented dermatologists are extremely less. To conquer this issue of exactness and deficiency of clinical dermatologists, AI calculations can be utilized for identifying the presence of skin malignant growth. The cutting-edge model for skin malignant growth location is proposed by many creators (Esteva et al., 2017; [Kittler et al., 2002](#ch33.xhtml#ref33_10); [Yu et al., 2016](#ch33.xhtml#ref33_11)). Using this quality service can be provided. Due to the advancement in cloud computing, deploying our model in the cloud this service can be used by almost everyone. The Internet serves as a great helping hand in utilizing cloud-based systems. The image of the patient skin condition can be sent to the cloud system, which can predict the return of the result to the patient immediately. Furthermore, the cost and time taken for implementing this service are very less. An additional advantage is that patients do not have to wait for a skilled dermatologist for accurate results. A mobile-based model detection system is been proposed ([Xiangfeng Dai et al., n.d](#ch33.xhtml#ref33_12).). However, it has its drawbacks such as: High-performance mobile is required for such a model to run, time taken for the model to predict is very high and the machine learning model cannot be updated

In our paper, we overcome these drawbacks by proposing a model in which we deploy the model in a cloud-based computer so that prediction is done in the server rather than in the client device. Therefore, the client’s role is to just take a photo and upload it to the server. The processing and prediction are performed in the server and the result is sent back to the client. If we get a model with higher performance, it can be easily deployed in the server system.

## Recent Works

Earlier researchers first perform lesion segmentation, then extract the features from them and use that for skin cancer classification. To identify skin cancer, Manu and Yu made use of artificial neural networks, namely fully-convolutional residual networks ([Yu et al., 2016](#ch33.xhtml#ref33_11)). For lesion classification, Codella recently merged recent developments in machine learning technology with deep learning \[[14](#ch33.xhtml#ref33_14)\].

In order to train the model using supervised learning techniques, a lot of data and processing power are required. Duraipandian presented the use of the cloud for IoT for increasing the computation speed ([Duraipandian, 2020](#ch33.xhtml#ref33_15)). Therefore, these models can be deployed in cloud-based computers. For example, Alghatani and Rezgui (Khalid Alghatani & Abdelmounaam Rezgui, 2019) presented a platform for remote monitoring of patients. In addition, a system to monitor hypertension patients was presented by Melillo and Scala ([Ruiz-Zafra et al., 2013](#ch33.xhtml#ref33_17)). They used a cloud-based platform to develop mHealth apps that could be used for monitoring, collecting information, and viewing diagnostic videos remotely.

## Application Design and Architecture

### Overall System Design

We propose a cloud-based skin cancer detection system. It can be broadly classified into three parts — client input layer, cloud platform layer, and output visualization layer. The client takes a photo with help of input sensors like the camera. After capturing the photo is encrypted using a certain encryption algorithm and then it is uploaded to the server. When the cloud system receives the photo, it first decrypts the data using a specific decryption algorithm and it starts processing it. After predicting the result, it is encrypted and sent back to the client. The client receives the data from the server, decrypts the data, and displays the result. The server is used to deliver the detection of skin cancer model, which is trained separately. In order to guarantee total security, the information is encrypted during transmission.

In this architecture, the dataset is stored in the cloud environment and the deep learning model is completely trained in the cloud platform. Also, the prediction i.e. classifying whether the image contains skin cancer or not is computed in the cloud platform. The client’s role is to just upload an image and everything else is performed in the cloud. This also contains an authentication module so that only the authorized user can use this application. This architecture is exhibited in [Fig. 1](#ch31.xhtml#fig31_1).

## Client Input Layer

The client’s main role is to capture an image and send and receive data to and from the server. The client mainly consists of three modules: authentication, image capturing, and uploading the data to the cloud. In the authentication module, the end-user has to first register with his detail, and Cloud storage for the data is encrypted. Then the user has to log in with the same credentials. These credentials are again sent to the server. If the credentials are correct the send a positive reply then the user is allowed to use our application else not allowed.

![Fig. 1. Conceptual diagram of the proposed system](images/fig33_1_C.jpg)

Fig. 1. Conceptual diagram of the proposed system

After successful authentication, the image is captured with help of the input sensors and uploaded to the server via a gateway device. This device sends an HTTP request to the server with the captured image with the help of the internet.

## Cloud Platform Layer

The server mainly consists of five modules: An authentication module, a Database module, a Machine learning training module, reception and transmission of data, and a machine learning model for prediction.

The server authentication module is to check and verify the user. When a user registers the details are saved in the database. Then when the user login those credentials are cross-checked with the database. If the user has already registered positive response is sent else a negative response is sent to the client. The dataset “HAM10000. Dataset” is downloaded from the source website and it is stored in the cloud storage. This database can be accessed by the API provided by the cloud service provider. The resource accessing overhead time is also managed by the cloud provided. The database module also contains user authentication data.

The complete deep learning model training is done on this cloud platform. The deep learning training module gets the data database and trains the machine learning model according to the given configuration. The time taken to train the model is normally very high. The model is trained before we deploy the application for public use. So this training time is not related to our application usage. It generates a model using deep learning with direct skin cancer prediction capabilities. This model is stored in a cloud database for further use.

Reception and transmission of the data module are used for communication with the end user. It decrypts the received data and encrypts the data sent to the client. The image which is sent by the user is sent as input is classified using the trained model. This classification is also completely done on the cloud platform. The time taken for this computation is very less because of the huge computation power available in the cloud platform, so there is not much delay for the result to be sent back. After this result is computed, the result is sent back to the client.

## Output Visualisation Layer

This module receives the output data from the cloud platform and displays that result to the user. It contains the skin output label corresponding to the input image.

## Experimentation and Implementation

The cloud environment for this application was created using Amazon web services. We use the skin cancer dataset from “The HAM10000. Dataset: A Large Collection of Multi-Source Dermatoscopic Images of Common Pigmented Skin Lesions” ([Tschandl et al., 2018](#ch33.xhtml#ref33_18)), which contain 10015 labeled images of seven types of skin problem which are 1) Melanocytic nevi 2) Melanoma 3) Benign keratosis 4) Basal cell carcinoma 5) Actinic keratoses 6) Vascular lesions 7) Dermatofibroma.

This entire dataset is downloaded and saved in the Amazon S3 bucket. From here the data is taken for the training of the deep learning model using the API provided by the Amazon S3 services.

The machine learning algorithms can be developed and trained using python (Python, n.d.)\] libraries like TensorFlow (Tensorflow, n.d.), PyTorch, Fastai, etc. We employ a technique known as transfer learning ([Pan & Yang, 2010](#ch33.xhtml#ref33_21); Karl [Weiss et al., 2016](#ch33.xhtml#ref33_22)) . In this method, we can use the features gathered from all the pre-trained models that were trained on a particularly large dataset for our model. DenseNet ([Huang et al., 2016](#ch33.xhtml#ref33_23); [Duraipandian, 2020](#ch33.xhtml#ref33_15))CNN is being used. We are using the feature-extracting layer of the DenseNet model and adding our custom classifier which helps us map the features to the corresponding label in our skin cancer detection. The precision of our model is 0.889166 and recall is 0.889166, and F-Measure is 0.88916.

## Conclusion

The prominent drawback in implementing CNNs or the one which is impermissible in adopting and executing the CNN architecture is fitting the high computational power, which is very well handled with a cloud monitoring system. As the image is sent to the cloud systems the computation is done in the cloud. Also, our deep layered model captures the features and classifies the result with high accuracy that the leading dermatologist. Also, this solution is available to a wider range now. Summing up, good quality medical service is now available to everyone at the correct time, irrespective of place and time. So, this disease can be identified and cured easily.

# Human Brain Tumors and the Role of the Neural Network

R. Sankaranarayanan^([^(27)](#fn27))

E-mail: [sankarnba@gmail.com](mailto:sankarnba@gmail.com), [msen1982@gmail.com](mailto:msen1982@gmail.com), [profbcr@yahoo.com](mailto:profbcr@yahoo.com)

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-35](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-35)

## Abstract

The brain acts as the body’s master control system. It regulates the mind, memory, voice, and body. When the brain is functioning properly, it acts swiftly and instinctively to govern the operation of several organs. But, when issues arise, the consequences may be catastrophic. Inflammation in the brain is the root cause of most mental health issues in humans. Yet, the death of brain cells, as occurs in a stroke, may also put pressure on nerves and impair cognitive ability. Images play a crucial part in the diagnosis of brain disorders in humans and may be used to diagnose a wide variety of neurological conditions. Imaging examinations may be used to detect a brain Tumor. The brain is imaged with the use of X-rays, powerful magnets, or radioactive chemicals. Examining the brain using a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or computed tomography (CT) scan is the gold standard for diagnosing brain disorders. If a brain Tumor is present, it will be seen on these scans in virtually every case. The images are converted into data sets and analyzed datasets analyze whether the tumor is low, stable or whether it an be decreased or the steps to take regarding brain tumor. Neural network predicts what happens to the tumor in the future. Data Sets are converted to neural networks which exactly predict what happens in the future.

Keywords: Brain tumor, Brain tumor classification, Convolutional Neural Network, Recurrent Neural Network, Visual Geometry Group

## Introduction

In response to input from the senses, the human brain processes the data and relays it to the rest of the neurological system, which in turn relays it to the rest of the body, including the muscles. The human brain, like the brains of other mammals, contains a basic structure and a layer that is related to the body ([Fig. 1](#ch35.xhtml#fig35_1)). The human brain weighs 31 bees and makes two percent of human body weight. The average male brain has nearly 78 cubic inches and average female brain has 69 cubic inches, the female brain is lesser than 10% of male brain. The cerebrum is the primary brain structure and is found posterior to the skull. The human brain contains 86 billion nerve cells and also the same number of non-neuronal cells.

![Fig. 1. Human Brain](images/fig35_1_C.jpg)

[Fig. 1. Human Brain](#ch35.xhtml#R_fig35_1)

An artificial neural network, or simply a network of cells. In the aspects of deep learning, neurone network is considered as its subset. In general, the biological neurons receive signals from one another and it is received through human brain ([Fig. 2](#ch35.xhtml#fig35_2)). An artificial neural network has two distinct layers. I) Input layer II) hidden layer. For data to go to the next layer of the network, each node must be connected to another node and have Hassan associated with it. The neural network uses the data it is trained on to make incremental improvements over time. These learning algorithms, which have been optimized for precision, are potent resources in the fields of computer science and artificial intelligence, enabling us to rapidly classify and cluster data. Speech or picture recognition tasks that used to take specialists hours may now be accomplished in minutes. The many varieties of neural networks each serve a specific function. In feedforward neural networks, in- and out-layers are the primary areas of concentration. Knowing that they are made up of sigmoid neurons and not perceptions is crucial because of the nonlinear nature of most situations in the real world.

![Fig. 2. Neural Network](images/fig35_2_C.jpg)

[Fig. 2. Neural Network](#ch35.xhtml#R_fig35_2)

Convolution Neural Networks (CNN) is similar to feet-forward networks which are usually utilized for image recognition patterns and for all computer vision ([Fig. 3](#ch35.xhtml#fig35_3)). The feedback loop that characterizes a recurrent neurone network also identifies the algorithms that use such data to anticipate stock market and sales trends in real-time. Acute spinal cord injury, Alma diseases, and other neurological ailments affect many people (type). An aberrant cell development that forms a mass in the human brain is called a brain Tumor. Some brain Tumors are benign, representing the earliest stage of cancer in the brain, while others may be very deadly. Tumors that originate in the brain are called primary brain Tumors, whereas cancers that spread from other parts of the body are called secondary primary Tumors. The brain Tumor is classified into acoustic neuroma Astrocytoma (type). Depending on the brain tumor’s size, location, and development pace, the underlying science and symptoms of the disease could vary greatly different. Symptoms may include a shift in headache patterns, an increase in the severity of existing headaches, nausea, and vomiting, blurred vision, trouble maintaining balance or expressing oneself clearly in writing or speech, extreme fatigue, mental fogginess, uncertainty, a lack of impulsive behavior, and changes in personality or behavior ([Fig. 4](#ch35.xhtml#fig35_4)). There is an effort to use artificial neural networks to detect and diagnose human brain cancer.

![Fig. 3. General Workflow of Brain Tumor Classification with FFN, CNN & RNN](images/fig35_3_C.jpg)

## Materials and Methods

The brain diseases are diagnosed by the following methods such as biopsy, dynamic testing, image test, laboratory test, mental function test, neurological exam. In this paper, we focus to identify brain Tumors using pet, CT, MRI, and ultrasound scans.

The metabolic or biochemical activity of tissues and organs may be seen on a Positron emission tomography scan. Radioactive drugs are used in the PET scan to display both typical and aberrant metabolic functions. When other imaging tests, such as computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging, fail to identify disease, a PET scan may be used to detect aberrant metabolism following the injection of a tracer. PET scans for brain problems, PET scan be used to examine specific brain disorders including Tumors, Alzheimer’s decision, and seizures; PET pictures are frequently paired with CT and MRI and are hence dubbed PET-CT & PET-MRI scans. A PET scan may show the differences between a healthy brain and one damaged by Alzheimer’s disease, in which red is lost and yellow, blue, and green are increased.

In testing the human brain there are different modalities. In the process of testing the brains, the images are received through the sources like CT and MRI scanning process. As a result of testing the images from the brain and its functional process. It is observed that MRI scanning technology produces remarkable results compared to the other CT scanning technology.

In clinical practice, it is expected to possess significant precision in scanning technology. The CNN based scanning technology extends to provide the expectation of clinicians. The values received in CNN are classified and the accurate value is denoted as a system with low level of complexity. The output of the CNN is classified into five types of brain images. These images are obtained from MM scanning technology. The objective framework of the MRI scanning technology states that it helps clinical practitioners to classify the brain images of the brain that is affected by Tumors. The morphological operations and region filling is undertaken to receive images from database.

When the picture has been prepared, several techniques, such as BWT, are used to segment the Tumor area, and then the futures are extracted using other methods and the image is categorized. The MRP brain image that was retrieved from the database was a 256 x 256-pixel axial plane ([Fig. 5](#ch35.xhtml#fig35_5)). If you have an MRI of your brain and want to pinpoint the exact location of the Tumor, you may utilize a technique called “segmentation,” which involves converting the resulting gray image into a white-and-black version of the original. In obtaining the data for medical purposes there is a highly significant role played by the Naive Bayes hash. The result of the data shows that there is a superior performance due to the attributes being independent of each other.

Stick metrology is used for the classification. Class probabilities are computed, and the most probable classes are predicted. Naive Bayes classification methods use Bayesian statistics, which places heavy emphasis on the importance of prior probabilities for making predictions about the future. the possibility under certain conditions can

  
$$P(B \\mid A) = \\sum\\limits\_{i = 1}^{n}P(Ax \\mid B)$$  

It is feasible to calculate the conditional probability of each Ax given B, where A = A1, A2, A3,... An, if the attribute A has the capabilities of an attribute with a restive probability ratio.

## Result and Discussions

In analyzing the brain Tumors many researchers have their view in proposing the experimental research with qualitative and quantitative. The studies that are undertaken qualitatively show that there is a need for lexicon feature investigation. The present research undertaken shows that the classification of brain Tumors is segmented based on the image analysis. Many studies are being undertaken now on the topic of voxel and volume feature extraction. # Best Fit Topic Model Coherence Improvement for Subectivity Analysis of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus

J. Jeyalakshmi[^(28)](#fn28)

Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Rajalakshmi Engineering College-Chennai-India

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-36](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-36)

## Abstract

The subjectivity analysis can shed light on the crux of content over an open discussion forum. Gestational Diabetes Mellitus(GDM) has become more common among young pregnant women in India. To analyze the public mentality, causality analysis, and spreading awareness, it will be helpful to analyze the content of tweets. Methods and Material: The system uses Best Fit Topic Modeling and Coherence improvement by hyperparameter tuning on the corpora crawled from Twitter over GDM. Results: The Best Fit Topic Model is drafted from LDA, CTM, and Gibbs Sampling. The measures like Inter topic Distance relations are drafted using Multi Dimension Scaling, Coherence scores are quantified and is optimized to 70.8% from 39% using LDA-Mallet by hyperparameter tuning. The system gives inferences regarding Physical activity-based control measures for GDM, Low Glycemic Index diet, Consumption of prescribed medicine, and quantity ex. folate content, Risk of potato causing GDM. Conclusion: The proposed work shows subjectivity analysis on Twitter content for GDM and presents better inferences on the subject of discussion.

Keywords: Data Mining, Gestational Diabetes, Diabetes Mellitus, Machine Learning, Prediction, Geo-Spatial Analysis, Etc

## Introduction

GDM (Gestational Diabetes Mellitus) is becoming a more common short-term illness among middle-aged women. Women diagnosed with GDM have remained at risk for diabetes for 4-5 years, even though it is a short-term condition. GDM has been found to affect at least 10% of all pregnant women. Sentiment analysis is used in the proposed system to try to extract such tacit information from tweets and give an analysis of the symptoms, precautions, and preventive treatments discussed in the tweets. In light of this knowledge, the proposed study analyses population health using open social network content, such as Twitter, and uses Opinion, Sentiment mining, Topic Modelling, Coherence improvisation, and Inter-topic distance parameters to identify people’s mentalities and disease-specific content of discussion. Building Best Fit Topic Models to properly infer the substance of the discussion is the focus of the research. With MALLET, it improves the coherence of topic models. The paper is organized to [Chapter 1](#ch1.xhtml) based on Introduction, chapter 2 based on Literature and existing work, chapter 3 based on Experimentation, and [Chapter 4](#ch4.xhtml) on Conclusion and Future Work.

## Related work

The existing systems are summarized in this chapter in regard to the analysis of textual content over social media.

Hao [Cui et al. (2021](#ch36.xhtml#ref36_1)), proposed a study on social media in China based on COVID-19. They used content on Sina Weibo microblogging website for their analysis. They discovered a decay in attention which did not help find the impact of the efforts by the government towards spreading awareness on COVID-19 pandemic. Sebastian [Hermes et al. (2020](#ch36.xhtml#ref36_2)), had suggested a model to study the impact of social media on patients ([Cui & Kertez, 2021](#ch36.xhtml#ref36_1); [Hermes et al., 2020](#ch36.xhtml#ref36_2); [Dyer & Kolic, 2020](#ch36.xhtml#ref36_3)). The social media in comparison with the traditional industries, work with data and people who generate the data and content. The influence of the actors in generating value for the healthcare service provider. The value of the organization, the transformation in the value, the capture of the value and the transformation of the process, and the delivery of value were discussed in the paper ([Ferretti et al., 2019](#ch36.xhtml#ref36_4); [Salas-Zarate et al., 2017](#ch36.xhtml#ref36_5); [Singh et al., 2017](#ch36.xhtml#ref36_6)). Joel Dye et al. (2010), had proposed a study on sentiment of risk perception over Twitter on COVID-19. The study of the open social network was based on a hypothesis, that the mortality rate during COVID-19 was related to the attention of the netizens([Takabe, 2016](#ch36.xhtml#ref36_7); [Barnwal et al., 2016](#ch36.xhtml#ref36_8); [Woo & Chen, 2016](#ch36.xhtml#ref36_9)). The emotion and semantic analysis were done. Co-occurence of the words was investigated. The “death” was an interesting node with lot of co-occurring terms. Many such inferences were drafted. The study has led to usage of Topic Models and hyperparameter tuning to improvise the inference of content in the unstructured text.

## Experimentation

The proposed system architecture is presented in this section along with the results and discussions in [Fig. 1](#ch36.xhtml#fig36_1). The work is implemented in Python and R Studio using packages like TwitterR, Sentiment, etc., The analysis is presented in broadly two categories as suggested below.

![Fig. 1. Proposed System](images/fig36_1_C.jpg)

[Fig. 1. Proposed System](#ch36.xhtml#R_fig36_1)

1.  Best Fit Topic Modeling
2.  Coherence Improvement by Hyper-parameter tuning

## Best Fit Topic Modeling

The results of topic modeling are retrieved by creating a best fit out of Latent Dirichlet allocation, Correlated Topic Model, and Gibbs Sampling as an ensemble. The Subjectivity analysis reveals facts about the following issues regarding GDM in [Fig. 2](#ch36.xhtml#fig36_2).

![Fig. 2. Topics discussed in the GDM tweets](images/fig36_2_B.jpg)

[Fig. 2. Topics discussed in the GDM tweets](#ch36.xhtml#R_fig36_2)

*   Physical activity based control measures for GDM.
*   Risk of potato causing GDM

# A Decentralized Application-DAPP for Remote Voting System Based on Blockchain Technology

K. Iswarya,^([^(29)](#fn29))

E-mail: [aishwaryakannan45@gmail.com](mailto:aishwaryakannan45@gmail.com), [bpecleela2005@gmail.com](mailto:bpecleela2005@gmail.com), [cdevimayavanpd@gmail.com](mailto:cdevimayavanpd@gmail.com)

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-37](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-37)

## Abstract

In any country, democratic voting is mandatory because of widespread mistrust of the traditional voting system. It has been observed that people have been violated in their fundamental rights. Lack of transparency has led to challenges to other digital voting systems. The majority of voting methods are not sufficiently transparent, which makes it highly challenging for the government to win over voters’ trust. The previous and present digital voting systems have failed because they are susceptible to manipulation. The major objective is to address any errors or unfair voting practices that may arise in both the traditional and computerized voting systems. To ensure a fair election and lessen unfairness, blockchain technology can be included in the voting process. The computerized voting methods are not flawless enough to be used on a broad scale, and the physical voting systems have numerous problems as well. This evaluates the requirement for a remedy to safeguard citizens’ democratic rights. This editorial proposes a framework built on cutting-edge blockchain technology to create a reliable working relationship between voters and election officials. Without using any actual polling places, the suggested method offers a framework that may be used to conduct voting activity digitally through blockchain. Our suggested architecture employs adaptable consensus techniques to allow for a scalable blockchain. During a chain transaction, smart contracts offer a safe connection between the user and the network. Discussions have also focused on the voting system’s security, which is built on a blockchain. Transactions on the blockchain can now be encrypted using cryptographic hashes. We assess the potential of appropriated record developments in particular through the depiction of a pertinent examination, specifically the pattern of a political race, and the use of blockchain-based software, which takes good care of security issues and reduces the cost of administering a cross-country political campaign.

Keywords: Blockchain, Smart contracts, Cryptographic hash, Consensus algorithms

## Introduction

The voting system must be as precise, effective, and efficient as possible because voting is one of the most crucial democratic instruments. With regard to defining the locations, hiring employees, and mitigating security threats at polling places, blockchain can significantly reduce the time and resources required. Blockchain-based digital elections provide cost savings while lowering the possibility of unfair votes. It can improve transaction traceability, voting system reliability, and transparency.

A voting machine that is connected to a centralized database has been utilized in traditional digital voting systems. A person with physical access to this device can tamper with it. In contrast to an immutable blockchain, which wouldn’t be affected by a single network saboteur, the voting system’s entire network might as a result experience one potential point of failure. Information is decentralized and kept on a blockchain, where the veracity of the records is continuously checked. As a result, the peer-to-peer network would continue to provide all services even if a node were the victim of a malicious attack; just that node would be affected. Blockchain technology has developed to the point where it can be trusted and utilized as a private voting ledger. More security and trust may now be found with blockchain than with earlier systems. It doesn’t need a real voting machine or module, which is always susceptible to hacking through tampering tools. The most appealing aspect of this method is its transparency, which gives voters confidence that their votes are being cast in the most appropriate ways. Considerable systems are being studied for deployment, including banking, healthcare, food safety, and cryptocurrency trading. Blockchain technology can be used to conduct an honest election that protects voter confidentiality and confidence.

The opportunity to meddle with votes or add fake votes while they are being counted exists in the traditional voting procedure. The authorities have the authority to proclaim false results when they are influenced by a third party. The voter is not given any assurance that his vote would be counted or not. Overall, the traditional voting procedure does not guarantee unbiased voting or transparency. Only digitalizing the system or using digital voting devices to cast ballots won’t fix the problem. Hackers may manipulate these computerized voting devices, which would interfere with the voting process. Therefore, a decentralized system is needed that can maintain data security even if one node becomes corrupt. This paper’s primary goal is to encourage the use of a blockchain-based system of voting in order to safeguard against manipulation of the voting process and win over voters. The premise that a node connected to the network will never be erased is one of the fundamental characteristics of blockchain technology. Blockchain technology, which provides decentralized data storage, makes it possible.

It is impossible to simultaneously delete the data from every node since it is duplicated across every node in the network and is stored on numerous nodes across the chain. Additionally, since each node computes the data separately before combining it, the computation required to tally the results is minimized. The use of blockchain in the voting system is proposed as a way to prevent vote tampering and the casting of ghost votes. Each ID may be used to cast one vote. Blockchain prevents any unauthorized attempts to modify any part of the chain. It ends the voting system’s reliance on middlemen, which helps conserve resources and reduces human error.

## Related Work

In order to prevent vote fraud or tampering, Yang [Yang et al., (2021](#ch37.xhtml#ref37_2))proposes a self-tallying electoral system based on blockchain called “PriScore” that supports score voting. Each voter can give the candidates distinct assessment ratings (within a given range) using PriScore. The aggregate of each ballot’s assessment scores, which are anonymous to protect the privacy of voters, should equal a predefined constant.The simultaneous verification of both constraints demands, range proof and sum proof, is a critical problem in score casting. To demonstrate the scores satisfying two important conditions, we provide a novel method we term dual zero-knowledge proof (dual-ZKP), which nontrivially mixes distributed ElGamal crypto with 1-out-of-K” proof. Any party using PriScore can compute and check the election results because of the self-tallying process, which ensures fairness and avoids conflicts. According to the security analysis, PriScore satisfactorily satisfies the following requirements: eligibility, thoroughness, coherence, widespread verifiability, and multiple-voting detection.

A cryptographic method for an election with verified, end-to-end verifiable, and secret ballots was suggested by [Panja & Roy, (2021](#ch37.xhtml#ref37_3)). It suggests a safe and reliable system for voter registration and identification. It stops attempts to stuff ballots. In order to prevent any adversary from creating and secretly posting a legal ballot posted on the community noticeboard, they updated the DRE-ip system. This work suggests a technique that uses secure multi-party computing, non-interactive zero-knowledge (NIZK) proof, and Direct-Recording Electronic (DRE) devices to broadcast the final count without revealing the totals from particular DRE devices. The analysis demonstrates that the effective zero-knowledge proof (NIZK) made by [Lin & Zhang (2019](#ch37.xhtml#ref37_12)) for APSIPA ASC 2019 is invalid because it does not satisfy the bystander distinguishability requirement. As a result, it adds a superior NIZK proof, which boosts the system’s efficiency.

In order to establish and intimate the numerous fulminations brought on by an intrusion at multiple levels; Using Blockchain technology, [Rathee et al, (2021](#ch37.xhtml#ref37_4))created a secure and open IoT platform for electronic voting. Message tampering, DoS and DDoS attacks, and authentication latency are only a handful of the security factors that are investigated in order to certify the proposed system. They used the Social Weighted Rank technique and the Algorithm of Secured E-Voting Using Trusted IoT Devices to assess IoT trust.

A platform developed by [Farooq et al, (2022](#ch37.xhtml#ref37_1)) is based on cutting-edge blockchain technology and offers maximum system transparency and dependability in order to foster a relationship of trust between voters and election officials. With the use of this software, voting activities might be carried out online using blockchain without the need for physical polling places. Thanks to the use of adaptable consensus techniques, this provides a scalable blockchain. The voting process is more secure because of the Chain Security Algorithm used in the system. During a chain transaction, smart contracts provide an encrypted connection between the client and the network. The suggested system’s performance evaluation demonstrates the system’s capacity for deployment in a huge population.

Ethereum’s Blockchain-based electronic voting method was introduced by [Al-Madani et al, (2020](#ch37.xhtml#ref37_5)). This application can overcome the limitations and potential vulnerabilities of the centralized voting mechanism by utilizing Blockchain technology. This study illustrated the data security features of a blockchain. It developed a voting system that employs a smart contract in a decentralized way. After that, a local blockchain received a shared ledger for this application. As a platform, the application uses Ethereum Blockchain technology, and a decentralized database is used to store information about candidates, votes, and ballotter identities.

[Roopak & Sumathi, (2020](#ch37.xhtml#ref37_6))proposed a structure for a cryptographically secure electronic voting mechanism using a separate virtual ID offered by UIDAI. The Aadhar database allows for the collection of voter demographic data, including fingerprint data. To safeguard the confidentiality of the vote in the block, the fingerprint is turned into a digital signature during encryption. With the use of a private key and the use of hash work, this framework includes a method for carrying out operations on encoded data.

A mobile voting system was suggested by [Abayomi-Zannu et al, (2020](#ch37.xhtml#ref37_7))to lessen election fraud in Nigeria. This study developed a mobile system of voting that securely stores votes using blockchain technology and verifies voters using two factors. The suggested system was then assessed using the ISO 9241-11 usability paradigm, and the findings indicated that it obtained a good usability rating, indicating that it may be used in a voting process.

A mechanism called Provotum was suggested by [Killer et al, (2020](#ch37.xhtml#ref37_8)). By deploying a private blockchain as a publicly viewable message board and allowing the explicit allocation of trust across various permission blockchain nodes, Provotum introduces a brand-new and entirely decentralized blockchain-based Regional E-Voting system. Client-side encryption is used in Provotum’s fully distributed operation, enabling features like ballot secrecy, distributed key generation, smart contracts, asymmetric cryptography, and cooperative decryption. In order to enable open and end-to-end verification, the BC creates an audit trail.

In order to safeguard voter and vote confidentiality as well as poll integrity, [Qureshi et al, (2019](#ch37.xhtml#ref37_9)) presented SeVEP, a secure and fully transparent voting system. It also authenticates voter identification using a multifactor authentication technique, permits multiple votes throughout the allotted voting period, prohibits double voting, and offers verifiability and uncoercibility in the event of malfunctioning voting machines. SeVEP is a secure, verifiable, and useful e-polling system, as demonstrated by its efficiency, security, and comparative evaluation in terms of security attributes and cryptographic costs.

In order to improve voting security and transparency, [Pandey et al, (2019](#ch37.xhtml#ref37_10))created the VoteChain voting system using the blockchain. Vote data is kept on a distributed public ledger using a blockchain. For establishing consensus among servers, this system uses Proof of Work and a HashCash variation called VoteMaker.

[Sivaram et al, (2022](#ch37.xhtml#ref37_11))suggested the COVID-19 Pandemic - Remote Voting System (C19P-RVS). The system’s entire operations will be dependable based on the application software, which further minimizes duplication during the Aadhaar data verification. With his automatic authorization and verified system compliance, the voter is granted access to remote voting activities, and the entire process provides legitimacy.

[Lin & Zhang (2019](#ch37.xhtml#ref37_12))have developed a method that uses Blockchain as a bulletin board and “Efficient One-out-of-T” zero-knowledge proof to facilitate multiple-candidate voting (ZKP). The concerns with adaptable and reversible are also fixed. It can be utilized in intimate, private situations that require anonymity, such as board elections in corporations. The results of the performance assessment demonstrate that the recommended ZKP uses less time.

## Proposed Methodology

The envisaged architecture provides a framework that might be utilized to carry out voting procedures virtually using blockchain technology without using any actual polling locations. In this approach, a person’s computerized National ID is confirmed from the database so they can vote from anywhere, regardless of whether they are in another country. Each user has equitable access to the entire voting process through the system. Additionally, it provides post-voting traceability. Voters register in the system using their access data. To enroll a voter into the system, the system uses her ID information and checks it against an online database. Complete voter data is stored in the system. Voting Coins (VC) awarded to each voter who successfully registers in the system will be added to your wallet. Thus every voter receives a single VC in in order to avoid double voting.

After completing the verification, the voter is added to the database of the system. The blockchain is configured using a single-chain system. The method also leverages the country’s national database in order to protect the people’s voting right to cast an honest ballot. Each vote triggers a transaction that includes the voter’s National ID. The transaction is subsequently mined by the minors, who then deposit it in the blockchain. All across the voting process, Vote Coin from the voter’s account is also exploited.

The registered voter is only permitted to use one vote coin at a time. After signing in with their credentials, the ballotter is routed to the vote-casting portal, where they can see every contender in the race in their district. When a voter requests to cast a ballot, the system uses the blockchain to cross-reference the ballotter’s digitized National ID credentials with all of the previously completed transactions to verify the ballotter’s right to poll.

If a session hash is discovered to match the voter’s electronic National ID, the voter will be unlogged from the system and the claim will be rejected. If no vote has been cast, the miner gets the request to append the node.

A transaction hash is used to track the transaction, which is performed out by the miner. The voting chain is then connected to the node after that. The votes are completely protected by a cryptographic hash. The chain will grow by one block for each registered voter. The voting method also makes sure that each user could only cast one vote by utilizing the voting currency. Regardless of whether the casting coin’s balance is left unchanged due to a technical issue, the process ensures that no voter has cast a duplicate ballot. The miner will immediately reject any rogue nodes or requests made by voters if it can tell if the transaction hash was generated using the voter’s computerized National ID or not. After effectively executing the transaction, the vote was added to the overall number of votes cast in the election. The voter offered a unique session hash that he could use to authenticate his vote online. The voter’s wallet will be depleted of all vote currency if a vote is correctly cast.

With the utilization of blockchain technology, various systems have incorporated the voting mechanism. The information about their typical response time and security requirement compliance in graphs [Figs. 2](#ch37.xhtml#fig37_2) and [3](#ch37.xhtml#fig37_3).

## Cryptographic Hash

The privacy of the user’s identity is one of the many advantages of cryptographic hashing, which sustains the statistics secret from any system intruders, and cryptographic hashing is implemented with SHA-256 and Advanced Encryption Standard (AES). Because only the person who is authorized to use the transaction can decrypt it and access the data using his private key, the transaction is secure while it travels over the network to be pushed to a node. By entering the address of his transaction, it is possible to track the voter’s vote; the voter is informed via SMS and email as soon as the vote is cast. By using the hash value of the transaction that is provided on the registered phone number, voters can monitor their vote on the blockchain. The information gathered during the voting procedure is included in the vote data. The content is still obscured, safe, and secure. Only the voter has access to the tracing information, and only the ballotter can witness and validate their voting history. The transaction is locked using the citizen’s public key once it has been committed in a block. The tracking node is perceived using the ballotter’s public key. Using his individual secret key, the voter can see the transaction that was made by his wallet. Once a vote has been cast, a voter can only observe their vote; they are never able to modify or cancel it. Cryptography is used to encrypt any user information transferred during a transaction.

![Fig. 1. Block diagram](images/fig37_1_B.jpg)

Fig. 1. Block diagram

## Smart Contract

Simple blockchain entrenched strategy called “smart contracts” that execute when certain criteria are met. A contract is often implemented automatically so that both participants can be sure of the outcome right away, without the need for a mediator or a lag. Smart contracts provide a secure link between the user and the network during the execution of a transaction in the chain. These rules are universal to the blockchain and cannot, even under any conditions, be ignored. All nodes must follow the smart contracts in order for the vote to be successfully saved in the system.

## Result and Discussion

The proposed decentralized application for a distant location voting system based on blockchain technology is built using smart contracts, advanced encryption standards (AES) and SHA-256. This system satisfies the security criteria for maximum ballot secrecy, completeness, soundness, Fairness, personal and global verifiability, detection of double votes, and the absence of disputes and self-tallying. Because it employs the more efficient method of developing a dynamic consensus algorithm to lessen the large computational power utilized by the blockchain, this system’s usability functions effectively. When the system operates transparently, people are much more likely to count on it and trust it.

## Conclusion

The purpose of the suggestion of an ethereum - based electoral system solution was to foster confidence between both the government and the public to persuade them that their voting integrity is safeguarded. The blockchain voting system also makes the process accessible and trustworthy.The existing voting process is incredibly expensive in every country, but the alternative approach would use blockchain polling technique to make voting less expensive, quicker, and more trustworthyPeople’s relationships with their representative democracy are thus improved as a result of the system’s dependability and transparency. The suggested strategy offers a well-founded, open, and trustworthy framework for the government and the populace. The outlined structure provides a favorable result according to the performance assessment of blockchain-based in VMS. The study indicated the system’s effectiveness maintains efficiency even when handling a significant volume of blockchain transactions.

# Diagnosis of Mild Cognitive Impairment Using Multimodal Imaging With Machine Learning Techniques

Ms. K. R. Nandhashree,^([^(30)](#fn30))

E-mail: [nandhashree29@gmail.com](mailto:nandhashree29@gmail.com), [pjshree12@gmail.com](mailto:pjshree12@gmail.com)

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-38](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-38)

## Abstract

Computer-aided identification of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) can assist physicians to a wide extent in the timely diagnosis of the presence of dementia in aged people. Also, the unavailability of indisputable diagnostic methodology makes early recognition of AD a significant health concern. A few non-invasive biomarkers have been proposed, including Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) based volumetric analysis, Positron Emission Tomography (PET) based metabolic activity analysis, as alternatives in contrast to neuropsychological assessment, which helps in diagnosis. These methodologies have indicated encouraging results, but a complete data fusion analysis has not led to examining whether these various modalities convey corresponding data and assuming this case, the framework of whether they can be joined to give a progressively precise analysis is taken for the research. In this exertion, an analysis of consolidating MRI and PET data utilizing an ensemble classifier-based joined pixel fusion approach is employed in this work. The feature extraction is performed using a novel hybrid method combining GLDM, MSER, and EHS. Better performance is obtained using this novel technique with ensemble classifiers. Accuracy of about 86% is achieved using this CAD approach.

Keywords: Alzheimer’s disease, Feature optimization, Feature Extraction, MRI. PET.

## Introduction

AD, is a kind of neurodegenerative dementia and the most recognized reason for dementia, comprising 60 to 90% of all symptoms considered (American Psychiatric Association-APA 2013). AD accounts for one in the list of valid reasons for death in many nations. Early diagnosis helps in preventing the advancement of AD (Ding & Yei, 2019; [Peng et al., 2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_26)). Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) is the starting stage of dementia ([Agarwal & Bedi, 2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_2); [Anter et al., 2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_6); [Baltrusaitis et al., 2018](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_7); [Baskar & Annadurai, 2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_9)). On the off chance that the ailment is analyzed at this stage, medication can be arranged, and through regular follow up we can predict the advancement of dementia. MRI scans are utilized to investigate the structural deformations of the internal organs within the body. To defeat the challenges in analyzing the clinical image, the segmentation procedure of computerized imaging is utilized which gives an increment in demonstrative efficiency. The Positron Emission Tomography (PET) scan is a brain imaging technique that gives information about how the brain tissues are functioning.

## Exploratory Study

For AD prognosis, many methods have employed development in feature extraction ([Acharya et al., 2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_1); [Alickovic et al., 2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_5); [Lulu et al., 2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_23)) and selection ideas using one or two modalities. In [Alickovic et al, (2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_5)) the histogram is used to transfer images to feature vectors. AD classification in [Ahmed et al, (2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_4)); [Duc, (2020](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_12));[Han, (2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_13)); [Islam & Zhang, (2018](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_14)); [Jain et al, (2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_15)); [Jimenez-Mesa, (2020](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_16)); [Ju et al, (2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_17)); [Kanghan et al, (2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_18)); [Kruthika et al, (2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_19)); [Liang et al, (2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_20)); [Lowe et al, (2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_21)); [Lu et al, (2018](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_22)); [Lulu et al, (2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_23)); [Bhatia, (2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_10)); [Ju et al, (2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_17))is done using deep learning techniques employed on the brain network and using gene data. The network is built by considering the connectivity of the regions of the brain obtained using resting-state fMRI. In [Ahmed et al, (2018](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_3)) a survey is given by the researchers where a conclusion stating that the deep learning and multimodal approach combing functional and structural modality can enhance the accuracy of disease identification. Disease diagnostics with neuroimaging information have utilized many machine-learning calculations ([Bastia, 2018](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_8); [Moore et al., 2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_24); [Pan et al., 2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_25); [Peng et al., 2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_26); [Razavi et al, 2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_27)). The reason is that multimodal information has more amount of information than considering single modality data \[2\]. The concept of fusion in images helps in providing an accurate description of the framework and reduces the memory requirement by fusion of images instead of storing all the imaging modalities ([Richhariya, 2020](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_28); [Sanchez-Reyna, 2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_29); [Shaikh & Ali, 2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_30)).

From the literature survey, the inference made is that only a single modality is used in most of the works ([Anter et al, 2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_6); [Moore et al, 2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_24); [Pan et al, 2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_25)) . Thus, considering the multimodal approach of combining a structural modality (i.e.) MRI and functional modality (i.e.,) PET is a rationale for this research work. Multimodal image fusion ([Liang et al, 2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_20); [Lowe et al, 2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_21); [Lu et al, 2018](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_22))and classification ([Baskar & Annadurai, 2019](#ch38.xhtml#ref38_9))have drawn a considerable amount of research space in the past decade.

## Methods

In this section, the proposed framework and the procedures used are described in brief. The proposed multimodal framework is portrayed in [Fig. 1](#ch38.xhtml#fig38_1).

![Fig. 1. Multimodal Classification Framework](images/fig38_1_B.jpg)

[Fig. 1. Multimodal Classification Framework](#ch38.xhtml#R_fig38_1)

## Image Acquisition

The MRI and the PET scan images are obtained from the standard ADNI, and from that ADNI1\_ Annual 2 yr\_3T and ADNI1\_Baseline\_3T are used in particular. 520 MRI and 728 PET data have been used in the work.

## Preprocessing

For all the ADNI data obtained, we consider the MRI modality achieved at 1.5T and the PET modality. All the artifacts of both modalities are pre-processed to remove the skull, which may lead to an accurate classification. This removes the non-brain regions of the brain and is done using a brain surface extraction algorithm. The midsagittal line alignment is done to align the sagittal part of the brain. The original image differs from its coordinate system because the patient’s head remains tilted. The inhomogeneity is corrected initially to reduce the errors in the co-registration of the images.

## Segmentation

The algorithm partitions an image into discrete regions consisting of each pixel having the same attributes. To be meaningful and valuable for image analysis and understanding. The fuzzy c - means is a technique for grouping that permits one bit of information to have a place with at least two clusters.

## Image Fusion

The multimodal fusion method is used with the nonsubsampled contourlet transform (NSCT). Initially, on preregistered raw images, NSCT was run to obtain their low and high-frequency subbands. The NSCT is a multiscale, shift-invariant, multi-direction expansion that helps in giving a fast execution. The NSCT has demonstrated to be extremely proficient in image denoising and image enhancement.

## Feature Extraction

This module is done with the hybrid novel algorithm by combining the below 3 algorithms. All the feature extraction algorithms used are texture-based analyses.

## Gray-Level Difference Method (GLDM)

Two pixels were given an absolute difference in grey level and separated by a specific displacement d. The motion vector can be computed from [Eq. (1)](#ch38.xhtml#math38_1) and the probability density function can be computed from [Eq. (2)](#ch38.xhtml#math38_2).

(1)  
$$\\begin{array}{l} {\\delta = (\\Delta x,\\Delta y)} \\\\ \\left. \\text{Let,~}S\\delta(x,y) = \\middle| S(x,y) - S(x + \\Delta x,y + \\Delta y) \\right| \\\\ \\end{array}$$  

(2)  
D(i ∣ *δ*) = *P**r**o**b*\[(S*δ*(**x**, **y**) = i\]  

The initial values are attained from the input image. By concatenating the angular second moment, contrast, entropy, and mean that are calculated from PDF, a feature vector is calculated.

## Maximally Stable Extremal Regions (MSER)

MSER is a stable connected component with a sequence of gray-level pixels of the image. If we exhibit a sequence of thresholded images inside frame t relating to threshold t, We would initially see a black image at that point and the white spots associated with the local intensity minima would appear. All pixels below the threshold would be white, and all pixels above or equal to the threshold would be black. Gradually the white level becomes greater. Over a period, these white spots will merge until the whole image is white. *Edge Histogram Descriptor (EHD)*

An EHD is a type of feature vector that depicts the spatial distribution of five types of edges. A neighborhood is a set of five edges that are relative to one another and may be considered a sub-image or an image block. The sub-image is found by partitioning the available image space into 4 x 4 non-overlapping blocks. In this way, the image partition makes 16 equivalent estimated blocks that are independent of the size of the initial image.

## Feature Selection

Feature selection, also termed as a selection in variables or attribute selection, is the technique for choosing a subset of features (variables, indicators) that are used in model construction. Discrete Particle Swarm Optimization (DPSO) is a kind of optimization technique that falls under the category of an Iterative optimization technique that optimizes a candidate solution by attempting to improve it based on a proportion of input value.

## Results and Discussion

The proposed framework is extended to classify normal control patients and MCI patients. Different classification algorithms are used and clearly, from [Figure 2](#ch38.xhtml#fig38_2) the ensemble classifier outperforms the other classifiers like SVM, KNN, and Naïve Bayes. The Ensemble classifier produces an accuracy of 86%. Other performance metrics that are calculated are precision, recall, F-measure, and specificity. The specificity for all the other classifiers is 100%.

## Future Work

Several ideas are outlined that can be used to extend the scope of this research work to diagnose and classify patients with multiclass diseases like CN, MCI, and AD. The region of interest and the background of medical images, which often depict clinically relevant regions and clinically irrelevant backgrounds, may be separately coded at different quality levels.

## Conclusion

A clear investigation of the type of classification on AD is done using the classification techniques and the multimodal strategy which will aid the neuro medical clinicians and doctors to identify and to provide a follow-up for the patients with an accuracy of 86% using the MRI and PET images. The given method is based on the multimodal fusion strategy and the texture-based features are obtained with the hybrid of GLDM, MSER, EHD from which the optimal set of features is further extracted.
