# Contact Less Virtually Controlling System Using Computer Vision Techniques

Yakkala Lahari, Genipi Yaswanth and D. Chitradevi[^(35)](#fn35)

Department of Computer Science Engineering, Hindustan Institute of Technology and Science, Chennai, India

E-mail: [yakka1a1ahari1181@gmail.com](mailto:yakka1a1ahari1181@gmail.com); [yaswanth2808@gmail.com](mailto:yaswanth2808@gmail.com);

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-44](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-44)

## Abstract

The paper suggests a contact-free virtual controlling system that uses hand movements and fingertips to detect mouse clicks (Scrolling functions, Left-click, Right-click, Brightness control, Volume control, drag operations) rather than using a physical mouse or wireless (Bluetooth) mouse. This proposed system has a built-in camera or web camera which will detect the face of authorized persons, only those persons can access the virtual mouse. The physical mouse and wireless mouse are great inventions of HCI technology. Currently, technology is rapidly changing so this paper introduces a mouse that replaces the physical and Bluetooth mouses. The Bluetooth mouse needs a dongle that should be connected to a laptop or system and a battery is needed for power. By capturing hand movements, we can detect using computer vision, the proposed method can get over the limits by means of a webcam or integrated camera. It also decreases the contagious virus COVID-19 spread as there is no human interaction with the devices/computers.

Keywords: Face Recognition, Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), Hand gesture recognition, Hand tip detection, Virtual mouse.

## Introduction

A mouse is an important device used to perform all the operations in system/laptop. The screen shows the operations that are requested. There are various kinds of mouses such as mechanical mouse, optical mouse, and wireless mouse ([Shriram et al., 2021](#ch44.xhtml#ref44_13)). The movement of the rubber ball, which is the only component of the mechanical mouse and may rotate in any direction, controls the pointer movement. A mechanical mouse also be called as ball mouse. The rubber ball is located underside of mouse, the sensors inside it will detect the movement and send the signals to cursor displays on the screen. As the technology is changing the optical mouse replaced the mechanical mouse as it is more weighted and more costly ([Venkateshwar et al., 2021](#ch44.xhtml#ref44_10)). The optical mouse consists of an LED sensor and a small camera that will take thousands of pictures and detects the movement of the pointer. An optical mouse has a light, but a mechanical mouse has a rubber ball. The laser mouse was suggested after some time had elapsed to get over the optical mouse’s drawbacks. The development of technology has led to introducing wireless mouse for overcoming the limitations of mechanical, optical, laser mouses and for helping the persons having problem to operate the physical mouse ([Katona et al., 2021](#ch44.xhtml#ref44_4)). When there is no space to utilize a mouse in the actual world, the proposed contact free virtual controlling system can be employed to solve the problems ([Nandhini et al., 2014](#ch44.xhtml#ref44_12)). The computer vision-based, contact- free virtual controlling mouse system uses the SSD algorithm to detect hand gestures. The proposed system employs a transformational technique to translate the fingertip’s coordinates a full-screen computer monitor is used for mouse control after moving the camera there (Lugaresi et al., 2019). The proposed model outcome demonstrates good accuracy and excellent performance in using a CPU instead of a GPU for real-world applications.

## Related Work

Shriram discussed about a system that uses computer vision and deep learning to prevent the spread of COVID-19. The mouse is important to perform operations in system/laptop. The mouse uses Human Computer Interaction (HCI) technology to complete its work properly. It also decreases the contagious virus COVID-19 spread as there is no human interaction with the devices/ computers ([Shriram et al., 2021](#ch44.xhtml#ref44_13)). Devanshu Singh described Virtual Mouse using Open CV. It recommends that you rebuild your hardware. The idea is to show that can we use digital technology and a webcam for monitoring mouse movements (clicks and scrolls) and make all conventional mouse devices. This paper shows how to build a mouse operating system ([Singh et al., 2021](#ch44.xhtml#ref44_9)). Venkateshwar described the HCI’s use of a virtual mouse by identifying hand gestures. Since, the advancement of computer technology, HCI technology has developed continuously. Having additional devices in the mouse complicates the hardware. Recommended mouse systems are outside this limit (Venkateswar et al., 2021). The authors of “Virtual Mouse Control Using Colored Fingertips and Hand Gesture Recognition” ([Reddy et al., 2020](#ch44.xhtml#ref44_15)) described this technique. Using image- based fingertip recognition and hand motion tracking in real-time videos, a contact-free virtual mouse has been built for human and computer interaction. The control of a virtual mouse using hand motion recognition and fingertips detection is described in this work ([Pranav et al., 2020](#ch44.xhtml#ref44_11)). Manthan Bhatkar, Ofrin Lopes, Prof. Monali Shetty, and Christina Gtv. Daniel described about using an object tracking system as a virtual mouse. All devices today use touchscreen technology for their systems, and not all applications can use them. A virtual mouse that helps you interact using gestures and specialized interactive modules such as object tracking is a possible substitute for conventional screens ([Reddy et al., 2020](#ch44.xhtml#ref44_15)).

## Materials and Methods

In [Fig. 1](#ch44.xhtml#fig44_1), the proposed work’s entire development is shown. There are six steps in the procedure they are as follows:

![Fig. 1. Proposed workflow diagram.](images/fig44_1_B.jpg)

[Fig. 1. Proposed workflow diagram.](#ch44.xhtml#R_fig44_1)

### A. Workflow

1.  Step 1 Download and install the requirements in the system. Import the modules and libraries.
2.  Step 2 The algorithm usage should be known completely.
3.  Step 3 Testing contact-free virtually controlling system is very hard as the available datasets are limited. The faces for the access are added in dataset. The tests are performed under different conditions and distances using webcam/built-in camera for face recognition and hand movements ([Vinay et al., 2016](#ch44.xhtml#ref44_7)).
4.  Step 4 There are 0-20 co-ordinates or landmarks which makes hand tip detection easy and improves the accuracy in detecting hand gestures. The proposed model of the hand will contain 21 joint coordinates which mainly focus on fingertips ([Shriram et al., 2021](#ch44.xhtml#ref44_13)).
5.  Step 5 Firstly, the hand detection model is implemented and trained for detecting and tracking hand movements. In the next step, face biometrics is added as security for the virtual mouse.
6.  Step 6 The proposed model can perform various mouse functions. It is used to control system as a physical mouse but performs functions virtually.

### B. Select a framework for hand tracking

It is an opensource and cross-platform. It is mainly utilized for hand motion detection and tracking ([Singh et al., 2021](#ch44.xhtml#ref44_9)). The framework analyses and build the graphs of system by developer and for the sake of application develops the systems. It includes a few Machine-Learning (ML) pre-trained solutions, including face and object detection, pose estimation, hand and object recognition, and more.

### C. Capture frames using webcam

The virtual contact-free controlling system captures every frame of the video until the video is completed by using webcam in system/ computer or a built-in camera. To identify hand movements from frame to frame, BGR color is transformed to RGB. The face and hands movements are tracked by webcam and the mouse operation will be performed according to the movement (Christina et al., 2020; [Katona et al., 2021](#ch44.xhtml#ref44_4)). The hand movements are detected and according to that the mouse operations are performed.

### D. Detect the hand gestures, hand tips, and face recognition.

The faces are detected by generating a rectangular box around face and it also shows the name of person. The hand movements are detected and according to that the mouse operations are performed. The computer detects the movements of fingertips and performs functions ([Reddy et al., 2020](#ch44.xhtml#ref44_15)). A single-shot detector model is utilized to detect and identify hands and fingers in actual time. A landmark model of the hand is composed of the locations of 21 joints or knuckles in the hand region. The algorithm can determine the location of the face, which can be utilized to direct the motion of the virtual mouse. In order to accomplish this, the algorithm would first need to be trained to identify the user’s face before being used to authenticate the user before granting them access to the virtual mouse.

### Algorithm for SSD

*Step 1:* The foundation of SSD is a feature map based tiny convolutional filtering that predicts a particular set of default bounding boxes, there are category scores and box offsets ([Venkateshwar et al., 2021](#ch44.xhtml#ref44_10)).

*Step 2:* The explicit group predictions by aspect ratio and create predictions made at various scales using feature maps of various sizes to achieve excellent detection accuracy ([Venkateshwar et al., 2021](#ch44.xhtml#ref44_10)).

*Step* 3: Losses in localization (loc) and confidence (conf) are weighted sums that make up the function of the total objective loss:

  
$$L(x,c,l,g) = \\frac{1}{N}(L\_{conf}(x,c) + \\alpha L\_{loc}(x,l,g))$$

## Results

The web camera of a laptop or computer is used to capture images for the planned contact-free virtual controlling system. The webcam begins recording footage as soon as the computer vision library is used to identify the object in the video footage. A rectangular frame is generated when a hand is detected and the finger that should carry out a specific mouse function is identified and the area moves the mouse cursor through the window. To determine which finger is raised, this step uses the Id of the associated finger and the matching Id’s of the top finger:

### 4.1 To perform left click operation

When the thumb and index finger are both up and there is less than 30 pixels between them, the system is designed to click the left click operation when the two fingers are together. The system is designed to click the left click operation as illustrated in [Fig. 2](#ch44.xhtml#fig44_2)., whenever the thumb finger’s tip Id=0 and the index finger’s tip Id=1 are both up and there is less than 30px.

![Fig. 2. To Click the Left Button on the Mouse.](images/fig44_2_B.jpg)

[Fig. 2. To Click the Left Button on the Mouse.](#ch44.xhtml#R_fig44_2)

### 4.2 To use right click function

As shown in [Fig. 3](#ch44.xhtml#fig44_3), the system is designed to use the right-click button on the mouse when the middle finger has a tip Id of 2 and the index finger has a tip Id of 1, both of which line up, and there are fewer than 40 pixels total.

![Fig. 3. To Use the Right Button on the Mouse.](images/fig44_3_B.jpg)

[Fig. 3. To Use the Right Button on the Mouse.](#ch44.xhtml#R_fig44_3)

### 4.3 To execute a scroll-up action:

**If the middle finger has a tip Id of 2, and the index finger has tip Id of 1, and both fingers are up, the distance between them is higher than 40 pixels, and they move over the page.**

### 4.4 To execute a scroll-down action:

The two fingers are relocated to the bottom of the screen if the space between them is greater than 40 pixels if the middle finger has tip Id=2 and the index finger has tip **Id=1** are up. If the index finger is up and has tip Id = 1 or if both the index finger and middle finger have tip Id = 2 are up, as shown in [Fig. 4](#ch44.xhtml#fig44_4), the mouse cursor can be made to move around the computer window.

![Fig. 4. To scroll the computer display with the mouse cursor.](images/fig44_4_B.jpg)

[Fig. 4. To scroll the computer display with the mouse cursor.](#ch44.xhtml#R_fig44_4)

The system is designed to conduct the double click using a package, as illustrated in [Fig.5](#ch44.xhtml#fig44_5)., if the middle finger has tip Id = 2 and the index finger has tip Id = 1 are both up and there is no space between the two fingers. If the distance between the index finger’s tip (Id = 1) and the thumb’s tip (Id = 0) is less than 30px and both fingers are bent at an angle where all other fingers are up. As shown in [Fig. 6](#ch44.xhtml#fig44_6)., the computer is designed to perform sound operations using packages when the space between the other fingers is less than 10px. If all the fingers are closed and there is no distance between any two fingers, the computer is made to perform the drag and drop operations using packages, as shown in [Fig.7](#ch44.xhtml#fig44_7).

## Discussion

In the recent papers, as compared to the existing systems which have accuracy of 82%, 73%, 71%, 65%, 58% respectively ([Pranav et al., 2020](#ch44.xhtml#ref44_11)). The proposed system also contains extra features compared to existing systems like face recognition for authorized persons. Before, virtual mouse systems used You Only Look Once (YOLO) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) algorithms, but the newly proposed system is based on the Single Shot Detector (SSD) technique to increase performance and accuracy. The accuracy of facial recognition for authenticated users will increase with the creation of a custom dataset. The quality and quantity of training samples, the input images, the model parameters, and the accuracy threshold all affect how accurate an object detection model.

## Conclusion

The contact-free virtual controlling system is an idea for personalized multifunctional navigation/ interaction tools that break down physical barriers. The system is realistic enough that it does not significantly affect the interaction. Ease of use is improved accessibility, customization, features, and security. To lessen the growth of coronavirus and the conventional physical mouse, the proposed technology can be utilized virtually without palm motion. The right-click function in this model has a little loss of accuracy, and selecting text by clicking and dragging has problems. A virtual keyboard function can also be added to the suggested method so that it can be used in addition to a mouse function. This is yet another potential future application for **HCI.**

# Underwater Benthos Detection in Marine Benthic Zone Using Single Shot MultiBox Detector

A. Milan Hussain, Vikram Varma and D. Chitradevi[^(36)](#fn36)

Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Hindustan Institute of Technology and Science, Chennai, India

E-mail: [hussainmilan1@gmail.com](mailto:hussainmilan1@gmail.com), [vikram14202@gmail.com](mailto:vikram14202@gmail.com)

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-45](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-45)

## Abstract

The marine benthic zone refers to the bottom of a body of water, such as an ocean or lake, and includes all the organisms and physical features that are found there. Due to the maritime economy’s rapid growth, the demand for marine resources has increased dramatically in recent years. At present, target detection technology has several uses and future potential in ocean construction and benthic observation. However, the underwater environment is diverse and variable benthic organisms, existing systems may struggle to accurately detect and classify benthic species. This can lead to missed detections, false positives, and misclassifications, which can affect system’s accuracy. This paper addresses these issues for detecting and classifying benthic organisms in underwater images using the algorithm for single-shot multi box detection. The algorithm uses a single deep neural network to predict bounding boxes and class probabilities for objects in an image. The model has succeeded to get an accuracy 87.5% in detecting marine benthic organisms.

Keywords: Deep Learning, Convolutional Neural Networks, Segmentation, Fully Connected Layers, Pooling Layers.

## Introduction

In recent years, advances in technology have provided new opportunities for underwater benthos detection, such as acoustic and optical sensors, autonomous underwater vehicles, and machine learning algorithms. These technologies offer the potential for more efficient, accurate, and non-destructive methods for studying benthic organisms. The benthic zone, which is the bottom layer of an aquatic ecosystem, is a vital component of marine and freshwater environments ([Yang et al., 2020](#ch45.xhtml#ref45_1)). The benthic community comprises a diverse range of organisms, including plants, invertebrates, and microorganisms, thatplay critical roles in nutrient cycling, sediment stabilization, and the overall health of the ecosystem ([Kumari et al., 2019](#ch45.xhtml#ref45_7)). Hence, identifying and keeping track of benthic organisms is essential for determining the ecological health of aquatic ecosystems (Huang et.al, 2019). Yet, conventional benthic survey techniques like bottom trawling and visual inspection can be time-consuming, expensive, and harmful to the benthic ecosystem. This work explores a technique for employing Single Shot Multibox Detector to detect underwater benthic organisms in the marine benthic zone ([Bochkovskiy et al., 2020](#ch45.xhtml#ref45_6)). The proposed method involves using annotated underwater images of benthic organisms to train the model (Zhang et al., 2021). The model is then used to detect and classify benthic organisms. Nowadays, nonphysical model image enhancement and physical model- based picture restoration are the two main categories of underwater image improvement and restoration techniques ([Zhang et al., 2020](#ch45.xhtml#ref45_16)). This paper comprises 4 main phases. Phase 1 involves the acquisition of underwater images of the benthic environment. In phase 2, the images are pre-processed. Image preprocessing is an essential phase in underwater benthos detection as it helps to improve the standard and suitability of the dataset for analysis ([Zhang et al., 2020](#ch45.xhtml#ref45_16)). In phase 3, The SSD model is trained to recognize objects using the annotated images ([Bochkovskiy et al., 2020](#ch45.xhtml#ref45_6)). The training process involves adjusting the model’s weights and parameters to optimize its performance. Phase 4 involves the process of detection of benthos organisms. Once the model is trained, it can be used to detect and classify benthic organisms like Sea Urchins, Starfish, Crabs, and Corals.

## Related Works

Models with Deep learning are more effective in detecting the capacity to work with a larger amount of data concurrently and the ability to extract information from photos in challenging circumstances. Tian Zhou et al. described “Automated Small Targets Underwater Detection using Forward-Looking Sonar Images.” One of the fundamental imaging tools used to explore underwater targets is forward-looking sonar. This article proposes a clustering, segmentation, and feature discrimination-based autonomous underwater target identification technique. The experimental findings demonstrate that the suggested low detection inaccuracy and good real-time performance with low false alarm likelihood are characteristics of the technique, which is comparable to current mainstream deep learning algorithms ([Zhou et al., 2022](#ch45.xhtml#ref45_14)). [Yeh et al. (2022](#ch45.xhtml#ref45_8)) in “Lightweight Deep Neural Network for Concurrent Learning of Color Conversion and Underwater Item Identification” described that it has been shown that there is great potential for underwater image processing in the research of underwater ecosystems. A deep model must be supplied in order to successfully learn color conversion and object detection for underwater photographs. The experimental outcomes showed with our implementation on the Raspberry Pi platform ([Yeh et al., 2022](#ch45.xhtml#ref45_8)). Jia Liu et.al explained in — “Swin Transformer- Based Two-Stage Underwater Object Detection Network” that Ocean exploration relies heavily on underwater object detection, and research into effective underwater object recognition algorithms is crucial for use in real-world applications due to the increasing number of underwater object image data. In order to resolve these problems, a Faster R-CNN-based. The proposed algorithm is enhanced to 80.54% when compared to other algorithms since it is based on improved Faster- RCNN using the URPC2018 dataset. ([Liu et al., 2022](#ch45.xhtml#ref45_11)). Athira. P et.al (2021) described “Deep neural networks-based Underwater object recognition model based on the YOLOv3 architecture” a deep learning model that uses YOLOv3 architecture, the darknet framework, and automatic underwater object detection. Also, this study investigates the potential for tailoring YOLOv3-based aquatic object detection algorithms using the dataset ([Athira et al., 2021](#ch45.xhtml#ref45_5)). [Huang et al. (2019](#ch45.xhtml#ref45_10)) described — “Convolutional Neural Network-Based Object Detection in the Water” and suggested a multi-scale convolution neural network-based underwater multi-target identification technique (MSC-CNN). The evaluation parameters used include accuracy and test time, and the recognition performance of several underwater picture recognition techniques is examined by comparison with leading algorithms. The results of underwater image experiments demonstrate the benefits of this strategy for many evaluation measures ([Huang et al., 2019](#ch45.xhtml#ref45_10)).

## Materials and Methods

The proposed method for underwater benthos detection using SSD is a promising approach that can automate the discovery and investigation of benthic ecosystems in marine environments. The project aims to create a system for detecting species in the benthic zone, the lowest region of the ocean floor which is often difficult to study due to limited visibility. The detection of underwater benthos in marine benthic zones can be achieved using the Single Shot Multi-box Detector algorithm, which is a popular object recognition algorithm. The following steps can be followed for underwater benthos detection using the SSD algorithm:

 ![Fig. 1. Proposed workflow diagram](images/fig45_1_B.jpg)

Fig. 1. Proposed workflow diagram

### Workflow:

1.  Step 1 Download and install the requirements in the system. Import the modules and libraries.
2.  Step 2 The second step determines the study area and depth range. We choose Marine Benthic zone as our area of interest that we want to study and determine the depth range that we will be exploring.
3.  Step 3 Collect underwater image dataset. Ensure that the data set at a high enough resolution and frame rate for accurate detection.
4.  Step 4 The data is Pre-processed and cleaned by removing any unwanted frames.
5.  Step 5 Training the SSD algorithm using a dataset of annotated images of the benthos species that we are going to detect.
6.  Step 6 Applying the trained SSD algorithm to the pre-processed image data to detect and localize the benthos species.
7.  Step 7 The results are post-processed to remove false positives and track the movement of detected benthos species.
8.  Step 8 Optimization and Tuning step involves optimizing and tuning the hyperparameters, such as learning rate, batch size, optimizer, etc., until the desired accuracy is achieved.

Underwater benthos detection using Single Shot Detector (SSD) is a module designed for automated detection and recognition of benthic organisms in underwater images. Data collection is the first step in the module where input images of underwater benthos are collected and the unnecessary images are removed. Data Preprocessing and Annotation is the second step where the images with bounding boxes around each benthic object and labeling with their respective species. We used the CLAHE enhancement method in this blog to improve image quality in a real-time system. CLAHE method helps in improving visibility and it preserves local details. The next step is to select an appropriate machine-learning algorithm for Underwater Benthos Detection. The proposed method uses SSD algorithm for underwater benthos detection. The algorithm uses a single deep neural network to predict bounding boxes and class probabilities for objects in an image. The Single Shot Detector uses a multi-box to identify several items in a single shot. It is a high-accuracy object-detecting technique is substantially faster. The SSD model is a trained annotated dataset that has been pre-processed using CLAHE method. The SSD model takes an input image and outputs a set of predicted bounding boxes and their corresponding class probabilities. The performance of the SSD model is evaluated using standard metrics such as precision, recall, and F1 score. This helps to assess the accuracy of the model in detecting benthos in marine benthic zones.

### Algorithm for SSD:

1.  **Step 1 :** The foundation of SSD is a feature map based tiny convolutional filtering that predicts a particular set of default bounding boxes, there are category scores and box offsets.
2.  **Step 2** : The explicit group predictions by aspect ratio and create predictions made at various scales using feature maps of various sizes in order to achieve excellent detection accuracy.
3.  **Step 3 :** Losses in localization (loc) and confidence (conf) are weighted sums that make up the function of the total Objective loss:
    
      
    $$L(x,c,l,g) = \\frac{1}{N}(L\_{conf}(x,c) + \\alpha L\_{loc}(x,l,g))$$  
    
4.  Step 4 We go backwards to the default bounding box’s offsets parameters in a manner similar to Faster R-CNN.
5.  Step 5 center (cx, cy), as well as for its width (w), and
    
    height (h).
    
      
    $$\\begin{array}{l} {L\_{loc}(x,l,g) = \\sum\\limits\_{i \\in Pos}^{N}\\sum\\limits\_{m \\in \\{ cx,cy,w,h\\}}x\_{ij}^{k}smooth\_{\\text{L}1}(l\_{i}^{m} - {\\hat{g}}\_{j}^{m})} \\\\ \\begin{array}{ll} {{\\hat{g}}\_{j}^{cx} = (g\_{j}^{cx} - d\_{i}^{cx})/d\_{i}^{w}} & {{\\hat{g}}\_{j}^{cy} = (g\_{j}^{cy} - d\_{i}^{cy})/d\_{i}^{h}} \\\\ {{\\hat{g}}\_{j}^{w} = \\log(\\frac{g\_{j}^{w}}{d\_{i}^{w}})} & {{\\hat{g}}\_{j}^{h} = \\log(\\frac{g\_{j}^{h}}{d\_{i}^{h}})} \\\\ \\end{array} \\\\ {L\_{conf}(x,c) = - \\sum\\limits\_{i \\in Pos}^{N}x\_{ij}^{p}\\log({\\hat{c}}\_{i}^{p}) - \\sum\\limits\_{i \\in Neg}\\log({\\hat{c}}\_{i}^{0})} \\\\ {where\\,\\,{\\hat{c}}\_{i}^{p} = \\frac{\\exp(c\_{i}^{p})}{\\sum\_{p}\\exp(c\_{i}^{p})}} \\\\ \\end{array}$$  
    

### Performance Metrics

Precision = (Number of True Positives)/ (Number of True Positives + Number of False Positives).

The ratio of actual (relevant) objects to genuine positives is known as recall.

Recall = (Number of True Positives)/ (Number of True Positives + Number of False Negatives).

There is a value range of 0 to 1, with 1 denoting the maximum accuracy.

Fl score = (Precision x Recall)/ (Precision + Recall)/2.

## Discussions

The results of these studies imply that SSD has the potential to be a useful method for finding underwater benthos. In comparison to conventional sample techniques, SSD can save time and resources by automating the identification and counting of benthic species. Moreover, SSD can deliver data that is more precise and consistent than manual sampling techniques, which are subject to bias and human error. The use of SSD algorithm for underwater benthos detection shows promise and is an area of active research. SSD and other computer vision techniques are anticipated to play a more and bigger role in understanding and monitoring the health and ecology of aquatic ecosystems as technology and algorithms continue to advance. The accuracy of an object detection model depends on a number of factors, including the input photos, model parameters, and accuracy threshold ([Kumari et al., 2019](#ch45.xhtml#ref45_7)). A ratio can be used as a threshold to determine whether a certain transaction is a true positive or a false positive using the Intersection over Union (IoU) method ([Dixit et al., 2019](#ch45.xhtml#ref45_12)). The IoU ratio quantifies the degree to which the bounding box of a projected item overlaps the bounding box containing the ground reference data. The proportion of real positives to all forecasted positive outcomes is known as precision.

## Conclusion

In conclusion, Underwater Benthos Detection in the benthic zone is a significant area of research with numerous applications in marine biology, ecology, and conservation. Techniques like the SSD algorithm are used in this process. Researchers can better understand the distribution, abundance of benthic creatures by precisely detecting and localizing them. The utilization of marine resources sustainably can be supported by this knowledge as well as management and conservation activities. Yet, finding underwater benthos is a difficult undertaking that calls for specific tools and knowledge of picture processing and analysis. As a result, furthering our understanding of the benthic zone and its inhabitants will depend on ongoing research and development in this area.

# Digital Human Creator Using Facial Expression and Voice

Medagam Siva Vamsidhar Reddy, Tanikanti Venkat Kiran, D. Chitradevi[^(37)](#fn37)

Department of Computer Science Engineering, Hindustan Institute of Technology and Science, Chennai, India

E-mail: [m.s.vamsidhar678@gmail.com](mailto:m.s.vamsidhar678@gmail.com), [Tanikantikiran@gmail.com](mailto:Tanikantikiran@gmail.com)

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-46](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-46)

## Abstract

The Digital Character Creator is a state-of-the-art system that allows users to generate and animate virtual characters using facial expressions and voice commands. Manually creating a digital character takes more time and human effort. The software can reliably recognize and understand these inputs by employing powerful machine learning techniques, resulting in distinct characters with a spectrum of emotions and personalities. The system is intended to be simple and easy to use, with a number of tools and interfaces that allow users to create original characters from scratch or build on pre-existing templates. With real-time manipulation capabilities, Overall, the Digital Character Creator is a powerful and innovative tool that has the potential to transform the way characters are generated and animated. Its advanced features and accessibility make it an essential resource for artists and animators seeking to bring their creative visions to life. the Digital Character Creator is ideal for use in creative industries such as film and gaming.

Keywords: Digital Character Creator, Facial expressions, Voice commands, Animation, Machine learning

## Introduction

Deep learning plays a significant role in the advancement of computer vision by improving the speed and accuracy of assigned tasks. It is opening opportunities for improvement and enhancement of processes and initiating human- driven tasks in an automated manner. Digital character creation has become a significant area of research in computer graphics and animation. The creation of digital characters that can express emotions and exhibit personality traits has many applications in fields such as film, video games, virtual reality, and social media. One of the most challenging aspects of digital character creation is animating the characters’ facial expressions and voices (Hongcheng [Wang and Ahuja, 2003](#ch46.xhtml#ref46_6)). Facial expression and voice recognition technology have been used to create digital characters that can mimic human emotions and speech patterns ([Hong et al., July 2002](#ch46.xhtml#ref46_9)). These technologies use machine learning algorithms to recognize and analyze facial expressions and audio input. The output is then used to generate corresponding facial animations and speech output (Andre Teixeira [Lopes et al., 2017](#ch46.xhtml#ref46_1)). One of the commonly used approaches for facial animation is facial animation parameter generation. This involves mapping facial movements to a set of animation parameters that can be used to control the animation of a virtual character’s face (Zoric, 2003). Motion capture data is used to generate realistic and natural- looking facial expressions and movements. Automated rigging and facial animation systems are also being developed ([Testa et al., 2021](#ch46.xhtml#ref46_12)). These systems incorporate machine learning algorithms that can generate facial animations in real time from speech or other input. The systems enable the creation of virtual characters with automated facial animation capabilities, making it easier for artists to create believable and natural-looking facial expressions and lip-syncing ([Sadoughi and Busso, 2021](#ch46.xhtml#ref46_8), [Kim et al., 2021](#ch46.xhtml#ref46_14)). Digital character creation using facial expression and voice technology has the potential to revolutionize many industries. It has many applications in healthcare, education, communication, and entertainment. As these technologies continue to evolve, we can expect to see the emergence of more realistic and human-like virtual characters. Another approach is real-time facial animation, which allows virtual characters to display facial expressions in real time as the user interacts with them (Spiros [Ioannou et al., 2005](#ch46.xhtml#ref46_11)). This is accomplished through the use of motion capture data or by developing machine learning models that can generate facial animations in real- time from speech or other input ([Vougioukas et al., 2020](#ch46.xhtml#ref46_13)). Several systems have been developed that combine facial expression and voice recognition to create more realistic and expressive virtual characters. These systems typically incorporate machine learning algorithms that analyze speech and facial expressions to generate corresponding facial animations and lip-syncing (Fu Jie Huang and Tsuhan Chen, 1998). Developing digital character creation systems that incorporate facial expression and voice recognition can be a complex and challenging task to the above literature. Accuracy of the digital character, facial expression, and voice recognition will be increased by using tools. Face animation may be utilized to produce more realistic and engaging educational and training simulations, such as medical simulations or public speaking simulations. design more natural and intuitive assistive technology interfaces.

## Related Work

Despite the success of traditional shallow features and generic image descriptors, recent development in convolutional neural networks (CNNs) has demonstrated ed-significant success of automatically learned features ([Hill et al., 1988](#ch46.xhtml#ref46_5)). Other studies have explored the use of motion capture data to create realistic facial animations. Several systems have been developed that allow for the creation of virtual characters with automated rigging and facial animation capabilities. These systems incorporate machine learning algorithms to generate realistic and natural-looking facial expressions and lip-syncing (Huang and Chen, 1998). Other studies have explored the use of facial expressions and voice recognition to create more realistic and expressive virtual characters. Speech-Driven Automatic Facial Expression Synthesis, M. Ozkan, and A. M. Tekalp proposed an approach to voice- controlled facial animation for virtual characters. The system uses machine learning algorithms to analyze speech input and generate corresponding facial animations ([Bozkurt et al., 2008](#ch46.xhtml#ref46_2)). Deep Facial Expression Recognition (DFER) is a type of machine learning technique that focuses on automatically recognizing emotions expressed by a person’s face in real time. DFER involves using deep neural networks, which are a type of artificial intelligence model, to analyze facial images and extract features that are indicative of specific emotions such as happiness, sadness, anger, or surprise (Li and Deng, 2002). Facial expression recognition from images is the task of identifying the emotional state of a person from an image of their face. It has applications in various fields such as psychology, human- computer interaction, and security ([Wang et al., 2019](#ch46.xhtml#ref46_4)). Automatic analysis of facial expressions refers to the process of using machine learning algorithms and computer vision techniques to automatically recognize and interpret facial expressions in images or videos. This technology has applications in various fields such as psychology, human-computer interaction, and security ([Pantic and Rothkrantz, 2000](#ch46.xhtml#ref46_7)).

## Methodology

Our proposed method for creating digital characters using facial expressions and voice consists of the following steps:

***Step* 1**: Go to the Reallusion website download and install the I clone 8 and Character Creator 4, headshot plugin, and live link plugin. (We need iPhone to capture facial data with help of live mocap it will be available in App Store.)

***Step 2:*** Collect a dataset of facial expressions and voice samples from real actors. This data contains a wide range of emotions and expressions that the character will need to

*Step* 3: The obtained data must be processed to reduce noise and match the facial expression and speech samples. To extract features from processed data, we employ plugins that operate with deep learning approaches such as convolutional neural networks.

***Step 4:*** Integrate the trained model with the digital character to enable it to express emotions and communicate with the users through facial expressions and voice.

***Step 5:*** Evaluate the performance of the system using metrics such as animation quality, computational efficiency, and user satisfaction.

***Step 6:*** Refine the system based on the evaluation results and repeat the evaluation process until satisfactory results are achieved.

iClone 8 is a powerful **3D** animation software that allows users to create and animate virtual characters, environments, and objects. It offers a variety of tools and features to create high-quality animations, including motion capture, facial animation, physics simulation, and more. Character Creator 4 is a companion software to iClone 8 that specializes in character creation. It provides a suite of tools and features to create and customize **3D** characters, including facial and body morphs, clothing and accessories, and textures. Live Motion Plugin is a plugin for iClone 8 that provides motion capture capabilities. It allows users to capture live motion data and apply it to their **3D** characters in real time, creating realistic animations with minimal effort

## Discussion

Face animation parameterization methods involve mapping facial movements to a set of animation parameters that can be used to control virtual character facial animations. This approach has proven to achieve the most advanced results in terms of animation quality and computational efficiency. However, this requires a large dataset of facial expressions and can be difficult to implement in real-time systems. The real-time face animation approach allows virtual characters to display facial expressions in real-time as the user interacts with them. These systems have been shown to generate realistic facial animations from voice input and have potential applications in areas such as entertainment and education. Systems that combine facial expressions and speech recognition are capable of creating more realistic and expressive virtual characters. These systems use machine learning algorithms to recognize and analyze voice input, and animate faces and lip-sync accordingly. They have been proven to produce realistic facial animations and lip-sync from voice or video input.

## Conclusion

The article describes the technical aspects of the Digital Character Generator, including the algorithms and techniques used to interpret facial expressions and voice commands. It also provides examples on how to create and animate virtual characters using this technology. This article argues that digital character generators using expressions and voices represent a new frontier in character animation, providing a powerful and creative tool for artists and creators. It has the potential to revolutionize the way characters are created and animated, providing a more intuitive, accessible, and flexible approach to character animation. The document suggests that the technology is an essential resource for anyone looking to create engaging and dynamic virtual characters. These characters can be used in using facial animation, allowing filmmakers to create more lifelike and emotionally engaging characters.

# Enhancing the Security of Electronic Health Records Using Consortium Blockchain

G. Suman, C. H. Maruthi and S. Revathy

Department of Computer Science Engineering, Hindustan Institute of Technology and Science, Chennai, India

E-mail ID: [sumangadde54@gmail.com](mailto:sumangadde54@gmail.com), [maruthich432@gmail.com](mailto:maruthich432@gmail.com), [srevathy@hindustanuniv.ac.in](mailto:srevathy@hindustanuniv.ac.in)

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-47](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-47)

## Abstract

Security of electronic records (EHRs) is of foremost significance in the medical services industry, given the delicate idea of patient information. The existing restrictions on the use of private and public blockchains in healthcare include issues of scalability, data transmission latency restricting interactions between the different systems. By providing a tamper-proof, decentralized, and permission environment for storing and sharing patient data, consortium blockchain can improve the security of electronic health records (EHRs) by overcoming the drawbacks of private and public blockchains. The consortium blockchain is the combination of private and public blockchain, where it converges the advantages of both the blockchain. The proposed model restricts data sharing and transmission among patients and doctors by the validation of their roles using smart contracts. It increases transparency and security as the health records are managed by both the patients and doctors.

Keywords: Consortium blockchain, EHR, Security, Smart contracts

## Introduction

Electronic health records (EHRs) contain private and sensitive patient data, their security is of the utmost importance to the healthcare sector. The term “blockchain” refers to a distributed ledger that keeps permanent records of all networked transactions. Protecting a patient’s health record from adversary attackers is crucial. The ability to store patients’ health records in a decentralized ledger is made possible by the blockchain, which enables medical professionals to gain a better understanding of the patient’s medical history.

Consortium blockchain’s potential to improve EHR security is provided. The difficulties of implementing blockchain in healthcare, the modules of a consortium blockchain system for EHRs, and related works in the field are discussed. Additionally, the advantages of using consortium blockchain include reduced expenses, enhanced data privacy, improved patient outcomes, and more efficient data sharing. There are drawbacks to using blockchain, including issues with scalability, data transmission latency, interactions between various systems, and concerns about data security and confidentiality.

Consensus blockchain provides a private and secure environment for storing sensitive health data, enhancing data privacy. Patient care is improved and costs associated with duplicate tests and procedures are decreased when healthcare providers share data effectively. Costs can be cut, errors can be reduced, and middlemen can be eliminated by automating processes. the implementation of consortium blockchain and its potential benefits, which have the potential to significantly enhance the security and efficiency of electronic health records.

Stages involved in the processing of health records using blockchain are:

1.  ***Patient registration and identity management*** Patients can register and create an identity on the blockchain network using this module, which stores personal information like name, date of birth, contact information, and medical history.
2.  ***Electronic health record creation:*** The secure and tamper-proof creation and storage of electronic health records (EHRs) on the blockchain network, ensuring that authorized healthcare providers have access to accurate, complete patient health data.
3.  ***Access control and authentication:*** In order to guarantee the confidentiality and integrity of health data, this module is used to authenticate users and control access to health records
4.  ***Data sharing and interoperability:*** ensures interoperability between various blockchain networks by sharing health data among various healthcare providers and systems.
5.  ***Data analytics and reporting:*** To support clinical decision-making, research, and quality improvement, analyze health data and produce reports.
6.  ***Smart contracts:*** A smart contract is a transaction protocol or computer program designed to automatically execute, control, or record events and actions as specified in a contract or agreement.

### Challenges in the Security of Health Records in Blockchain

The key challenges in securing health records using consortium blockchains are

1.  ***Interoperability:*** Standardization and compatibility between various blockchain networks are required to ensure seamless data exchange in order to overcome the difficulty of interoperability when securing health records using a consortium blockchain
2.  **Scalability:** Due to the requirement of a robust infrastructure that is able to support the growth of the blockchain and handle a high volume of transactions, securing health records
3.  **Security:** attacks such as 51% attacks, double-spending attacks, and other forms of malicious activity. Robust security measures such as strong authentication, access controls, and encryption must be implemented to prevent unauthorized access to health data

### Consortium blockchain technology

Compared to a public blockchain & private blockchain network, a consortium blockchain is more secure, scalable, and effective. Like mixed and private blockchains, it has access restrictions.

The structure of the paper is as follows: Section 2, various use cases of blockchain technology are discussed, and in Section 3, the related work on security enhancement of blockchain technology in electronic health records is covered. Section 4 illustrates the existing system of EHR detection. The proposed work on blockchain technology based on security enhancement of electronic health records using consortium blockchain is presented in Section, and the conclusion is presented in Section 5.

## Use Case of Blockchain Technology

***Secure sharing of data:*** Secure data sharing between various healthcare providers can be made possible by blockchain-based **EHR** systems, allowing for improved collaboration and care coordination.

***Data control by the patient:*** Blockchain-based EHR systems give patients more control over their health data because they can grant or deny access to their data as needed.

***Enhanced data precision:*** Blockchain-based EHR frameworks can guarantee information precision by carrying out information approval and confirmation components, which can diminish mistakes and irregularities in well-being information.

***Clinical research and trials:*** EHRs based on the blockchain can make it easier to share health data for clinical trials and research by protecting privacy and confidentiality.

## Related work

Blockchain technology has been used in education, agribusiness, and healthcare, according to the literature review (Almery et al., 2019). Identified the potential of blockchain in enhancing the transparency and security of educational data through a systematic review of blockchain- based applications in education ([Rocha et al., 2021](#ch47.xhtml#ref47_2)). Proposed a blockchain-based electronic health record system that aims to enhance the trustworthiness of healthcare data and improve patient outcomes. The authors of Mahmoud et al. (2019) conducted a systematic review of blockchain technology in healthcare and identified the potential of blockchain in enhancing data privacy, security, and interoperability of healthcare data. [Reegu et al. (2021](#ch47.xhtml#ref47_4)) conducted a systematic review of blockchain applications in agribusiness and highlighted the potential of blockchain in enhancing supply chain management and traceability of agricultural products. [Makridakis and Christodoulou (2019](#ch47.xhtml#ref47_5)) highlighted the potential of blockchain in enhancing trust, transparency, and security in a variety of domains. [Alex et al. (2022](#ch47.xhtml#ref47_6)) highlighted the need for effective security and privacy mechanisms to ensure the trustworthiness of blockchain-based systems and discussed the security and privacy challenges in blockchain applications.

According to the review of the available literature, blockchain technology can enhance education, agribusiness, and healthcare’s transparency, security, and trustworthiness. However, in order to ensure the successful implementation of blockchain-based systems, scalability, interoperability, and regulatory compliance must also be addressed.

The data in previously used systems is unstructured, making data exchange challenging. Therefore, we intend to implement the provided model for managing health records in blockchain using Medicare in order to resolve the aforementioned issues. The medical industry is being transformed by blockchain-based EHR.

To build trust in the medical industry, it addresses the majority of the issues that arise today. It not only provides a fast and empowering system but also a dependable platform for the exchange of patient data. Utilizing an electronic health record (EHR) can significantly reduce the amount of time and effort required to manage patient data and produce results that are both effective and efficient.

## Proposed Security Enhancement of Elec- tronic Health Records Using Consortium Block Chain

The doctors and patients should register the patient management system with a unique identifying address. After registering a patient can find a doctor and book an appointment. The doctor can request access to the patient’s electronic health record after registering with the system. The doctor can look at the patient’s records if the patient agrees to share their EHR information and the same applies to patients to view doctor information. Once the transaction request is validated, the block will be added to chain.

The working of proposed consortium blockchain technology has been illustrated in [Fig. 2](#ch47.xhtml#fig47_2).

![Fig. 2. Patient management system using Consortium blockchain](images/fig47_2_B.jpg)

[Fig. 2. Patient management system using Consortium blockchain](#ch47.xhtml#R_fig47_2)

1.  Establishing a blockchain consortium network is created by a number of healthcare providers and stakeholders involved in the management of electronic health records.
2.  Patient identification and registration on the blockchain network, patients’ identities are protected through encryption, digital signatures, and two- factor authentication.
3.  Electronic health records creation when creating and storing electronic health records on the blockchain network, data integrity and confidentiality are guaranteed by access controls and encryption.
4.  Access control and authentication clients are verified with advanced marks and two- factor validation to forestall unapproved admittance to wellbeing records, which are controlled by both the patients and doctors.
5.  Data sharing and interoperability by sharing health data among various healthcare providers and systems, standardization, and compatibility measures guarantee interoperability between various blockchain networks.

## Conclusion

The private blockchain has more restrictions as only the owners of able to manage the data- sharing privileges. The public blockchain is vulnerable to threats as all can participate in the network. To a tamper-proof, decentralized, and permission environment for storing and sharing patient data, consortium blockchain is the best solution as it improves the security of electronic health records (EHRs) with fewer restrictions and more security. The proposed EHR management using consortium blockchain leverage the existing restrictions and vulnerabilities of private and public blockchains by converging the advantages of both blockchains. It increases transparency and security as the health records are effectively managed by both the patients and doctors. In the future, the work will be extended by integrating the blockchain with machine learning to identify anomalies in the healthcare network.

# Deep Learning Model for Segmentation of Brain Tumor in MRI Images

Kamani Praveena, Mopati Gowtham Reddy and S. Sathya Priya[^(38)](#fn38)

Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Hindustan Institute of Technology and Science, Chennai, India

E-mail: [praveena.kamani@gmail.com](mailto:praveena.kamani@gmail.com), [mopatigowthamreddy@gmail.com](mailto:mopatigowthamreddy@gmail.com)

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-48](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-48)

## Abstract

Segmenting brain tumors manually from the numerous magnetic resonance imaging **(MRI)** images generated in cancer diagnosis labs is a challenging and intensive undertaking. Segmenting a brain tumor is a necessary step in the processing of a medical image. Early diagnosis of the brain tumor improves the chances for successful treatment and improves the survival rates. The proposed method is divided into three categories: MRI image preprocessing, data augmentation, and segmentation. The models like UNet, AlexNet, and LeNet don’t include data augmentation, so the accuracy of the model is reduced. So in the proposed system, the three data augmentation techniques Cropping, Rotation, and Shifting are included to the CNN and ResNet models to improve the accuracy. An adaptive filter is used during the image pre-processing stage to get rid of the noise in the MRI picture. In order to visualize the presence of tumor in brain, image segmentation is utilized. Also utilized a deep learning model to categorize different sorts of pictures. Hence, the segmentation of brain images for tumor identification becomes necessary. CNN and ResNet models were used to create picture segmentation in an effort to solve current issues, and utilizing data augmentation, the model’s accuracy was improved. The proposed CNN method is compared with the ResNet model.

Keywords: Deep Learning, Convolutional Neural Networks, Segmentation, Fully Connected Layers, Pooling Layers, and Activation Function

## Introduction

To train and optimize complicated models, deep learning needs a lot of data and processing capacity. Additionally, it necessitates careful adjustment of the hyperparameters and critical thought on the moral implications of using the models. Deep learning is still an active area of research and development as a result, with lots of room for growth and use. An aberrant cell or tissue growth in the brain can cause the formation of a brain tumor. Currently, neither the particular causes of brain tumors nor their symptoms are known. Hence brain tumors may be present in persons who are unaware of how serious their condition is. To preserve the patient’s life, early tumor detection and removal are essential. For early detection, the **MRI** is a crucial tool. However, analyzing an MRI image requires expertise, time, and effort. Furthermore, manually detecting tumors is extremely difficult, and depending on the level of knowledge, the results can vary from clinical expert to clinical expert. In many clinical applications, MM is an essential step, as it impacts the overall outcome of the examination. Precise segmentation of anatomical regions is necessary for various processing steps, including surgical planning, image-guided interventions, lesion delineation, and measuring and visualizing different brain regions, among others that rely on it. Due to the wide range of image processing applications, numerous segmentation algorithms have been created, each with varying degrees of complexity and precision. A brain tumor is one of the most deadly conditions that individuals today might have.

Typically, tumors are visible all across the brain. Less cancers in the brain may make it more challenging to identify them by image processing methods or manually segmenting images, which may have an impact on how the body operates. Finding dangerous tumors in diverse body parts and treating them in a timely manner are difficult tasks. The signs of these tumors didn’t appear for a very long time before they posed a major threat to human life. Personality changes, memory loss, hearing or speech difficulties, frequent headaches, vision loss, and memory loss can all be brought on by brain disorders. Semantic segmentation, object detection, and image categorization are just a few of the computer vision problems that deep learning techniques have shown promise in solving. Brain tumors have been divided using a variety of deep learning-based algorithms, with positive results. The primary goal of this approach is to distinguish malignancies from healthy brain tissue. Here, deep learning-based MRI image segmentation of brain cancers saves millions of lives through early diagnosis. Magnetic resonance imaging (MM) can improve patient survival by finding brain malignancies earlier. Brain tumor predictions made using the CNN model on MRI scans can help patients receive therapies much more quickly and accurately. Existing systems like Unet, LeNet, AlexNet, and ZfNet, which take a lot of time to analyze images, do not incorporate data decompression.

The results are accurate since data enrichment enhances the image quality. Not only is the classification of tumor types the primary driver but also the identification of brain cancers. Also, it supports clinical practice and offers helpful information for planning a diagnosis and a course of therapy. The following graphic represents the paper: The Literature review is thoroughly explained in Section 2. The Methods and Implementation are detailed in Section 3. The paper concludes with Section 4, the last section.

## Related Work

A system where a deep learning model is utilized model to categorize different sorts of pictures, including meningiomas, pituitary tumors, non- tumors, and gliomas, by identifying characteristics in MRI scans ([Vankdothu and Hameed, 2022](#ch48.xhtml#ref48_1)) to increase the precision of tumor identification, an efficient automated system must be put in place. Medical image processing experts have acknowledged the complexity and difficulty of brain picture segmentation.

A system was proposed where brain cancers can be found and diagnosed using MM ([Agrawal et al., 2022](#ch48.xhtml#ref48_2)) Yet, in real practice, only the time and expertise of medical experts can manually identify brain cancers from a huge number of MRI pictures. These studies’ MRI scans are volumetrically segmented using the 3D- UNet model, and then the tumor is identified using CNNs. Despite their high computational costs, 3D DNNs have a huge potential for several medicinal applications. The size of these medical picture volumes can be greatly decreased by using interpolation techniques.

In this system, many computer science disciplines, including computer vision, picture classification, object recognition, image segmentation, and others, have demonstrated the effectiveness of deep learning ([Loey et al., 2021](#ch48.xhtml#ref48_6)). The deep learning picture data augmentation is demonstrated. The most recent advances in using picture data augmentation approaches in various deep learning research and applications will be surveyed ([Loey et al., 2021](#ch48.xhtml#ref48_6)).

The model is formed by two parts. The ResNet-50 deep transfer learning model’s feature extraction technique is implemented in the first section. A single dataset made up of two medical face mask datasets will be used in this study. The optimal number of anchor boxes has been determined using Mean IoU to improve the object-detecting procedure. According to the results, the Adam optimizer, which served as a detector, had the highest average precision percentage (81% ) (Aheli Saha et al., 2019).

The authors proposed a novel multi-pathway UNet to divide multimodal magnetic resonance imaging into the glioma sub-regions. Also suggested a common encoder is used, then distinct decoders are used for each category in place of a cascaded design for the hierarchical areas. The model’s use of residual connections makes it easier to improve performance (Shehab and Zhang, 2021). In order to overcome the gradient problem of DNN, the authors provide an automatic method for segmenting brain tumors that relies on Deep Residual Learning Network (ResNet). ResNets are more accurate than their counterpart DNNs and can speed up the training process. To achieve this gain. Parallel to the convolutional neural network layers, ResNets also have a short-cut skip connection.

It is often used in computer vision applications, such as image recognition, where the number of available training examples is limited.

## Conclusion

The categorization of brain tumors was separated into four categories Glioma, Meningioma, no tumor, and Pituitary tumors. The most current data augmentation techniques for segmenting brain tumors from an MRI are analyzed and the data augmentation tactics utilized in these approaches are explored. According to the findings, adding additional data improves the prediction potential of the model. Lastly, similar approaches may be easily applied to both single-modal and multi- modal scans, generally by generating bogus instances specifically for each visual modality. The suggested technique’s performance was evaluated on the Kaggle dataset utilizing the Keras and Tensorflow Python tools with testing and training data. Cropping, Rotation, and Shifting are also included as Data Augmentation techniques for the CNN and ResNet models, and the two models were compared to existing models that performed better. Utilizing MR images, the proposed method correctly diagnosed the tumors 91% of the time. Further Augmentation techniques, including flipping and shearing, might be used in the future to increase the accuracy of the suggested system.

# Embedding Intelligence on Edge Computing for the Classification of IoT Data Using Machine Learning with Deep Autoencoder

S. Sujiritha and Linda Joseph

Department of Computer Science, Hindustan Institute of Technology and Science, Chennai, India

E-mail: [sujiritha.s11@gmail.com](mailto:sujiritha.s11@gmail.com), [linda24in@gmail.com](mailto:linda24in@gmail.com)

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-49](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-49)

## Abstract

There is a demand for a centralized system or cloud storage due to the massive amount of data produced by numerous IoT devices. But there is a possibility of network traffic or data packet loss. In order to prevent this, Edge Computing is introduced. Keeping the edge device close to the source helps perform computation much easier. By embedding intelligence on the edge, less data will be sent to the cloud, allowing it to keep only the data that is necessary. Since edge computing has limitations on computational capacity, the proposed framework, Machine learning with Deep Autoencoder is a lightweight approach. This approach divides the data into normal and problem data, with only the problem data being sent to the cloud via edge gateway. Using the Deep Autoencoder, the problem data is compressed at the edge and reconstructed at the cloud end. Thus, the reconstructed data can be visualized to analyze the abnormalities seen from the sensor to take appropriate action.

Keywords: Internet of Things (IoT), Edge Computing, Machine Learning (ML), Deep Autoencoder

## Introduction

Edge computing can be referred to as a computational process of sensor data toward various data sources, close to the edge of the network and away from centralized nodes. It may be defined as a distributed IT network architecture that allows mobile computing to produce data locally [Shen et al., (2021](#ch49.xhtml#ref49_2)). Rather than relying on centralized cloud data centers, edge computing distributes processing power to safeguard real-time processing without loss of data while maintaining storage space bandwidth and on the network. Without edge computing, IoT today is functional across a wide spectrum of use cases ([Ashouri et al., 2019](#ch49.xhtml#ref49_13)).

Edge computing, however, may become a key enabler as more and more things become connected and as we investigate use cases with progressively stricter latency, bandwidth, and security requirements (Ananda Mohon Ghosh & Katarina Grolinger, 2021; Junlong [Li et al., 2022](#ch49.xhtml#ref49_6)) . But there are still questions and difficulties that will determine how much of an impact edge computing will have on IoT in the future ([Liu et al., 2021](#ch49.xhtml#ref49_16)). These include technical difficulties with assuring the edge infrastructure’s physical security ([Hastbacka et al., 2022](#ch49.xhtml#ref49_5)), as this infrastructure is likely to be used to store data outside of the extremely safe setting of dedicated data centers. Another technical challenge that many platforms are attempting to address is how to solve interoperability problems and make device management and control simpler.

While edge computing can enable real-time processing of data, many IoT edge devices, like sensors, do not have enough computational power to carry out any deep learning algorithms locally which may be complex ([Wisultschew et al., 2022](#ch49.xhtml#ref49_4)). As a result, these devices may rely on cloud or centralized systems which are used for storage and computational processing. Nevertheless, there are also efforts to develop more lightweight machine learning models that can be implemented directly on edge devices, such as sensors, without relying on cloud or centralized systems. These models, known as edge AI models, are designed to be more computationally efficient and require less memory and processing power than traditional deep learning models. This can help enable real- time processing and analysis of data directly on the edge devices, without transmitting data to a central system. Combining both edge and cloud computing has the likely to overcome the latency and support complex data analytics tasks. Considering Edge-Cloud, maximum features to be reduced can be a challenging problem. However, transferring all the data to the cloud is not feasible for computation as well as for storage ([Ghosh & Grolinger, 2021](#ch49.xhtml#ref49_1); [Li et al., 2020](#ch49.xhtml#ref49_8))and requires edge devices to act and perform computation ([Liu et al., 2021](#ch49.xhtml#ref49_16)). In this paper, only the necessary IoT sensor data is transferred to the cloud leaving the others.

Machine learning can be a powerful tool for classifying IoT data, as it enables the automatic identification and classification of patterns and trends within the data. This can help to unlock insights and drive better decision-making in a variety of domains, such as manufacturing, healthcare, and smart cities. Applications of ML for classifying IoT data include predictive maintenance in manufacturing, anomaly detection in healthcare, and traffic flow prediction in smart cities. By using ML to classify IoT data, organizations can gain new insights, optimize operations, and improve decision-making.

The remaining of this paper is ordered as follows. Section 2 discusses the related work. Section 3 presents the proposed framework on the edge. Section 4 shows the implementation of Edge. Section 5 presents the evaluation of the paper. Section 6 shows the result. Finally, Section 7 concludes the paper.

## Related Work

This section presents the combination of IoT- Edge-Cloud for different applications using algorithms of various sorts. Edge computing is playing a major role in the present day by connecting IoT and the cloud for purposes like storage, computation, alarm, prediction, gaining insights, etc.

Ghosh & Grolinger,(2021) investigated integration of edge and cloud computing by means of decreasing network traffic and latencies for IoT based data using Autoencoder. Sliding window is applied for data reduction ([Fekri et al., 2020](#ch49.xhtml#ref49_12); [Essien & Giannetti, 2020](#ch49.xhtml#ref49_9))and network traffic reduction Ghosh & Grolinger,(2021). On the other hand, [Ferrari et al., (2020](#ch49.xhtml#ref49_14)) examined the personalization of Human Activity Recognition models and carried out sliding windows and the generation of input features. [Li et al., (2022](#ch49.xhtml#ref49_6))used fog computing to provide privacy protection for the data getting from smart grid via SCADA while transferring from IoT to cloud.

[Essien & Giannetti (2020](#ch49.xhtml#ref49_9))proposed ConvLSTMAE which is a multi-step machine speed prediction for time series data. The presented framework of both Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) combined which extracts features for representation and sequential learning respectively. Finally, the encoder and decoder for dimensionality reduction which ultimately reduced the computational demands and the time taken for training.

[Pelle et al., (2021](#ch49.xhtml#ref49_7))introduced the public serverless E-C platform which uses the AWS Greengrass making it easier for computation on edge. On the other hand, [Wisultschew et al., (2022](#ch49.xhtml#ref49_4))shift the computing from cloud to the edge of IoT. Deep Neural Networks (DNN) work well with high-volume data in terms of accuracy. This paper uses different edge architectures for object classification and compares them to make a perfect solution for IoT applications.

[Lahasan & Samma (2022](#ch49.xhtml#ref49_15))attain a lightweight model, an effective two-layer optimizer that develops a lightweight Deep AE model by carrying out instantaneous selection for the input features, the number of hidden neurons and the number of training instances. The dataset is normalized where all the features are scaled to \[0,1\] using a min-max scaler ([Fekri et al., 2020](#ch49.xhtml#ref49_12); [Lahasan & Samma, 2022](#ch49.xhtml#ref49_15)).

[Cheng et al. (2021](#ch49.xhtml#ref49_17)) used a framework, Transformation Invariant AutoEncoder (TIAE), that accomplishes constant and better performance for unsupervised outlier detection by learning high-level semantic features. For each epoch, it incorporates self-paced learning for training the dataset. [Queiroz et al. (2022](#ch49.xhtml#ref49_3)) use fuzzy recommendation system which identifies data analysis needed at a certain layer of cloud-edge-IoT.

### Proposed Framework

This section represents Machine learning with Deep Autoencoder. The proposed framework for IoT devices to identify the abnormal behaviors from the sensor using the proposed algorithm at the edge device and making a Visualization of the problem data to analyze the issues.

### Data Preprocessing

*Normalization:* Data standardization is accomplished using the pre-processing method of normalization. Having various data sources that fall within the same range. It can be problematic for the network to train if the data is not normalized prior to training, which will significantly slow down learning. The min-max scaling can be used for normalizing the data. The formula for a min-max of \[0, 1\] is given as:

  
$$x^{\\prime} = \\frac{x - \\min(x)}{\\max(x) - \\min(x)}$$  

Where x represents the actual value, max( x ) and min( x ) are the maximum and minimum of the feature values and represents the standardized value.

*Parallel processing:* In the context of autoencoders, n\_jobs could potentially be used for data preparation or other parts of the training process that do not involve the neural network itself. For example, n\_jobs could be used to parallelize loading the data and pre-processing steps before feeding the data into the autoencoder for training. This can be useful for large datasets where loading and pre-processing the data can be time-consuming.

### Deep Autoencoder

This algorithm shown in [Fig. 1](#ch49.xhtml#fig49_1), will help with compressing the huge data being transferred from edge to cloud with the encoder-decoder concept. Encoder at the edge side and decoder at the cloud side. At the cloud side, the compressed data is reproduced to its original state.

![Figure 1 Deep Autoencoder](images/fig49_1_B.jpg)

[Figure 1 Deep Autoencoder](#ch49.xhtml#R_fig49_1)

*Feature selection:* To overcome the limitation of overfitting from happening, Embedded methods like regularization L1 and L2 is carried out for feature selection which by Selecting the best features help the model to perform well.

a) LI *Regularization -* L1 helps to overcome overfitting as well as improves the efficiency of the model. L1 regularizer can also be used for feature selection since it sets the weights of unrelated features to zero.

  
$$\\left. f = \\frac{1}{2}\\sum\\limits\_{L = 1}^{N}{(\\hat{y} - y)}^{2} + \\lambda\\sum\\limits\_{i = 1}^{N} \\middle| \\theta\_{i} \\right|$$  

Where N is the number of features. *λ* represents the regularization parameter and *θ* is a sum of vectors. *y* and *y*’ are the actual and predicted value.

### ML Classifier

The encoded data is classified into normal and problem data which is separated using Logistic Regression (LR) model since the data comes closer to linearly separable after encoding. Logistic regression can identify a linear decision boundary that separates the data into different classes. However, when the data is not linearly separable, logistic regression may not be able to find a good decision boundary and may lead to poor classification performance. SVMs work by finding the hyperplane that best separates the data into different classes, where a hyperplane is a decision boundary that maximizes the margin between the classes. Thus, it can be compared with original data being classified using Support Vector Machine (SVM) as its accuracy is comparatively similar to the classification of encoded data. The separated problem data is easily transferred to the cloud.

### Implementation on Edge Device

Data normalization is a common pre-processing step in machine learning, which involves scaling and shifting the values of a dataset so that they fall within a specific range. The goal is to ensure that different features in the dataset are on a similar scale, which can increase the efficiency of the model, and make it easier to interpret the results. Autoencoders ( [Kurihana et al., 2022](#ch49.xhtml#ref49_10); [Ohashi et al., 2021](#ch49.xhtml#ref49_11); [Chinnasamy et al., 2023](#ch49.xhtml#ref49_18)) are a type of neural network that can be used for unsupervised learning tasks, such as data compression, feature extraction, and anomaly detection. They consist of two main parts: an encoder which can be used to map the input to a lower-dimensional latent space, and a decoder which rebuilds the original data from the latent space representation.

This algorithm will help with compressing the huge data being transferred from edge to cloud with the encoder-decoder concept. To overcome the limitation of overfitting from happening, Pre-processing step shown in [Fig. 2](#ch49.xhtml#fig49_2) like regularization is carried out for feature selection which by Selecting the best features helps the model to perform well. Parallel processing reduces the time taken to train the model. Classification of normal and problem data can be done by logistic regression and support vector machine. Each can be used for the classification of encoded data and the original data. The problem data thus gets transferred to the cloud for visualization.

(4)

Where n is the total number of data points, y[i] is the actual value of the target variable for the i-th data point and ŷ[i] is the predicted value of the target variable for the i-th data point.

### Experimental Result

The experimental result provided by the implementation of ML with Deep Autoencoder is presented in this section. This part includes the different metrics which is used for checking the performance of the proposed model. These include: Accuracy, precision, Fl score, and recall shown in Table III. Precision and recall are two important metrics for evaluating the performance of a binary classification model, which classifies examples into one of two classes, typically labeled as positive or negative.

Precision calculates the ratio of true positive predictions amongst all positive predictions made by the model. It is calculated as:

(5)  
$$Precision = \\frac{TP}{TP + FP}$$  

Recall calculates the ratio of true positive predictions amongst all actual positive examples in the dataset. It is calculated as:

(6)  
$$Recall = \\frac{TP}{TP + FN}$$  

The Fl score is a frequently used metric for evaluating the performance of a binary classification model, which is the mean of precision and recall. It can be calculated as follows:

  
$$F1\\ Score = \\frac{(2 \\ast Precision \\ast Recall)}{(Precision + Recall)}$$  

Where TP represents the true positive, FP and FN are the false positive and false negative respectively.

## 7 Conclusion

By sending sensor data to any centralized system or to the cloud from IoT devices for processing and storing. Increased latencies and strain on communication networks and computations involved in cloud would result due to the expansion of linked devices. This paper investigates the combination of edge as well as cloud computing for IoT to decrease data loss and the computation at cloud side by minimizing the input features and selecting the appropriate data which is needed for monitoring and identifying issues utilizing the suggested approach. With the use of ML and Deep Autoencoder, computation can be executed efficiently and inexpensively on the edge. In the end, the suggested algorithm helps data from IoT devices get transmitted to the cloud without any need for further computation and data cleaning of the IoT data. At the cloud’s end, the minimized data get reproduced and used it to make visualization to identify issues and gain insights leaving cloud with less computation and space storage.

Future work will involve working with real-time world data and adding features to the proposed framework like alert messages getting from the cloud via an Android application or mail.
