# Teens, Screens, and Mental Health- A Study on Digital Wellbeing

Elizabeth Leah George^([^(39)](#fn39))

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-50](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-50)

## Abstract

Social media is a new trend of socializing, communicating, and maintaining friendships among the young and old. Major amount of time is spent interacting through a screen, the conversations in the digital space through texting, Instagram posts, and Facebook comments, Twitter tweets make it difficult to understand unexplained emotional changes. This minor research study examines the different ways in which social media impacts social comparisons among individuals of different age groups, and how this influence affects their overall physical and mental well-being. The study specifically focuses on the digital paradigm shift of social comparisons brought about by social media use. The study explores the frequency of social media usage, cyberbullying, sleep patterns, FOMO, and self-identity using questionnaires as primary data. A classification of mental health-related tweets with accuracy parameters can relate to health data analysis. Data visualization to understand the most influential parameter of digital well-being is relevant to social media.

Keywords: Social media, Mental health, Sentiment Analysis, Naive Bayes, K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic regression, Data Visualization

## Introduction

Social media is a forum that captures real time moods of users in different forms of communication. In a study #status of Mind by the royal society for public health mental disorders have been taken as a serious public health problem. Many of the individuals with depression go undetected. Various theories and research studies have found profound influence on social relationships that can help young people manage the challenges of adolescence, reduce face-face communication, freely express ideas online, and anonymity in internet communication for identity formation. The digital platform allows people from all different age groups to connect with one another globally creating an impact on both the physical and emotional health of a person.

An individual’s mental health varies depending on their age group, gender, line of work, and social environment. Similar to how a person’s mental health is influenced by their dietary habits, way of life, sleeping patterns, and extracurricular activities.Individuals ranging in age from 14 to over 45 access social media. Depending on their ages, it has different consequences on their mental and physical health. This research paper aims to analyze how social media usage affects an individual’s mental health regardless of age.

## Related Papers

The reviews by [Hilal Bashir (2017](#ch50.xhtml#ref50_1)) explore the correlation between adolescents’ mental health and their use of social media. It delves into identifying the specific social media platforms the findings of the survey, adolescents who spent more than 2 hours per day using social media tended to have lower levels of mental well-being compared to those who used it for less than 2 hours. that exert a considerable impact on mental well- being with a focus on social relationships and mental health, social media and anxiety, stress, depression, loneliness, etc of any age group. The Studies by Stones (2019) have mentioned mental issues in youngsters such as Cyber-bullying, body image concerns, irregular sleep cycles, and self- abuse due to social media, and provided valuable resolutions for each problem such as reducing screen time, portraying yourself without makeup and filters, blocking/reporting abusive and offensive content, etc. Latest studies by [Mireya Marquez (2022](#ch50.xhtml#ref50_3)) portrayed a comparison between Millennials (1981-1995), and Generation-Z (1996-2012) with a self-respond survey using Bergen social media addiction scale, Beck depression inventory **(BDI),** the generalized anxiety disorder 7-item scale (GAD-7), Rosenberg self-esteem scale (RSES) to check how long an individual is using social media, which platform is used majorly by them and to check their present mental state and in the past if they were under any medication due to social media. After conducting the survey, they came up with the conclusion that generation-Z faces more depression, anxiety, and loss of self-esteem compared to the millennial generation. A similar survey conducted by Anjali Singh (2020), the mental health effects of social media were examined among 100 adolescents aged between 16 to 18 years old which includes stress, depression, anxiety, etc. The scale which they used for collecting data was proposed by Lovibond (1995). Lovibond Then they used several statistical tests to examine. According to

## Methodology

The information gathered here is divided into two categories: primary data and secondary data. Actual questionnaires conducted using Google Forms were used to gather primary data and Twitter web scraping was used to gather the secondary data. 275 responses were cleaned from the core data and 1000 plus data was retrieved from the web using several keywords. The objective is to establish that the conclusions drawn from primary data regarding the influence of social media on mental health are equivalent to those obtained from secondary data through comparison and demonstration.

Various studies, such as [Abbasi (2008](#ch50.xhtml#ref50_5)), Chau (2012), and [Ceron (2014](#ch50.xhtml#ref50_7)), where machine learning has been widely used in text-based contextual classification and object recognition, resulting in successful applications in fields such as sentiment and affect analysis. [Cambria (2013](#ch50.xhtml#ref50_6)) and [Feldman (2013](#ch50.xhtml#ref50_9)) are examples of research that have demonstrated on the effectiveness of machine learning in sentiment and affect analysis. Nonverbal behavior analysis ([Subasic, 2000](#ch50.xhtml#ref50_12)) is used as a key to automatically understanding social interactions. The cues can then be used as machine-detectable evidence for automated analysis and understanding of social behavior. The performance of the machine learning approaches can be improvised with a rule-based classification approach ([Hutto, 2014](#ch50.xhtml#ref50_10); [Neviarouskaya, 2010](#ch50.xhtml#ref50_11); Wu, 2006).Datasets: Collection of Primary dataPrimary data was collected through a survey that was spread online across different age groups where the intended age ranged from 14 to 18, 18 to 30, 30 to 45, and 45+. They were questioned about their screen time uses, frequently used platforms, and their physical and mental well-being. After the survey was completed 275 responses were gathered. The outcome of the survey’s key questions are as follows: 141(51.3%) of the total replies are from women and 134(48.7%) are from men. The highest response rate 213(77.5%) came from respondents who were 18 to 30 years old while the lowest 18(6.5%) came from respondents who were 30 to 45 years old. The usage pattern of social users have their time spent on social media as 2-3hrs (41.8%), 3-5 hrs (25.1%), and more than five hours (19.6%). According to our survey, 207(75.3%) respondents chose Instagram as their most used app, which is consistent with the fact that it is one of the most widely used social networking applications thanks to its appealing features. WhatsApp is the second most popular app 206(74.9%) that practically everyone uses. A few more frequently utilized apps include Facebook, Linkedln, and YouTube. The survey revealed that social media has an impact on both their physical and mental health with stress on pain in the head, eyes, neck, and body, interrupted sleep etc are few examples of how social media negatively affects people’s physical health. Similar repercussions on mental health include anxiety, depression, stress, and development of an inferiority complex, etc.

![Fig. 1. Schema of Research](images/fig50_3_B.jpg)

Fig. 1. Schema of Research

**Collection of Secondary data:**

Web scraping to extract secondary data from Twitter using the keywords #mentalhealth, #mentalhealthandwellbeing, #healthandwellbeing, and #MHSM. Data was collected from over 1000 tweets using the hashtags #mentalhealth, #mentalhealthandwellbeing, #healthandwellbeing, #MHSM. A total of 1531 tweets were collected as secondary data. Tweets are randomly sampled, 80-20 training tests are distributed across the dataset, and all classifiers are trained and scored. Sentiment analysis, also known as opinion mining with computational linguistics, enables us to determine the sentiment of provided data, whether it is positive, negative, or neutral as shown in [Fig. 2](#ch50.xhtml#fig50_2). Machine learning algorithms make predictions, discover hidden patterns, and improve performance. We employed a range of machine learning techniques, including the Naive Bayes classifier, Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machines (SVM), and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), to analyze our data sets.

## Results and Discussions

The experiments and results discussed are the outcomes of the methodology. The pre- processing of the collected data is mentioned with classification scores, sample influence measures, and recommendations for sentiments. The keywords from Twitter taken are based on mental health keywords such as #mentalhealth, #mentalhealthandwellbeing, #healthand wellbeing, #MHSM. For the above keywords, a sentiment analysis is done to find the polarity of the keyword. The same dataset is analyzed through Gephi to find the influential nodes based on three categories (Text-Location), (User-Text), and (User-Location) as in [Fig. 3](#ch50.xhtml#fig50_3).

![Fig. 3. Data visualization in Gephi with the keywords](images/fig50_2_B.jpg)

[Fig. 3. Data visualization in Gephi with the keywords](#ch50.xhtml#R_fig50_3)

The communities formed are chosen and the modularity is calculated as in [Fig. 4](#ch50.xhtml#fig50_4). The sentiment analysis approach used for the posts involved a classification strategy to determine whether a tweet was related to mental health or not. Using SVM classification, the multi-class classification approach achieved an 81% accuracy rate in identifying mental health conditions. The results of all four classifiers remained high, resulting in an overall weighted average of high precision, recall, and Fl score, as shown in the table below. It was observed that the overall accuracy of the classifiers varied based on the content of the tweets collected. The model provided better accuracy with higher tweet content. The mean Reciprocal rank (MRR) measure was used to weigh the probability distribution for each prediction and account for the ranked order of true calculations compared to actual predictions. MRR consistently outperformed accuracy for all classifiers.

## Conclusion

Digital well-being is an utmost important health influence based on mental and emotional satisfaction. It spans the way social networking tools impact social measures to lead a healthy and positive life. This minor research is a small initiative taken to understand mental well- being and physical health among different age groups using a questionnaire method. The study reveals comments Positive approach for users as an excellent platform for self- exploration, an advertising platform to pursue their career and encourage others, and a platform for news, information, spiritual and educational content, blogs, videos, and other forms of communication. Negative remarks of a confused mind with negative comments and posts deal with crimes, gender discrimination, and harassment of people. Social media takes up too much time and attention, often disrupting sleep patterns, causing memory loss, impairing academic performance, and leading users to begin comparing their lives to those of others. It appears that being always online is something that young people love “Fear of Missing — Out (FoMO).” Adolescence is also plagued by mental health issues, including depression, anxiety, etc.

The minor research carried out in social media was modeled on the basis of a collection of posts based on mental health keywords to create a dataset, the tweets analyzed had set parameters and user tags that formed small communities where the machine learning algorithms showed accuracy in classification to detect various mental disorders.

# AI-Enabled Human and Machine Activity Monitoring in IIOT Systems

S. Sridevi and S. T. Deepa

Associate Professor, SSS Shasun Jain College for Women, Chennai

E-mail: [sridevi@shasuncollege.edu.in](mailto:sridevi@shasuncollege.edu.in), [stdeepa@shasuncollege.edu.in](mailto:stdeepa@shasuncollege.edu.in)

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-51](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-51)

## Abstract

For the past few decades, getting insights from industrial systems are explored a lot, for timely decision-making, right from the era of switches, pneumatic gauges, PID controls, PLC/DCS to current IIoT automation, where over a trillion dollars are spent in research & manufacturing globally. Cyber physical systems along with recent advances in AI, ML, Cloud, Edge, virtual computing power, high volume streaming services and real-time big data analytics have enhanced information collection, exchange, analysis, decision making & control to much higher levels. Similarly, human activity monitoring plays a key role in elderly care, disease detection, assisted living & remote consulting. The prevalent human monitoring sensors like PIR, GPS & HD cameras are expensive and have limitations like compatibility with existing systems. The proposed model HMAMnet is built over device-free localization, hybrid capsule CNN combined with Model predictive controls (MPC) methods for input( s) optimization. Standard protocols like OPC enables open device connectivity and data exchange. The model process enriched activity data from popular IOT datasets, with random Smote & PCA methods, and with appropriate choice hyperparameters, this not only makes the model robust with enhanced accuracy but also insights to control input parameters to get the desired output pattern. Industrial advantages of these solutions include increased uptime, productivity, quality, and revenue while reducing the cost of ownership, maintenance, energy, and waste. This module supplements the digital twin simulation process, with trends of environmental behavior patterns. Thus, the idea enhances the intelligence of activity monitoring systems, to auto-sense, process, decide & act, over the possible scenarios, in industrial and social domains.

Keywords: Human Machine activity monitoring, IIOT, MPC, CapsuleNet, Predictive control, CNN

## Introduction

The invent of Internet of Things (IoT) ([Rose et al., 2015](#ch51.xhtml#ref51_1)) around 1999, has opened a plethora of applications in connected devices in consumer, automotive, business, industrial & domestic spaces [Beecham Research (2014](#ch51.xhtml#ref51_2)). IoTs widespread adoption simplified processes and opened new avenues there were not feasible earlier. In healthcare, it helps from remote consulting to elderly care by remote monitoring their vitals and activities, disease detection to assisted living & Medication adherence. IACS processes were well established over the last few decades. While the first 3 industrial revolutions are based on steam, electricity, and robot automation & electronics, industry 4.0 ([Moller, 2016](#ch51.xhtml#ref51_3)) is widely based on IOTs, sensors, and machine learning to create smart products, smart production, and smart services (The fourth ICT-based industrial revolution, 2015).

The inherent distributed but connected nature of IOT, along with the digital technologies backbone, proposes a simpler alternative to industrial control systems and resolved the data sharing & visibility issues across enterprises. While still the performance, availability, and security are the threats for its widespread adoption, this chapter proposes a framework for IIOT components to intelligently monitor & control machine activities schematically. Below section describes the characteristics of IIOT & the principles governing its operations ([Boyes et al., 2018](#ch51.xhtml#ref51_14)).

## IIOT Governing Principles & Characteristics

IIOT Governing principles typically include: 1. IIOT to offer Perpetual & continuous connectivity with the environment to Monitor, Maintain, and Monetize (the 3 M’s); 2. IoT resolves large Analog data conversion problems. The big data derived from physical world, people, devices, environment & things in real-time is massive. it is mostly sensor acquired and digitized via A/D converters; 3. IOT data is Real-time and the data from thousands of sensors and actuators pump through the PLC/DCS and we need robust Real-time DB and infrastructure to store & process its historic trends; 4. Business, Engineering, and scientific insights can be derived from IIOT data in real-time, motion, rest, or archival stages; 5. IOT outputs present a real Time to insight at acquisition vs In-depth historic data analysis needs and take control actions; 6. IIOT improves edge data visibility throughout an enterprise, along with its traditional goals of handling data volume with velocity, value, and variety; 7. The shift towards Operational technology ( OT), with high-performance computing, virtualization, improved latency, bandwidth, security, duplication, reliability, etc. to distributed devices, shall eventually collapse different layers of data flow from distributed IOTs to IT-cloud, which saves space, energy, and deployment time.

## IIOT Device Characteristics

The functionality, criticality & management of the IOT devices typically defines its characteristic like: a) Criticality defines how important the device is to the ecosystem, and its replacements and usually manufactured with high standards & security compliance; b) Functions like data collection and algorithms used to analyze/transfer data, etc.; c) Interfaces that are used to configure the device and control its operations; d) Relationship with the environment /devices like a temperature sensor sending insights to increase fan speed, close shutter, etc.

## Architecture

The proposed 4 stage IIOT architecture depicts all the components of data acquisition, collection, dissemination, analysis, cloud storage & visualization as in [Fig. 1](#ch51.xhtml#fig51_1).

![Fig. 1. Typical IIOT architecture solution](images/fig51_1_B.jpg)

[Fig. 1. Typical IIOT architecture solution](#ch51.xhtml#R_fig51_1)

Primarily the physical systems, environments, machines, devices, people who generate data in real-time like a valve controlling the water level of a tank, a burning kiln and cooler system that can generate thousands of parameters in a cement plant, an accelerating electric vehicle controlled by various sensors over its battery, weight, temperature, etc. The sensors and actuators (motion tracking systems) in stage-1 are the devices that track motion, position, measures mass, temperature, pressure, etc., and convert them to digital signals. It could measure discrete or continuous data feeds. The concentrators in stage-2 are the PLC (Programmable logic controllers), DCS (Distributed control systems), and visualization systems like SCADA (Supervisory control & data acquisition system), connected manufacturing systems & controllers

Stage-3 Edge IT systems transfer the data transferred from distributed systems to higher IT environments like cloud, virtualization, etc. IoT edge computing resolves the latency problems linked with the cloud, as data is processed in proximity to its point of origin. For example, devices in large distributed mobile communication towers can be synced with IOT edge model. Remote IT and enterprise IT systems on cloud processing these plant floor data and disseminating the insights to different stakeholders forms stage 4. Purdue ([Williams, 1992](#ch51.xhtml#ref51_5)) is another popular model which is built on separating the enterprise with different zones like manufacturing, demilitarized, and safety zones for better data security and control.

## Connectivity & Data Exchange

Below aspects are critical in devising the connectivity between different layers: a. Mechanism with the devices is connected like wired, wireless, and physical modes; b. The nature of data transfer like Real-Time, offline, or asynchronous; c. Date exchange initiation like, by the device, by receiver or both.; d. Security mechanisms like authentication, identification (mutual or one-way), authorization (by user role), encryption (full or partial); e. Protocols at discovery, infrastructure, data transfer and security layers. Above models provide infrastructure for better Connectivity, Compute, and Control needs of manufacturing and enterprise entities ([Bradicich, 2017](#ch51.xhtml#ref51_6))

## Protocols for IIOT Data Exchange

A software Process is defined as “*Program in execution.*” When 2 different programs are running in a system, they typically communicate with each other with a set of protocols. The data between these 2 distinct processes are exchanged through “Object Linking and Embedding (OLE)” method. The same concept is extended to do data exchange from a plant control system and an IT monitoring tool with protocols like OPC (OLE for Process control) which was framed during 1996 by OPC foundation and still it is prevalent in industries.

The other popular Inter-process communication (IPC) methods in use since late 80’s are like, Dynamic Data Exchange (DDE) ([Kostek, 1996](#ch51.xhtml#ref51_7)), Shared memory where a common memory space is used by both processes, named pipe connections, etc., as supported by the operating system. These are capable of connecting to the process running in another system in network as well like remote named pipes, NetDDE, etc. Thus, protocols like OPC lays the standards that the tools that intend to read/write data to & from proprietary PLC/DCS like ABB, Siemens, Allen-Bradley, etc., through set of communication handshakes and acknowledgment in asynchronous callbacks.

This is typically a COM/DCOM based client-server architecture, where a client system requests the server component running in PLC/DCS with inputs like the field parameter to read/write, its value, and timestamp and get data asynchronously. For example, to decrease the load on a grinding mill having higher vibration, the parameters from mill sound level, measurements, temperature, and grinding pressure sensor are to be read through OPC as input process variables and the input feed to the mill is to be reduced by writing back to the conveyer belt (RPM) speed parameter to maintain the feed set-point parameter of the mill.

The frequently used industrial protocols are: Modbus, EtherNet/IP, PROFIBUS, DeviceNet, IEEE 802.11, TCP ISA100.11a, HART etc ([Gutierrez et al., 2018](#ch51.xhtml#ref51_9)). Due to incompatible nature of these legacy protocols, data interoperability and exchange were always a challenge. Open Platform Communications Unified Architecture (OPC UA) is adopted more as it is based on TCP/IP, SOAP & higher security, as compared to older COM/DCOM methods ([Ferrari et al., 2018](#ch51.xhtml#ref51_10)). It can be used in TCP/IP layer or with cross-platform SOAP/https with 128 / 256 bits encryptions as in [Fig. 3](#ch51.xhtml#fig51_3).

This chapter proposes such an intelligent monitoring and control prototype, from data collation, learning (ANN), Predictive Control models (MPC), and act-generated insights on time. ## HMAMnet Model

The algorithm of the proposed Human & Machine Activity Monitoring network (HMAMnet) is depicted as in [Fig. 6](#ch51.xhtml#fig51_6). As in the notation list of [Fig. 6](#ch51.xhtml#fig51_6)., SP (Setpoint) is the value in which the plant system to be maintained like the water level of the tank in [Fig. *5,*](#ch51.xhtml#fig51_5) to be maintained at *75* feet for a given period. Manipulated variables (MV) is the inlet water valve used to regulate the water flow to the tank & maintain the level (CV)

1.  Let the nonlinear process data \[collated by IOT Edge\] being modeled be denoted by the difference equation: Ô (t + 1) = O(t- No + 1), I(t), I(t - Ni + 1))
    
    Where Ô is the output prediction, typically a target variable of the plant (CV). No & Ni are the Past outputs & inputs.
    
2.  Formulate deep learning neural model: f(x) ∂o (w[2] ∂o (W[1]x + a[l]) + a[2]) = Ô(t + 1),
    
    Where ∂o & ∂o — sigmoidal activation functions; W[1] & W[2]**:** optimized weights matrices & a[l], a[2]: bias vectors of output & hidden layers; x = \[O(t),..., O(t – No + 1), I(t), ..., I(t - Ni + 1)\]T;
    
3.  The neural network or a capsule convolutional neural network (CNN) model provides predictions like time series value or classification probabilities like an abnormality. The MPC model (model predictive control) which suggested input changes (MV) needed to maintain target setpoint are trained offline.
4.  The process data validated from IIOT/Edge are validated with PCA (Principal Component Analysis) or SVD (Singular Value Decomposition) to include only the influential inputs having a higher impact on predicted output and Weights are serialized to find forthcoming values of Ô.
5.  As above non-linear modeling is impacted by differences in replicating real plant processes, the stabilizer module is introduced to process noise and unknown disturbances in data.
    
    If model errors are represented as e(t) and if model without process uncertainties is: Ô, then the stable model is denoted as: O(t)= Ô (t) + ê (t)
    
6.  The above disturbance is restricted to the list of allowable policies defined by the Piecewise Affine function (PWA) of previous disturbances ([Bemporad et al., 2004](#ch51.xhtml#ref51_12)). The nonlinear MPC aims to minimize the cost function to attain the needed set point range the target systems are to be controlled. The HMAMnet output (future MV changes) is validated by a fuzzy optimizer and fed to process and the deviance of CV from setpoint determines the need for online tuning of the model again. The model asymptotically converges faster and closer to the process being modeled.

Thus, the intelligent AI/ML based monitoring and controls as in the proposed HMAMnet model above or at simplified versions to suit use cases are really helpful to avoid human interventions and ensure continuous monitoring of the process parameters by creating a stable environment for the systems to operate. The attributes of HMAMnet are listed in the below table

Table 1 I-IMAMnet characteristics

 
| Parameters || Methods used |
| --- | --- |
| Process dynamics || Non-linear |
| --- | --- |
| System Identification || ANN / Capsule CNN providing probability/pose of observation |
| Uncertainties Type || Invariant additive disturbances with multiplicative uncertainties |
| Uncertainty propagation || Unbounded disturbance through neural stabilizer model |
| Control input parameterization || Affine parameterization of control policy |
| Input constraints || PCA/SVD |
| Prediction Constraints || Output constrained tubes |
| Receding-horizon implementation || Output feedback |
| Optimization algorithm || Modified GPC cost function |

## IIOT Activity Monitoring Apps, Benefits & Challenges

IIoT has a transformative impact on productivity & operational efficiency across domains from manufacturing to supply chain, significantly with below use cases, benefits, and constraints.

Following are typical applications of industrial IoT: 1. Process monitoring, 2. Temperature / Pressure monitoring, 3. Water quality monitoring, 4. Flow monitoring, 5. Remote asset monitoring, 6. Steam trap monitoring, 7. Machine health monitoring etc.

## IIOT Monitoring Benefits

Offloading AI & Analytics capability and load to distributed devices. For example, when a predictive model is deployed on a quality control camera the IoT Edge triggers an alert when there is an issue and processes it locally or sends to the cloud for further analysis. Other benefits include 1. Reduced Downtime, 2. Reduced waste (Man, Machine & Material) 3. Improved System Security & Quality, 4. Proactive Maintenance 5. Valuable Performance Insights 6. Seamless visibility of plant floor data across enterprise; 7. Decreased Cost of Ownership,

## IIOT Challenges

Industrial IoT monitoring and control solutions are essential, but most industrial systems have proprietary monitoring solutions in silo. Constructing a unified custom monitoring solution is not practical for large industrial establishments. Customization of widely used industrial interfaces to localization needs is also a deterrent factor; Other challenges are listed below:

 1. Deployment and operation of a remote monitoring system across larger regions or countries is not feasible. 2. Interfacing equipment’s to a third-party monitoring solution makes the process more complex leading to uncertainty. 3. Capabilities from different suppliers with niche or additional features, makes the system more expensive. 4. Existing connectivity network infrastructure of older plants may not aid in the provision of a custom IoT monitoring solution. 5. Creating a custom mix of capabilities from solutions of different vendors can lead to a complex system. 6. To augment the capabilities of built-in systems, often additional instrumentation and sensors are to be added, and data collection capabilities are to be enhanced enterprise-wide.

## Conclusion

This chapter introduces the evolution of IIOT from legacy control systems, data acquisition, and aggregation layers along with its Edge distribution to cloud/enterprise-wide network. Various industrial connectivity protocols with elaboration on Open Platform Communications Unified Architecture (OPC UA) standards and its client-server communication on TCP/IP & SOAP layers are discussed. OPC UA can also assign manufacturing resources, and embedded systems, to needed areas and extended computing nodes through the address space & pre-built models. Its main advantage is enabling a platform for unified information access to different systems Chen et al. (IEEE)Machine activity monitoring through IIOT forms key areas of Cyber-physical systems and it can be enhanced to service-oriented models ([Rojas and Garcia, 2020](#ch51.xhtml#ref51_15)). Typical Machine Activity monitoring use cases along with the proposed HMAMnet intelligent prediction model prototype are discussed, which fits over the 4 stage IIOT stack to augment needed value. Such custom AI/ML solutions (William and Ferraro, 2022) which could be built over the wealth of inexpensive cloud data collated from IIOT Edge & underlying PLC/DCS systems gives the cost-effective and faster intelligence control advantage over legacy systems.

# Application Development for Solving the Farmer Yield Problem Using Cloud Computing

J. Jeron Berselin, R. Muthukani, N. Arunthathi and J. Frank Vijay

Department of Information Technology, KCG College of Technology, Chennai, India

E-mail: [jrnbrsln@gmail.com](mailto:jrnbrsln@gmail.com), [mahirajan279@gmail.com](mailto:mahirajan279@gmail.com), [jeirus.jeff@gmail.com](mailto:jeirus.jeff@gmail.com)

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-52](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-52)

## Abstract

The absence of warehouses and proper market places, suppress the farmers, and they are not able to sell their yields for a reasonable price. So, they are in a situation to depend on a mediator and local traders for selling their crops. Farmers are not given reasonable prices by the mediators and farmers are unable to live a happy life. They are really affected by some external factors such as broker commission, transport charges, and importantly they are completely dependent on the rate/price that the broker fixes. This paper presents an approach to create a farmer-friendly application that would enable them to sell their commodities to clients directly at a fair market price without the need of any middlemen. The buyer and seller concept is implemented and the yield of the crops are sold to the buyers without any hurdles. The Google app engine is used to find the location of the farmers and the customers can easily identify the crop products which are near to them.

Keywords: cloud computing; agriculture; Google app engine.

## Introduction

Cloud computing is an on-demand Automatic Data Processing system resource that is one of the biggest human resource providers and also particularly contains knowledge storage and computing power. The term Cloud mostly wants to describe the knowledge centers on the current market to several users via the internet. The main benefit of Cloud Computing is it mainly reduces the IT costs that is it reduces the cost of maintaining the IT system. Clouds are limited to a single organization which is enterprise clouds or are offered for sale to numerous enterprises via public cloud. Cloud computing is mostly based on resource sharing and also includes sharing of databases, networking, and software.

Farming is the backbone of any country. In agriculture, the yield is the activity of the amount of crops adult or a product created per unit space of land. the most drawback of the farmers is marketing their yield crops with profit. The farmers cannot bear the transportation charges and lots of farmers cannot ready to afford storage facilities. And also, the most significant issue faced by the farmers is promoting competition and also the demand for the merchandise. The yield from the farmers is stored in a storage go down (Warehouse) and it takes a lot of time for them to sell the yield in a certain quantity and finish them without any wastage. This application presented in this paper will remove the concept of waste and get the yield sold in the correct amount and the full amount. The intermediate seller often known as broker, is avoided in this application as the selling of yield is happening directly between the farmers and the buyers. The application is designed and created for easy and profitable usage for the farmers.

This application will help the farmers to sell their yield products directly to the customers without any hurdles. There will be no fear to lose income for both the farmers and buyers whose livelihood is dependent on this field. The Application helps the farmers to sell their yield through this platform and also, they can determine their price to the buyers. This helps in faster selling of their yield without it going to ruins, and yield profit also. Buyers who are looking for a yield product also can get the yields they want for a reasonable price. The information of both customers and farmers is stored in the Cloud and the product is sold with the amount and Quantity recorded for future clearance. This helps in calculating the profit from this application process.

## Related Work

A methodology and an application can be developed to assist the farmers by producing reports on weather forecasts, information about crops, and farming tools and trends. It was a cloud-based application that supports the farmer to know about the weather condition and cultivate accordingly ([Peng & Wang, 2014](#ch52.xhtml#ref52_7)).

Cloud Agro System ([Jansirani et al., 2022](#ch52.xhtml#ref52_3)) gcontributes to the agriculture of Bhutan. This cloud-based technology concentrated on e-knowledge for farmers, communication between farmers and traders, connecting demand and supply, and research outcomes of farmer-related issues. Sunidhi et al., (2018) presented a detailed survey on Cloud based Android applications that provide a solution for the day-to-day issues and challenges faced by the farmers. The authors suggested that an application must have information on soil, crop varieties to grow, market pricing, types of fertilizer and pesticides, and instructions on how to boost agricultural yield in order to be valuable to farmers. Soil Water Content (SWC) measurement technology was presented in [Bo & Wang (2011](#ch52.xhtml#ref52_1)). It offered a cloud based IoT system which used M2X from AT&T, an Internet of Things (IoT) data storage, service, and management system. Information including the kind of soil needed for plantations, details on the seasons, the optimal fertilizer for growth, etc. was presented in the system [Vijayaraghavan & Kumaresan (2015](#ch52.xhtml#ref52_12)).

The attractive feature of this work is that the system provides information in native regional language which can be easily understandable for farmers. [Peng et al., (2014](#ch52.xhtml#ref52_7)) introduced the idea of GIS based on cloud computing; based on the most popular trends in developing GIS applications today and essential cloud GIS technologies that store Geographical based data in the cloud. It was discussed how we handle agricultural data, examine its qualities, and develop a smart farm management information system

The farmer buyer/seller existing system only has the means to sell the yield with the price. The existing application has weather forecasts and other crop-related videos and news. The Security of the existing application is simple authentication with passwords and storage of data is not vast. Also, the existing system does not provide an option to chat with farmer directly. So, communication is a great barrier. Due to this, there may be a chance of getting a misunderstanding between the customer and farmer. And mainly the existing system does not provide any sort of live location tracking.

## Farm Management Process

Farm management is a difficult and time-consuming job that entails a variety of tasks. [Figure 1](#ch52.xhtml#fig52_1) depicts the farm management business process. In addition to managing crops, farms must also manage inputs, quality, and inventories. They must also analyze profitability and manage finances

![Fig. 1. Farm Management Process.](images/fig52_1_C.jpg)

[Fig. 1. Farm Management Process.](#ch52.xhtml#R_fig52_1)

Farm managers create standardized technical planting instructions to direct and guide fieldwork. Thus, technicians oversee workers as they plant crops in accordance with a sowing plan and technical sowing guidelines. At the same time, they record field operations data and images using Mobile Operation Records System on smartphones or Personal Digital Assistants, including the overall agricultural input, such as labor. These records are then collected in production archives after being uploaded to a distant data server. These production archives serve as informational documentation of the entire process, from product planting to delivery for each batch. Raw materials are selected, delivered, weighed, and stored in accordance with the daily harvest plan. Various product batches may be produced or packed with various material batches before being delivered for sale.

Farm managers can acquire information about the production process and create statistics summarizing sowing areas and cost of production based on the collected data. When acquiring agricultural goods, information on each type of agricultural resource is put into the DFMS. Information on each pesticide’s safety window is available in the agricultural material information database. To help with pesticide use, the HTTP protocol can be used to download safety interval data for pesticides to the MORS. Additionally, farm managers can study the use of pesticides and assess the safety of the production process. Managers can examine each batch of products, analyze the cost structure of the product, evaluate, and award planting technicians based on the whole process of the information for planting, processing, and delivery.

## Proposed System

The mentioned architecture diagram consists of admin, client, user, database, and functionalities present in it. The proposed architecture diagram ([Fig. 2](#ch52.xhtml#fig52_2)) represents the basic components when the application is in use & ([Fig. 3](#ch52.xhtml#fig52_3)) explains the detailed structure of the working system. The data for this application is supplied to the server by the user module. The data components include things like location data and login credentials. All queries to the database are passed from the server and are sent to the database, which is linked to the server, where the data is obtained. The user has the option to select the crop yield that the customer genuinely needs. Additionally, the user has the option of selecting their current location manually or automatically. After successfully selecting the crops the customer can chat with the farmer directly through this application. The live location is very comfortable for the customer to choose their yield crop products within their location. Between both the user and the system, the API serves as an intermediary. It is also used to ensure security, control, and authentication. Servers, clients, and resources make up the client-server architecture, and HTTP is used to manage requests. The crop details, farmer’s and customer’s details, and transaction history are stored in the database.

![Fig. 2. Architecture Diagram.](images/fig52_2_B.jpg)

[Fig. 2. Architecture Diagram.](#ch52.xhtml#R_fig52_2)

![Fig. 3. Working Model.](images/fig52_3_C.jpg)

[Fig. 3. Working Model.](#ch52.xhtml#R_fig52_3)

The Application will help selling/buying the yield directly without any intermediate sellers. Additionally, the scope of increasing the profit for the farmers is high with this solution. The Application has the exact location where the yield/product is and the buyer can contact and get their product. The security of this application is high compared to the existing system as it uses cloud storage for storing seller data and buyer’s data. Without any wastage to their yield due to intermediate resources to carry their yield, this application helps in selling the yield quickly without wastage.

The application has a search algorithm where the different yield products are searched according to the buyers and the results will be displayed. The Application has the location of the sellers (farmers), it shows the location and the quality available to them. The Live location of the yield and farmers are used with Dijkstra’s Algorithm: Shortest path. Chat facilities are also available through which the farmer and the customer can communicate easily.

The Advantages of this application are First, it is easy to use and the User Interface is adaptable for all types of users. Secondly, the Security in this application is secure as it uses the firebase. Thirdly, the media files and other data can be easily stored with the use of Firebase database. And also, the overall Storage in this application is easy and constantly maintained. Importantly it is more flexible for the customers to use day-to-day. And finally, the product and price can be legit compared with other third-party sources.

## Results & Discussion

In this paper, the proposed system was developed in Java, and JAX-WS (Java API for XML Web Services) was used to create the required web services. A cloud-based system consisting of a five-tiered architectural model was adopted for the system in order to handle a sizeable number of users, credibility, security, and expandability. Any terminal device (laptop compute; tablet, or smartphone) with a web browser and an Internet connection can access the proposed system because it has a browser-server design. Every field operation sequence’s agricultural inputs and labor details were monitored and noted to keep track of the planting process for concurrence with technical standards. The proposed system ([Fig. 5](#ch52.xhtml#fig52_5)) not only complies with farm data management requirements, but it also makes it possible to effectively and precisely track and trace each batch’s production process.

This application will increase the economic development in farming with selling the agricultural product at good and value prices. This application can also help the agriculture development in our country with techniques that evolved over time. Also, this application will help to maintain a balanced relationship with farmers and customers. Also, each and every farmer can gain high profits in a legit and simple way.

# AI Enabled E-Commerce Studio Website

V. Rajkumaran,^([^(40)](#fn40))

E-mail:[rajkumaran.1321@gmail.com](mailto:rajkumaran.1321@gmail.com), [svvivek136@gmail.com](mailto:svvivek136@gmail.com), [raj@gmail.com](mailto:raj@gmail.com), [jeirus.jeff@gmail.com](mailto:jeirus.jeff@gmail.com), [bharathikannansrinivasan@gmail.com](mailto:bharathikannansrinivasan@gmail.com)

## Abstract

Artificial Intelligence can automate tasks and simplify complex processes to make decisions based on customer’s reviews and comments. The application of artificial intelligence in the website gives a user-friendly approach to the customers. This paper focuses on how to build up a site with the help of AI technology in which individuals can be ready to distinguish the studio, photographic artist, and editor’s dependent on individuals like magazines, corporate occasions, birthday celebrations, weddings, occasions, and so forth. The clients can book the studio’s for their necessities on the actual site and also can purchase the studio items like cameras, collections, photograph outlines, and so on. The clients can redress their quires via mailing the admin in the controlled structure. It is a finished full-stack project which incorporates cloud for capacity and AI to figure out the best studios utilizing a survey framework. This paper employs artificial intelligence (AI) concepts to elevate and modify a studio website in order to improve the client experience and increase conversions based on user reviews. The affirmation for the client’s reserving will be sent to their particular mail id utilizing PHP. The front-end is developed using HTML, CSS & Javascript. The SQL Data set is utilized to get and store the client data. The bank end modules are created utilizing PHP and Javascript. This site presumes that the clients can purchase and book their occasions as per their requirements.

## Introduction

## Literature Survey

AI algorithms now evaluate user data and influence millions of people’s decision-making processes in areas such as loan rates, employment, and criminal justice ([Vijayaraghavan et al., 2021](#ch53.xhtml#ref53_11)). They play crucial parts in a variety of businesses. Still they have drawbacks that can lead to discrimination ([Akter & Wamba, 2016](#ch53.xhtml#ref53_1)) and erroneous decision-making. For example, news recommendations and algorithms to target certain audiences in online sites have recently gotten a lot of press for exacerbating the lack of knowledge variety on the platform (S. I. et al., 2020). An important problem is that decision-making systems that run via algorithms provide relevant information and the best options themselves instead of letting the users choose based on the list of recommended items like how recommender systems do. To bring this to notice, In order to mitigate the potential adverse effects of nascent AI autonomous systems, Vlasselaer et al., (2015)proposes the use of collaborative task representations that incorporate both machine learning models and human expertise. They provide instances of interactive systems that have active computational assistance. They argue that context-aware systems should not replace human decision-making. To ensure accountability for both the system and its users, they advocate for granting users control over the system. Being transparent can assist avoid blind trust by providing crucial information for decision-making that would otherwise be unavailable to end-users ([Ignatov et al., 2019](#ch53.xhtml#ref53_5)). The advantages of algorithmic openness and comprehensibility are manifold, including the detection of partiality and prejudice ([Bahnsen et al., 2015](#ch53.xhtml#ref53_2); Dhanalakshmi & Devi, 2020), enhancing user cognizance of the system’s conduct (S. I. et al., 2020), offering understandable actions by intelligent systems (K. N. et al., 2020), and guaranteeing user answerability ([Ignatov et al., 2019](#ch53.xhtml#ref53_5)). There is also a growing body of evidence highlighting the negative effects of algorithmic decision-making, particularly with regard to discrimination and legal challenges. Consequently, researchers are advocating for AI to be subjected to legal oversight and accountability in order to promote openness and transparency ([Halbe & Joshi, 2015](#ch53.xhtml#ref53_4)). Recommender systems, which may be found in news channels, social networking sites, and e-commerce, have become more and more important in consumers’ day-to-day online activities. By proposing more of what we desire, machine learning algorithms that learn from our preferences and biases enhance those preferences and biases.

Although the term “recommendation system” might seem to be brand-new, it was first used in the 1990s. His early research, which was inspired by people’s challenges in finding and choosing products in the face of the overwhelming amount of information available on the internet, concentrated on Information retrieval, forecasting theory, management, and marketing are all related to cognitive sciences ([Vijayaraghavan et al., 2021](#ch53.xhtml#ref53_11)).

As a result, the recommendation system has evolved as a business opportunity that uses the vast amount of data and knowledge accessible to generate profit desirably, in addition to solving a problem. Many consider Tapestry, which was developed at the time, to be the first recommendation system. Because in this approach, information was filtered by a team of people working together, he coined the term “collaborative filtering.” Initially, the term “collaborative filtering” was used to refer to any suggestion technique, but the creators started referring to it as a “recommendation system” since not every system requires the usage of the collaborative technique. Almost every service we use on a regular basis now uses recommendation algorithms, including social networks, ecommerce, and even app stores. Despite their differences, they all have one thing in common: the necessity to deal with a significant volume of data. The technology then assists in organizing the data in some more appealing manner, therefore improving EXPERIENCE of the user. The user won’t have to keep browsing through categories and selecting goods one by one if he is unclear about what he is looking for because he will have rapid access to a variety of possibilities ([Vijayaraghavan et al., 2021](#ch53.xhtml#ref53_11)). Depending on the industry and the items to be recommended, recommendations are given in different ways. But generally, everyone deals with three distinct types of proposals:

*   The ones that consider profile and more meaningful to him;
*   Those who take into account how well-liked the product is by all users;

## Technology Adopted

A set of tactics and algorithms known as recommender systems enable users to receive recommendations for “relevant” content. The recommended products should be applicable towards the user to encourage interaction. Recommender systems prioritize the most important information and arrange it in order of relevance for the user. The system must evaluate relevance primarily based on past data. Recommender systems apply two sorts of machine learning computations, namely content-based and collaborative filtering, to sort the data.

While collaborative approaches leverage interactions, methods based on contents use item attribute similarity to determine similarity ([Fig. 4](#ch53.xhtml#fig53_4)).

 ![Fig. 4.  Depicts the Recommendation Task](images/fig53_4_B.jpg)

[Fig. 4\.  Depicts the Recommendation Task](#ch53.xhtml#R_fig53_4)

This webpage was generated using the collaborative filtering technique. The initial step in creating a system that can recommend products to customers based on similar users’ interests is identifying analogous individuals or items. The second stage involves predicting ratings from users for products that have not yet been rated. A collection of methods known as collaborative filtering uses various ways to find comparable individuals or objects as well as various ways to generate ratings that are relevant to ratings of alike users. The similarity is not calculated in collaborative filtering utilizing parameters, examples of such data could be user age, film category, or any other relevant details on clients or goods. The explicit or implicit rating of a product is used to calculate the similarity. One technique to assess the outcome’s accuracy is to look at the square root of the mean of the squared differences between predicted and actual values, commonly referred to as RMSE that allows users to forecast ratings for test datasets of consumer pairings with previously identified rating values. The error would be the difference between the known and projected values. ([Fig. 4](#ch53.xhtml#fig53_4)).

Computing the RMSE involves calculating the square root of the mean of all standard errors in the test set.

To compute the rating (R) that a customer (U) is likely to assign to an item (I), the subsequent procedures are followed:

*   Identify other users who have reviewed the same product (I) as user U.
*   Use the ratings of those users to calculate The R (rating) that U (user) would allocate to item I.
*   The algorithm utilizes a roster of users who share similarities with user U. to determine their rating (R) for a given product I.
*   As per the algorithm, the rating (R) provided by user U for item I is expected to be in proximity to the mean of ratings given to I by the top 5 or top 10 users who share the highest similarity with user U.

The equation used to compute the mean of evaluations provided by n users is expressed as:

(1)  
$$R\_{U} = (\\sum\\limits\_{u = 1}^{n}R\_{u})/n$$  

The formula for determining the mean score given by n comparable users is as shown below:

Average Rating = Sum of Ratings Provided by n Similar Users / n

In other words, the mean rating given by the n comparable users can be obtained by dividing the total sum of the ratings given by them by the number of users similar to user U. The above-mentioned equation is frequently utilized in collaborative filtering methods to anticipate the rating that a user might assign to a specific item by taking into account the evaluations provided by comparable users.

# Correlational and Sentimental Analysis Using LSTM to Forecast Stock Price

E. Pavithra^([^(41)](#fn41))

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-54](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-54)

## Abstract

This research paper proposes an innovative technique for forecasting stock market trends and analysis by incorporating the interdependence of stocks, risk-identification, and sentiment analysis of financial news. Our approach utilizes data analysis techniques, correlation identification, natural language processing used for sentimental analysis with long short-term memory (LSTM) model. We apply Pearson correlation coefficient to identify the correlation between the top stocks and their interdependence. The proposed model incorporates identified risks associated with market movements, such as political instability, and economic changes to enable more comprehensive stock market analysis. Sentiment analysis is performed using natural language processing techniques, which allows the model to analyse financial news sentiment scores to predict the coming trend in the market. LSTM, a type of deep learning algorithm, is applied to analyse time series data, including historical data and trends, to predict future stock prices. The proposed model improves the accuracy of stock market forecasting and provides investors with a more informed decision-making approach that reduces their risk exposure. Overall, the proposed model for stock market prediction and analysis provides a comprehensive, efficient approach to analyzing the stock market movement, and it has the potential to help investors make profitable trading decisions.

Keywords: LSTM, Correlation, Risk identification, NLP

## Introduction

The stock market is an essential element of the financial industry that greatly boosts the economic development of a nation. The stock market is used as a benchmark to compare the economic growth of different countries, and its performance is closely monitored by investors, speculators, and financial analysts. Forecasting the movements of the stock market can be a difficult undertaking as it involves dealing with the intricate workings of the market and the unpredictability of constantly changing data. However, accurate predictions can provide valuable insights into the market’s trends and enable investors to make informed investment decisions, thus helping to improve the country’s economy and the financial status of everyone. Since the profit from stock market benefits for the country’s economy status also its citizens. The non-stationary nature of stock market price series presents a significant challenge for accurate prediction It is typical for stock price sequences includes lot of noise and oscillations. These characteristics making it difficult for representing the data in a meaningful way. Several techniques involve utilizing manual features like stochastic technical indicators and moving averages. Also, the advanced techniques using deep learning neural networks, and reinforcement learning have some limitations and need to be improved for the model to work more accurately. Hence, a fresh strategy for stock market forecasting and analysis is required. So, this research considers the interdependence of stocks, risks associated with market movements, and sentiment analysis of financial news.

This research paper presents a methodology for predicting and analyzing the stock market that leverages advanced data analysis techniques. Our approach utilizes the Pearson correlation coefficient to identify the co-dependency of the top stocks and identify the risks associated with market movements. We also employ natural language processing to analyze the sentiment scores of financial news for the stocks which are identified having low risk, enabling us to make more accurate predictions about the market’s future trends. Finally, we use long short-term memory (LSTM) algorithms to estimate the future values of stocks which have less risk, their sentiment scores, and the times series data. By combining these analyzed data, our proposed model aims to provide better accuracy for predictions which will give higher profits for investors.

## 3 Corelation Analysis

Correlation analysis is an important statistical technique used to measure the strength of the relationship between two variables.

The Pearson correlation coefficient measures the strength of the linear association between two variables. A score of +1 represents a perfect positive correlation, while a score of 0 indicates no correlation between the variables. A score of -1 represents a perfect negative correlation.

The Pearson correlation coefficient can be calculated using the formula:

  
$$r = \\frac{\\sum\\limits\_{j = 1}^{n}\\left( {\\left( {x\_{i} - \\overline{x}} \\right)\\left( {y\_{i} - \\overline{y}} \\right)} \\right)}{\\sqrt{{\\sum\\limits\_{i = 1}^{n}\\left( {x\_{i} - \\overline{x}} \\right)^{2}}{\\sum\\limits\_{i = 1}^{n}\\left( {y\_{i} - \\overline{y}} \\right)^{2}}}}$$  

r - correlation coefficient, n is the number of observations,

Σxy - sum of the products of the paired observations,

Σx and Σy - sums of the x and y observations,

Σ^2 and Σy^2- sums of the squared x and y observations.

Correlation analysis can provide valuable insights into the relationships between different variables in research, but it is important to note that correlation does not necessarily imply causation. Other factors that are not being measured may be influencing the relationship between the variables, so it is important to interpret the results of correlation analysis carefully and consider other possible explanations for the observed correlations.

### Sentimental Analysis

Sentiment analysis is a technique used in natural language processing (NLP) to identify and extract subjective information from text data. One of the most widely used sentiment analysis tools is VADER (Valence Aware Dictionary and sEntiment Reasoner) uses grammar rules and lexicons to analyze sentiment in the textual data. Unlike traditional methods that rely solely on keyword matching, VADER uses a combination of lexicon-based analysis and grammatical rules to determine the sentiment of a given text. VADER uses a sentiment lexicon that contains a list of words and their associated sentiment scores. The lexicon is specifically designed to handle sentiments expressed in social media, where conventional rules of grammar may not always apply. Each word in the lexicon is assigned a sentiment score based on its polarity (positive or negative) and intensity. For example, the word “good” has a positive polarity and a high intensity score, whereas the word “bad” has a negative polarity and a high intensity score.

To determine the sentiment of a text, VADER first tokenizes the text into individual words and punctuation marks. It then applies a set of rules to determine the overall sentiment score of the text. These rules consider factors such as capitalization, punctuation, and degree modifiers (such as “very” or “extremely”) that can affect the sentiment of a sentence.

The final sentiment score is a continuous value between -1 and 1, with negative values indicating negative sentiment, positive values indicating positive sentiment, and values close to zero indicating neutral sentiment. In addition to the overall sentiment score, VADER also provides scores for the positive, negative, and neutral sentiment expressed in the text.

Overall, the VADER algorithm provides a fast and effective way to perform sentiment analysis on textual data, particularly in the context of social media where traditional methods may not be as effective. Bottom of Form

## LSTM

An LSTM (”Long Short-Term Memory”) model is a form of artificial neural network that is designed to solve the vanishing gradients issue which is occurring in traditional RNNs, that can make it difficult to train networks on long sequences of data.

The LSTM architecture ([Fig. 1](#ch54.xhtml#fig54_1)) consists of memory with ReLU as it activation function except for the candidate state. The LSTM model includes multiple gates which regulate how information moves through the network.

![Fig. 1. Modified LSTM Architecture](images/fig54_1_B.jpg)

[Fig. 1. Modified LSTM Architecture](#ch54.xhtml#R_fig54_1)

*Forget Gate:* The forget gate selects which data to keep or discard from the previous cell state. It receives the previous hidden state and the present input as an input and uses ReLU as an activation function.

The forget gate equation:

  
fg(*t*) = *R**e**L**U*(**W****m**\_*f**g* ⋅ \[*h*(*t* − 1), *x*(*t*)\] + *b**v*\_*f*)  

Wm\_fg - weight matrix, by\_f - bias term, h(t-1) previous hidden state, and x(t) - current input.

*Input Gate:* The input gate determines which data is added to the cell state. It also receives the previous hidden state and the current input as input and uses ReLU as an activation function. The input gate equation:

  
ig(t) = *R**e**L**U*(Wm\_**i****g** ⋅ \[*h*(*t* − 1), **x**(t)\] + *b**v*\_**i**)  

Wm\_fg - weight matrix, bv\_f - bias term, h(t-1) - previous hidden state, and x(t) - current input.

*Candidate State:* The candidate cell state calculates the new candidate values that can be added to the current cell state. It uses tanh as an activation function.

The candidate cell state equation:

  
*c*\_*h**a**t*(t) = tanh (*W***m**[1]**c** ⋅ \[h(t − 1), **x**(**t**)\] + *b**v*\_*c*)  

Wm\_c - weight matrix, bv\_c - bias term, h(t-1) past hidden state, and x(t) - current input.

*Current Cell State:* The current cell state updates the previous cell state by removing the information that the forget gate wants to discard and adding the information that the input gate wants to add. It uses element-wise multiplication and addition operations.

The current cell state equation:

  
*c*(*t*) = *f**g*(*t*)^(\*)*c*(*t* − 1) + *i**g*(*t*)^(\*)*c*\_*h**a**t*(*t*)  

fg(t) - output of the forget gate, fg(t) - output of the input gate, c(t-1) - previous cell state, and c\_hat(t) - candidate cell state.

*Output Gate:* It decides which data from latest cell state to output as current hidden state. It receives past hidden state and the present input as input

The output gate equation:

  
$$\\begin{array}{l} {out\\\_ g(t)\\, = \\, ReLU(Wm\\\_ out\\\_ g \\cdot \\lbrack h(t - 1),\\mathbf{x}(\\mathbf{t})\\rbrack +} \\\\ {bv\\\_ o)} \\\\ \\end{array}$$  

Wm\_og - weight matrix, bv\_o - bias term, h(t- 1) - previous hidden state, and x(t) - current input.

The training of an **LSTM** model involves iteratively updating weights and offset values using an optimization algorithm to reduce the discrepancy between the expected output and the actual output.

## Data cleaning

### Times series data

For time series data, data cleaning includes removing the null values, Checking, and removing duplicate data to avoid skew analysis, handle missing data using backfilling method. When a company undergoes a stock split or pays dividends, it can affect the price and volume of data. To account for this, the data needs to be adjusted for these events. Examining extreme values and remove outliers.

### Textual Data Cleaning using NLP

Data cleaning ensures that the text data is uniform, consistent, and free from any unnecessary noise. We have used NLP techniques. [Table 4](#ch54.xhtml#tab54_4) shows the comparison of word counts in collected tweet dataset that was compiled before and after data cleaning process.

[Table 4 Comparison of Word counts](#ch54.xhtml#R_tab54_4)

 
| Data cleaning || Before NLP || After NLP |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Length || 1180 || 1180 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Words Count || 28967 || 23200 |

*   The process involves removing any irrelevant or redundant information.
*   Stop words are articles or frequent words that have no meaning, such as “the,” “and,” and “a.” need to be removed.
*   It also involves removing punctuation, converting all text to lowercase, and stemming words to their base form.
*   Regular expressions can be used to remove any unwanted characters, such as HTML tags or URLs, from the text data.
*   Identifying the language of the text and filtering out non-English text as non-English words can introduce noise.

## Proposed Methodology

Proposed methodology aims to reduce risk before building the model. It would help the investors to majorly focus on the least risk stocks for analyzing and prediction. Its is achieved by collecting the overall stocks on each sector or specifying index using Yahoo tickers. The proposed architecture ([Fig. 2](#ch54.xhtml#fig54_2)) is shown below:

![Fig. 2. Proposed Methodology](images/fig54_2_B.jpg)

[Fig. 2. Proposed Methodology](#ch54.xhtml#R_fig54_2)

After collecting the data, pre-processing should be done to avoid including invalid data. Using Pearson co-efficient, it would form a co-relation matrix for the whole collected index. Identify the positive correlation between stocks and choose those particular stocks for risk analysis and further processing.

Using the risk analysis method identify least risk data and collect times series data including (High, Low, Open, and Close) indicators. For the same identified stocks scraping tweet data and any other related data relating to the particular stocks. Vader analysis is used to calculate the sentiment scores. Integrate time series dataset with sentiment scores which is major factor in stock market for better prediction.

## Experiment and Results

### Correlation Matrix and Risk Analysis

Correlation matrix ([Fig. 3](#ch54.xhtml#fig54_3)) is constructed using Pearson co-efficient method to identify highly co-dependent stock data. This correlation matrix for 30 parameters shows positively correlated data which is data containing above 0.5 as co-efficient. Those parameters are TCS, Wipro, Bajajfinserve, Bajajfinance, IndusInd Bank, Bajajfinance, and Tech Mahindra.

![Fig. 3. Correlation Matrix](images/fig54_3_B.jpg)

[Fig. 3. Correlation Matrix](#ch54.xhtml#R_fig54_3)

Between these positive correlated data, calculate the risk value using standard deviation.

  
$$s = \\sqrt{\\frac{\\sum^{}{(X - \\overline{X})}^{2}}{n - 1}}$$  

> s- Standard Deviation,
> 
> X - Daily return,
> 
> X̄ - Average of daily return,
> 
> n - Total number of samples

It measures the degree to which an investment’s returns deviate from its average return ([Fig.4](#ch54.xhtml#fig54_4)). This figure represents the company risk level of each stock. It shows that TCS has a low-risk value and Induslnd Bank has a high-risk value among the correlated data.

![Fig. 4. Risk Analysis](images/fig54_4_B.jpg)

[Fig. 4. Risk Analysis](#ch54.xhtml#R_fig54_4)

### Sentimental Analysis

In this study, we employed the VADER tool to analyze the sentiment scores of a large corpus of text data collected from Twitter. The entire sentiment of the text is captured by the compound score, which is a single value. It is determined by adding up the valence scores assigned to each word in the text and adjusting for the intensity of the sentiment, and normalizing the score to be between -1 (most negative) and +1 (most positive). The compound score provides an overall measure of the sentiment of the text, considering both positive and negative sentiment. The Vader analyzed contains positive, negative, and neutral sentiment values from the collected tweets, and compound scores is displayed as sentiment score in [table 5](#ch54.xhtml#tab54_5).

## Conclusion and Future Works

The proposed multi-fusion information model presented in this research paper can assist investors in minimizing the risk of loss in the stock market. The model suggests identifying co-dependency among stock data and choosing the least risky stock data for different sectors, thereby providing valuable insights to investors for choosing the least risky stock in each sector which could be ideal for making long-term or short-term investments. Using VADER analyzer, Sentimental scores were identified for the stocks and integrated with historical data of the particular stock to identify patterns and analysis using LSTM algorithm. Above factors enhance the accuracy of future stock predictions. Since the model has an accuracy level of 95 percent. Overall, the proposed model can potentially improve investment decision-making and help investors mitigate risk in the stock market. A data-driven approach is crucial in stock analysis, and investors need to carefully consider various factors when making investment decisions. Future work should focus on choosing the dataset and approach by doing extensive research on stock market domain and its trading techniques and strategies. Developing an algorithm that incorporates stock market strategies can potentially enhance the efficiency of analysis. To enhance time-series data analysis, it is necessary to detect significant patterns in different technical indicators such as on-Balance Volume, Moving average, Average directional index, oscillators. Also identifying fake contents before calculating sentiment scores. Fake contents can be avoided using information from verified accounts and reliable social platforms.
