# A Novel Authentication System Based on CNN and IoT

Suraj Golthi,[^(42)](#fn42)

Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Hindustan Institute of Technology and Science, Chennai, India

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-55](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-55)

## Abstract

For many years, researchers have been interested in the use of biometric authentication in voting systems. This study suggests an anonymous voting system that makes use of deep learning techniques and finger vein detection to enable secure and reliable voter authentication in light of the growing demand for secure and anonymous voting processes. In order to ensure voter security and authentication, this paper suggests an anonymous voting system that makes use of deep learning techniques and finger vein recognition. Voters’ finger vein images will be captured by the system, which will then classify and extract features using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models. An Internet Of Things (IoT) - based alert system that can alert authorities to any fraud during the voting process is also integrated into the proposed system. In conclusion, the proposed system offers a secure and anonymous voting process that uses finger vein recognition and deep learning techniques. This paper presents a detailed methodology for the development of the system, including the dataset, the CNN model, and the IoT-based alert system.

Keywords: Anonymous Voting, Biometric Authentication, Finger Vein Recognition, Deep Learning, Convolutional Neural Network, IoT-Based Alert System, Secure Voting, Fraudulent Activities

## Introduction

Electronic voting systems have grown in popularity in today’s elections throughout the world with the advancement of technology. Electronic voting systems have been discovered to be open to attacks like hacking and fraudulent voting ([Pooja & Anuja, 2022](#ch55.xhtml#ref55_2)), raising worries about security and privacy. An anonymous voting system that uses Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Internet of Things (IoT) technology to distinguish verified and unverified users via finger vein recognition has been offered as a solution to these issues.

The finger vein images, which are obtained using a finger vein recognition device, serve as the system’s main dataset. The images are first cleaned up to get rid of any noise before being converted into numerical data using a variety of mathematical methods. With the help of this numerical information, a CNN model is trained to categorize the images as belonging to verified or unverified users. The system’s IoT component is used to monitor the voting process and send notifications in the event of any fraud. The data is gathered from various sensors and devices, including the finger vein recognition device, and transmitted to a central server using an Arduino microcontroller.

The proposed system differs from conventional voting procedures in a number of ways, including increased security, anonymity, and transparency. It eliminates the need for paper ballots, lowering the possibility of fraud or counting errors. The system can now provide real-time feedback thanks to the use of IoT technology, which could help to increase the effectiveness of the voting process.

The primary benefit of this system is its capacity to deliver anonymous and secure voting processes, preventing fraud while protecting voters’ privacy. For the implementation of a secure voting system, the use of finger vein recognition and deep learning techniques offers an accurate and dependable method for authentication.

This novel authentication system ensures anonymity and security during the voting process and addresses the problems with conventional voting systems. Experimental findings show the effectiveness of the proposed system, which makes it a workable option for putting in place a safe and dependable system.

### Literature Survey

Artificial neural networks are used in deep learning, a branch of machine learning, to model and resolve complex issues ([Boucherit & Zmirli, 2022](#ch55.xhtml#ref55_1)). It is a technique for teaching artificial neural networks to spot patterns in sizable datasets, enabling machines to gain knowledge from their mistakes and become more accurate with practice ([Pooja & Anuja, 2022](#ch55.xhtml#ref55_2)). Deep learning models are well suited for tasks like image and speech recognition, natural language processing, and anomaly detection because they have multiple layers of interconnected neurons that can process and classify data hierarchically ([Boucetta & Boussaad, 2022](#ch55.xhtml#ref55_6); [Ardak & Bardekar, 2022](#ch55.xhtml#ref55_4); [Khan et al., 2020](#ch55.xhtml#ref55_10)).

CNNs use a set of filters that are convolved with the input data to automatically learn and extract features from raw data, such as images ([Ardak & Bardekar, 2022](#ch55.xhtml#ref55_4)). The feature maps that result from each filter’s detection of a particular feature—such as edges, corners, or textures—are then combined and processed to produce higher-level representations of the input data ([Sruthi & Shanjai, 2021](#ch55.xhtml#ref55_8)).

Merge Convolutional Neural Network (Merge CNN), an improved deep network that makes use of several CNNs with short paths is used in finger vein identification using CNN ([Boucherit & Zmirli, 2022](#ch55.xhtml#ref55_1)). The method is based on combining the outputs of multiple identical CNNs with various input image qualities into a single layer ([AboSamra et al., 2017](#ch55.xhtml#ref55_12)). They created various networks and trained them using the FV-USM dataset to accomplish this. In final they merged CNN labeled A, which combines the original image with an image enhanced using the Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram (CLAH) method, and was constructed using the most optimal CNN architecture ([Boucherit & Zmirli, 2022](#ch55.xhtml#ref55_1); [Sruthi & Shanjai, 2021](#ch55.xhtml#ref55_8))

A biometric technique called finger vein recognition uses distinctive vein patterns in people’s fingers to identify them. It is a very accurate and secure authentication method that is challenging to forge or tamper with [Syazana-Itqan et al., (2016](#ch55.xhtml#ref55_5)); [Ayed (2017](#ch55.xhtml#ref55_7)). A near-infrared light source is used to take pictures of the veins in a person’s finger as part of the finger vein recognition process. The distinctive vein patterns and characteristics, such as their size, shape, and location, are then identified through analysis of these images ([Cruz & Kaji, 2017](#ch55.xhtml#ref55_9); [Hassan et al., 2020](#ch55.xhtml#ref55_11)).

Methods for identifying finger veins fall into three categories: traditional methods, machine learning-based methods, and hybrid methods. A conventional system can function in identification mode or verification mode depending on the application’s context ([Khan et al., 2020](#ch55.xhtml#ref55_10)). The three main steps of the traditional recognition process are image pretreatment, feature extraction, and comparison ([Picciuco et al., 2019](#ch55.xhtml#ref55_18); Ismail & Mohamed, 2019). The main benefit of the proposed system is its capacity to offer secure and anonymous voting processes, preventing fraud while protecting the privacy of voters. For the implementation of a secure voting system, the use of finger vein recognition and deep learning techniques offers an accurate and dependable method for authentication ([McCorry et al., 2017](#ch55.xhtml#ref55_3)).

## Proposed Methodology

Convolutional neural network (CNN) and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies are used in combination in the proposed methodology for the anonymous voting system using finger vein recognition. In order to maintain voter anonymity, the system attempts to categorize users as verified or unverified based on the pattern of veins in their fingers.

### System Architecture

[Figure 1](#ch55.xhtml#fig55_1) depicts the basic structure we intend to achieve finger-vein inputs are taken from the datasets and processed in MATLAB for authorization using deep learning algorithms such as Convolution neural network. This is sent to a microcontroller with power supply such as Arduino. This gives access to the IoT webpage and GSM using the ethernet shield which is casted upon the microcontroller and buzzer to activate for any of the fraudulent votes being casted.

 ![Fig. 1. System architecture](images/fig55_1_C.jpg)

[Fig. 1\. System architecture](#ch55.xhtml#R_fig55_1)

### Dataset

Images from verified and unverified users are included in the dataset which are nearly about 200+ images with both left and right images of the sample users. Whether or not the user is verified is taken into account when labeling these images.

A training set and a testing set were then created from the dataset. The CNN model was trained using the training set, which includes 80% of the images. The performance of the trained model was assessed using the testing set, which includes 20% of the images.

![Fig. 2. Dataset samples of finger-vein](images/fig55_2_B.jpg)

Fig. 2\. Dataset samples of finger-vein

Link: [https://wwvv.kaggle.com/datasets/ryeltsin/finger-vein](https://wwvv.kaggle.com)

### Features of the Dataset

1.  Vein Patterns: This includes the arrangement, orientation, and size of the veins in the fingerprint.
2.  Intensity values: This can include the brightness and darkness of the veins, which can be used to differentiate between different regions in the fingerprint.
3.  Texture features: This can include measures of the roughness, smoothness, and regularity of the veins, which can be used to distinguish between different types of fingerprints.
4.  Wavelet transforms: This can include the decomposition of the fingerprint vein data into different frequency components, which can provide additional information about the underlying patterns in the data and so on.

#### Way of Approach

*   Data collection: An infrared camera is used to take pictures of the finger veins, which are then saved as a dataset.
*   Pre-processing: To reduce noise and improve the quality of the acquired images, filters like Gaussian, median, and average are applied.
*   ROI Extraction: By segmenting the vein pattern using the line tracking method, the region of interest (ROI) is extracted from the pre-processed image.
*   Feature extraction: Gabor filters, local binary patterns (LBP), and histograms of oriented gradients are some of the filters that are applied after the ROI has been extracted to extract features (HOG).
*   Classification: A CNN model is trained for classification using the extracted features. An assortment of verified and unverified users are used to train the CNN model. The test images are then categorized as verified or unverified using the trained CNN model.

## Results and Analysis

The first step in preprocessing is to turn the color images into grayscale. This conversion increases contrast while reducing image data size, which can help the feature extraction algorithm perform better. The overall brightness of the image can be changed using the brightness adjustment technique. The contrast of the image may be improved, which may help the vein patterns stand out more clearly.

Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram equalization (CLAHE) is a method that uses histogram equalization to enhance the contrast by breaking the image up into smaller sub-regions.

Image noise can be eliminated using the non-linear filtering method known as median filtering. By using median filtering, each pixel’s value is changed to correspond to that of its surrounding pixels. This method can be used to reduce noise in finger vein images and enhance the visibility of the vein patterns.

Processing finger vein images for feature extraction and classification requires important steps like edge detection and segmentation as in [Fig. 6](#ch55.xhtml#fig55_6). Edge detection is the process of locating the borders between various areas of an image that could be veins or other structures. These algorithms highlight edges and other regions with a strong gradient or change in pixel values.

![Fig. 6. Edge detection and Segmentation](images/fig55_6_B.jpg)

[Fig. 6\. Edge detection and Segmentation](#ch55.xhtml#R_fig55_6)

Here, Segmentation is the process of dividing an image into various areas or objects based on their traits or characteristics. Segmentation can be used to separate the veins in finger vein images from the surrounding tissue or other structures. Techniques like thresholding, region growing, or clustering can be used for this.

![Fig. 7. Vein extraction frequency graph](images/fig55_7_C.jpg)

Fig. 7\. Vein extraction frequency graph

The graph that is produced can be used to determine the threshold grey value that distinguishes the vein region from the surrounding area. The image can be processed further using this threshold, such as by segmenting it or extracting its features. Overall, the vein extraction frequency graph provides a simple and effective way to identify the ROI in finger vein images, allowing for accurate and reliable vein extraction and recognition.

 ![Fig. 8. Success rate graph](images/fig55_8_C.jpg)

Fig. 8\. Success rate graph

The accuracy of the suggested system is represented by a graph with success rate on the y-axis and the label on the x-axis. The number of images that were correctly classified is divided by the total number of images in the dataset to determine the success rate or accuracy.

The success rate is plotted against various labels or dataset categories on the graph. The labels in this project are users who have been verified and those who have not. The accuracy of the system’s classification of images under each label will be displayed on the graph.

The predictive error of classification models is measured by classification loss functions. A lower loss indicates a better predictive model when the same type of loss is compared across numerous models. Think about the situation that follows. The weighted average classification loss is denoted by L.

## Conclusion and Future Work

In conclusion, this project suggests a safe and private voting system that makes use of deep learning methods and finger vein recognition. Finger vein images from verified and unverified users make up the system’s dataset, and a CNN model is used for feature extraction and classification. An IoT-based alert system that can quickly alert authorities to any potential fraud activity is integrated into the proposed system.

The integration of the IoT-based alert system further improves the proposed system’s accuracy in classifying finger vein images as verified or unverified, according to experimental results. The system’s success rate is determined by how well it can distinguish between verified and unverified users based on the images of their finger veins.

The primary benefit of the suggested system is its capacity to offer voters a private and anonymous voting process. The implementation of a secure and reliable voting system is made possible by the use of finger vein recognition and deep learning techniques, which offers an accurate and dependable method for authentication.

Future work may involve enhancing the CNN model’s accuracy and incorporating other cutting-edge deep learning methods to optimize the performance of the suggested system. Additionally, by creating a user-friendly interface and integrating it with current voting systems, the system’s usability and user experience can be enhanced.

# Cryptocurrency Price Prediction Using LSTM and RNN Techniques

Raguru Madhan,[^(43)](#fn43)

Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Hindustan Institute of Technology and Science, Chennai, India

E-mail: [tharun29072001@gmail.coml](mailto:tharun29072001@gmail.coml); [johndp@hindustanuniv.ac.in](mailto:johndp@hindustanuniv.ac.in); [jaravindhar@hindustanuniv.ac.in](mailto:jaravindhar@hindustanuniv.ac.in);

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-56](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-56)

## Abstract

The use of cryptocurrency has been steadily increasing in recent years. Cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin (BTC), Litecoin (LTC), and Ethereum (ETH) are currently a thriving open-source community and payment network used by millions of people. As the value of these cryptocurrency prices varies every day, technically it would be difficult to predict the buying and selling prices, at the same time investors must forecast the cryptocurrency pricing on a daily basis. Existing techniques for predicting cryptocurrency values use Convolution neural networks (CNN) which are suitable for classification, and might produce suboptimal accuracies in prediction when working with sequential data. Recurrent neural network (RNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) are used in this work to obtain more accurate and efficient price prediction. This work considers Mean Squared Error (MSE) matrix as the metric to evaluate the quality of predictions. The RNN algorithm is implemented in the first layer of LSTM. The algorithm is implemented using streamlit library in Python fetching live data from yahoo finance cryptocurrency data. The algorithm produces better accuracy when compared with the existing models.

Keywords: Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum(ETH), Long Term Short Memory (LSTM), Mean Squared Error (MSE), Recurrent neural network (RNN).

## Introduction

Many uncertainties influence cryptocurrency coin prices, including political issues, economic issues, and natural disasters ([Ibrahim, 2020](#ch56.xhtml#ref56_1)). These are the primary causes of the high volatility in the day-to-day price. To solve this problem regarding the fluctuations in the prices there is a need of a model to make accurate and efficient predictions that help the investors to gain certain knowledge over the drastic changes in the prices so that they can move their investments towards profits. In the cryptocurrency financial services sector, blockchain technology is frequently referred to as distributed ledger technology ([Chinnasamy et al., 2021](#ch56.xhtml#ref56_5)).

Cryptocurrency price data is a time series that changes over time. As a result, predicting the price of cryptocurrency is difficult. The model is implemented with LSTM and RNN. The RNN algorithm has the capability to store the previous data and it uses that data to predict present prices. The LSTM model provides more memory support to the RNN.

Existing model has less accuracy because of using CNNs ( [Pokhrel et al., 2022](#ch56.xhtml#ref56_4); [Kang et al., 2022](#ch56.xhtml#ref56_6); [Cavalli and Amoretti, 2021](#ch56.xhtml#ref56_11)). Sequential data, on the other hand, such as time series, audio, or text, are one-dimensional and lack the same spatial structure. Due to this applying CNN directly to the sequential data may not always give results in optimal performance.

RNN is a feed-forward neural network that was created to predict sequence problems by analyzing continuous changes in patterns. RNN has a feature that if it produces an output, this result is fed back into the memory of RNN’s hidden layer to make the next prediction, This makes RNN more accurate in the sequence prediction ([Pant et al., 2018](#ch56.xhtml#ref56_14); [Chinnasamy et al., 2023](#ch56.xhtml#ref56_2)). LSTM is a popular deep-learning technique in RNN for time series prediction. It has four layers: an input layer, a hidden layer, a cell state layer, and an output layer.

### Implementation

Using the Bitcoin, Litecoin, **and** Ethereum data, this code aims to predict the crypto closing price. Code starts by importing the necessary libraries and then preparing the raw data for training the model. Data is normalized by using min max scaler. Implementing the LSTM model for predicting cryptocurrencies prices and the model gets trained and tested with dataset ( [Nivethitha and Raharitha, 2019](#ch56.xhtml#ref56_8); [Pokhrel et al., 2022](#ch56.xhtml#ref56_4); [Loginova et al., 2021](#ch56.xhtml#ref56_15)). The LSTM model is run on the dataset with sequential and clear\_session functions.

The LSTM model performance is tested with the mean square error values, if the value of test MSE less means the prediction of the model is more accurate. The gen\_test\_pred\_frame function generates a test prediction data frame for the cryptocurrency closing price. The code then creates two plots using the generated test prediction dataframe ([Yiying and Yeze, 2019](#ch56.xhtml#ref56_3); [Madan et al., 2015](#ch56.xhtml#ref56_9)). The first plot depicts the predicted and true BTC, LTC, and ETH closing prices.

The data set values low, high, open, and close are similar. A number used to measure the strength of a link is the correlation coefficient. A value for the coefficient between -1 and 1 is possible. If the value -1 means it will have a negative correlation. If the value 0 means do not have a relationship with each other. If the value 1 means the variables correlate Eq. (1).

(1)  
$$r\_{xy} = \\frac{\\sum^{}(x\_{i} - \\overline{x})(y\_{i} - \\overline{y})}{\\sqrt{\\sum^{}{(x\_{i} - \\overline{x})}^{2}\\text{Σ}{(y\_{i} - \\overline{y})}^{2}}}$$  

The variance, mean, and covariance of a stationary series do not evolve eq.(2). Where *y[t]* denotes the value at the time instant t and E term denotes the error. To calculate *y[t]* it needs the value of *y*[*t*\-1].

Mean Squared Error, training accuracy, and validation accuracy are the metrics eq.(3) used to assess the effectiveness of the proposed cryptocurrency price prediction model. The difference between a variable’s observed and expected values, squared, is what is referred to as the mean square error.

### Algorithm

Step 1: Import the necessary modules and libraries, including matplotlib, MinMaxScaler, Keras, TensorFlow, Numpy, and Pandas.

Step 2: The cryptocurrency data are imported from yahoo finance into a pandas DataFrame with the date, open, close, volume, and symbol columns selected.

Step 3: Train the raw data with limits input, starts, cutsoff using pandas models dropna() and indexs for mapping the required data from the data sets.

Step 4: The data in the data set is normalized, with the MinMaxScalar function the range is set for (0,1) and the input raw data reshape into (-1,1).

Step 5: The Long Short Term Model is implemented for making the raw data in seq\_lengths which takes the raw values and input values for positioning the data.

Step 6: Yahoo finance contains cryptocurrency data. A list of cryptocurrency names that the function will use to generate predictions. The date on which the data will be divided into training and testing sets. Seq\_length() returns the sequence length to be used by the LSTM model.

Step 7: The gen\_train\_test\_data function is called with the input\_data, start\_date, and train\_test\_cutoffparameters to categorize the data into training and testing sets.

Step 8: Shape data for LSTM model: The shape\_for\_lstm function is called on X\_train, X\_test, Y\_train, and Y\_test to reshape the data into the format expected by the LSTM model.

Step 9: The Adam optimizer and mean squared error loss are utilized to construct the model. The mean squared error is the metric to monitor during training.

Step 10: The fit method is called on the model with X\_train and Y\_train as inputs. The batch\_size parameter is set to 1 to process each training sequence individually. The epochs parameter is set to 50 to train the model for 50 iterations.

Step 11:The predict method is called on the model with X\_test as input to make predictions on the testing data.

# A Study on Cybernated Watermarking Approach on Image With Cryptographic Encryption

Ms. R. Sivasankari,^([^(44)](#fn44))

E-mail: [shankarirathnam@gmail.com](mailto:shankarirathnam@gmail.com), [afraanmiza@gmail.com](mailto:afraanmiza@gmail.com), [blesslinjaffy@gmail.com](mailto:blesslinjaffy@gmail.com), [ayamini2003@gmail.com](mailto:ayamini2003@gmail.com)

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-57](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-57)

## Abstract

In recent years, digital watermarking of interactive media content has become an active experimentation area. In addition to reviewing some of the techniques for multiple media types that have been developed, a general framework for watermark engrafting and identification is described. We emphasize few of these application-oriented distinctions, some of them are copyright protection, substantiation, tamper detection, and data hiding, as well the technological and system prerequisite for various media kinds, such as digital photos, digital files, digital audio, and text. In this approach, we outline a general structure for digital watermarking-based image copyright protection. In this paper, we specifically outline the key components of an effective watermarking scheme, talk about concerns with robustness, and outline the key phases of tide marking mechanism.

Keywords: Robustness, Copyrights, Data Hiding, Confidentiality, Embed, Encryption, Recovery

## Introduction

In this paper, we have discussed that digitalized watermarking is an enclosing procedure of a unique imperceptible identifier into digital media such as images, videos, audio, or documents. The objective of a digital tidemark is to recognize and protect the ownership and integrity of the digital content. A digital watermark can take various forms, including visible or invisible text, images, logos, or a combination of these elements. The watermark is added to the digital media during the creation process or after it has been created using specialized software ([Sisaudia and Vishwakarma, 2021](#ch57.xhtml#ref57_8)). Digital watermarking is commonly used to prevent copyright infringement, piracy, and unauthorized use of digital media. It can also be used for tracking and monitoring the distribution and usage of digital content. Watermarks can be designed to survive various forms of manipulation or transformation, such as compression, cropping, or resizing, and can be used to identify the original source of the content. Overall, digital watermarking provides a way to protect the rights of creators and owners of digital content and to make sure the reliability and integrity of the content ([Wang et al., 2022](#ch57.xhtml#ref57_4)). However, for the protection of copyright, traceability for anti-counterfeiting purposes, and information integrity, digital watermarking is widely used. Traditional watermarking methods could alter the originality of the image permanently. Reversible Watermarking (RW) is suggested as a way to recover the refuge image and extract the hidden communication ([Dong et al., 2022](#ch57.xhtml#ref57_5)), and it is receiving more and more attention. A digital watermark can contain information about the owner of the digital content, such as their name or copyright information. This can help identify the owner of the content and prove ownership in case of copyright infringement. In case of copyright infringement, digital watermarks can be used as evidence in court. By proving ownership and the presence of a watermark, the owner can prove that the content was taken or utilized without permission. Overall, digital watermarking is an important tool in copyright infringement and can help deter unauthorized use and distribution of digital content. It can also help protect the rights of content creators and owners and ensure that they receive proper compensation for their work. The reversibility of the cover canvas in the watermarking strategy can be achieved using a variety of techniques, such as lossless compression ([Dong et al., 2022](#ch57.xhtml#ref57_5)), histogram shifting ([Hespanhol et al., 2021](#ch57.xhtml#ref57_9)), robust reversible watermarking ([Xing et al., 2022](#ch57.xhtml#ref57_3)), compression strategy \[[13](#ch57.xhtml#ref57_13)\], and event-triggered dynamic watermarking approach ([Xiao et al., 2022](#ch57.xhtml#ref57_1)). To resolve this issue, two fish algorithms are designed.

In recent research trends of digital data security, the robustness of different algorithms and methods was used. The ability of watermarking to sustain non-malicious image analysis operations such as compression, filtration, etc., is termed as robustness ([Xiao et al., 2022](#ch57.xhtml#ref57_1)). That is, even in the presence of various attacks, the watermark extraction algorithm can obtain proper watermark extraction from watermarked images. However, semi-fragile watermarks share some traits with both robust and fragile watermarks.

## Advantages of Digital Watermarking

Digitalise watermarking is the process of encapsulating a unique identifier, such as a code or image, into digital content to protect it from unauthorized use or distribution. Some of the advantages of digital watermarking include:

**Copyright Protection:** Digital watermarking can help protect the copyright of digital content such as images, music, and videos, by making it more difficult for others to use or distribute it without permission ([Wang et al., 2022](#ch57.xhtml#ref57_4)).

**Branding:** Digital watermarking can be used as a branding tool to promote a company’s products or services ([Dong et al., 2022](#ch57.xhtml#ref57_5)). For example, a company logo can be embedded into digital content, such as a video or image, to help promote the brand.

**Tracking and Identification:** Digital watermarking can be used to track and identify the origin of digital content (Xiao et al.., 2022). This can be useful for tracking the distribution of copyrighted material or for tracking the use of a company’s digital assets.

**Authentication:** Digital watermarking can be used to authenticate the source and integrity of digital content ([Ding et al., 2022](#ch57.xhtml#ref57_6)). This can be useful for ensuring that digital content has not been tampered with or altered in any way.

**Evidence in Legal Proceedings:** Digital watermarking can provide evidence in legal proceedings, such as copyright infringement cases, by proving the ownership of digital content and its unauthorized use ([Gong et al., (2021](#ch57.xhtml#ref57_11))\].

Overall, digital watermarking provides a powerful tool for protecting digital content and can be used to provide a range of benefits to individuals and businesses.

## Disadvantages of Digital Watermarking

While digital watermarking has many advantages, it also has some disadvantages. Some of the potential drawbacks of digital watermarking include:

**Reduction in Quality:** Embedding a digital watermark into an image or video can sometimes reduce the quality of the content, depending on the type and intensity of the watermark \[[3](#ch57.xhtml#ref57_3)\]. This can result in a degradation of the user experience, which can negatively impact the perception of the content.

**Vulnerability to Removal:** Digital watermarks can be removed by individuals with sufficient knowledge and tools \[[7](#ch57.xhtml#ref57_7)\], which can render them ineffective as a means of copyright protection or tracking.

**Complexity:** Embedding digital watermarks can be a complex process, requiring specialized software and expertise ([Hosny et al., 2021](#ch57.xhtml#ref57_10)). This can make it difficult for individuals or organizations to implement, especially if they lack the necessary resources.

**False Positives:** Digital watermarking algorithms may occasionally produce false positives, identifying content as infringing when it is not ([Ding et al., 2022](#ch57.xhtml#ref57_6)). This can result in legitimate use of content being incorrectly flagged as unauthorized, which can negatively impact users and businesses.

**Cost:** Implementing digital watermarking can involve costs, including the purchase of software or services and the training of personnel. This can be a significant barrier for smaller businesses or individuals ([Du et al., 2023](#ch57.xhtml#ref57_2)).

Overall, digital watermarking can be a useful tool for protecting digital content, but it is not without its limitations and potential drawbacks.

# A Survey on Implementation and Development of AES Cryptography Algorithm In Various Fields

S. Giridharan,^([^(45)](#fn45))

## Abstract

Cryptography is a way of using secure communications techniques that provide confidentiality and allow only the sender and intended recipient of a message to view its content. Given the prevalence of the internet, regular internet users must remain aware of cyber security issues. Nevertheless, most individuals lack the essential knowledge of how cryptography is used in passwords and other online contexts. AES, DES, and Triple-DES are only a few of the many algorithms that are presently available for encrypting data, but it is still necessary to enhance the current algorithms to guard against potential attacks on encrypted data. The current Advanced Encryption Standard algorithm’s benefits and drawbacks are discussed in detail, as well as how it affects data security in numerous industries.

**Keyword:** Encryption, Decryption, Cryptography, AES, Cipher

## Introduction

Security is the current top priority. Cryptography is crucial in the field of security. While the development and implementation of Advanced Encryption Standard algorithms in major domains are numerous, AES is implemented in both hardware and software fields to encrypt and secure various data. Every algorithm in cryptography has two sections. Encryption and Decryption. The act of converting plaintext to cipher text is termed encryption, while the process of converting cipher text back to plain text is termed decryption. The reason behind choosing cryptography in our survey is to create awareness among the general audience, who are unaware of the cyber attacks happening around them. The attackers steal the information without the authorized user’s knowledge, and the information is transferred without any kind of protection. On the other hand, the reason for choosing the AES cryptography algorithm is that it is more secure when compared to the DES (Data Encryption Standard), Triple-DES, etc., cryptography algorithms. The AES algorithm can never be cracked by a brute force attack (Brute force resistance). The number of transformation rounds required to convert plaintext into cipher text in AES encryption depends on the key size used. For a 128-bit key size, 10 rounds are needed; for a 192-bit key size, 12 rounds are required, and for a 256-bit key size, 14 rounds are necessary.

The AES includes:

1.  Key Expansion
2.  First-round key addition:
    
    *   Add Round Key
    *   9, 11, or 13 Rounds: Depending on the key size, the data is processed via a specific number of rounds. The following four stages are included in each round:
    *   Sub Bytes: A corresponding byte from a substitution table is used to replace each byte of the data.
    *   Shift Rows: The data’s rows have various levels of translation.
    *   Mix Columns: A matrix multiplication is used to change each data column.
    *   Add Round Key: The data is updated with the round key for the current round.
    *   Last Round: The Mix Columns step is not present in the final round, although it is comparable to the earlier rounds.
    *   The encrypted data is the outcome of the last round. The same procedure is used in reverse order to decrypt the data using the same key.

These different rounds, key sizes, and methods produce distinct and complex keys that are strong enough to secure resources. AES is also flexible for development and produces or enhances different varieties in its algorithm, which makes AES dynamic.

## Literature Survey

[Altigani et al., (2021](#ch58.xhtml#ref58_1)) proposed an effective, score-based, key-dependent P-AES algorithm of key avalanche as 0.496 and plaintext avalanche as 0.504. This methodology satisfied all NIST-recommended Statistical Test Suite (STS) criteria. The purpose of this proposal was to replace AES’ static properties and replace them with dynamic encryption. By manipulating the sub-bytes, shifting rows, mixing columns, and making it key-dependent, an Advanced Encryption Standard polymorphic variation was created. After implementing this algorithm, polymorphism was achieved and will not affect interoperability. As a result, cipher text can function in 128 distinct keys. There is a negligible difference in performance between the proposed P-AES and the standard AES.

Yendamury & Mohankumar (2021)proposed a Defense in Depth strategy on AES employing logic locking at the system level techniques. The lock blocks on AES are inserted in a subprocess of the AES decryption algorithm. The achieved output was 70% when an incorrect password was provided at the input. Three types of decryption algorithms are used depending on key size, and Key sizes of 128, 192, and 256 bits are supported by AES. The input text data size always remains at 128 bits. Insert logic lock blocks into corresponding sub-processes such as (1) inverse shift row, (2) reverse substitution byte, (3) add round key, and (4) reverse mix column. The analysis of Hamming distance, Levenshtein distance, and Jaro distance inferred that the output text is entirely corrupted with distances greater than 80%, 80%, and 50%, respectively. This technique provides flexibility to brute force, reverse engineering, and key sensitization assaults.

[Kumar et al., (2022](#ch58.xhtml#ref58_3)) proposed better protection of media transfers over social media and other modes of transfer. The implementation of this proposed work is a combination of steganography and cryptography to secure the information from unapproved access. To protect the information, the output obtained must have low Mean Square Error (MSE) and high Point Signal To Noise Ratio (PSNR) values. These values help in the better hiding of data in a media file, irrespective of its file format. In the suggested work, the MSE and PSNR values are improved when compared to the previous proposals. The PSNR value is 75.1375, while the MSE value is 0.0019922. from the proposed work. whereas the MSE and PSNR values from the previous proposed works are not even close to the work proposed here.

[Mohammad & Abdullah, (2022](#ch58.xhtml#ref58_4)) improved, developed, and proposed a Lightweight Cryptography algorithm (LWC) to increase the embedded systems’ and limited devices’ security. The enhancement of the AES algorithm was done by reducing the computation power of the algorithm and improving the cryptographic performance of constraint devices. In this procedure, which protects all types of data, the suggested technique was quick and lightweight. The mathematical fraction, or continuous fraction to compress, was used to process the ciphertext, making it more difficult and speeding up data transfer in the process. As compared to AES, the LWC-AES proved far more appropriate for speedy encryption and decryption. The computational power of the proposed algorithm was also less than the memory capacity of the Central Processing Unit (CPU). Together, the proposed algorithm is directly proportional to high security. On various platforms, the code for the LWC-AES text data type is fast and compact, with the programming result of the proposed algorithm being: idle CPU usage of 348.7 ms, memory size of 24 bytes, RAM size of 326 bytes, code size of 587 bytes, and bandwidth of 2.665 Mbps.

In this paper, [Reis et al., (2022](#ch58.xhtml#ref58_5))propose IMCRYPTO, an in-memory computing (IMC) fabric for accelerating AES. In order to perform encryption and decryption in a single-hardware architecture with merged sub-bytes and mix-column processes, this article uses a unique technique with a unified structure. A modular Look-Up Table (LUT) fabric is designed by utilizing consecutive arrangement and high parallelism provided by several Random Access Memory (RAM) and Random Access/Content Addressable Memory (RA/CAM) arrays, along with specialized encoders. Without compromising space or power use, the suggested LUT fabric offers high throughput encryption and decoding. Integration with RISC-V enabled the flexibility of performing different modes of operation.

[Chung et al., (2022](#ch58.xhtml#ref58_6)) proposed Grover’s algorithm here for implementation of AES with the help of S-box (Substitution box). By using the substitution approach, the S-box substitution procedure converts the 48-bit input from the XOR operation, which contains the compressed key and extended RPT, into a 32-bit output. As compared to other ways, the group’s solution in this proposal makes use of the fewest qubits, greatly lowering its T-depth. A total of 8 S-boxes are used in order to get the output where the values of the S-box are calculated using the formula GF(2⁸)=GF(2)\[x\]/(x⁸+x⁴+x³+x+1). When an oracle adds a negative phase to the solution states, Grover’s procedure resolves it. To be more precise, given every state in the computational foundation. The entry that corresponds to the indicated item in this oracle will have a negative phase. It will be a diagonal matrix.

[Bedoui et al., (2022](#ch58.xhtml#ref58_7)) proposed an efficient fault detection method for the AES algorithm. This approach was suggested regardless of how the S-Box and inverse S-box were constructed. The AES round design consisted of three pieces with two pipeline registers inserted in between to increase fault coverage. The proposed approach is designed to be compatible with different AES sizes, including AES-128, AES-192, and AES-256. The effectiveness of this approach was tested through fault injection simulations in VHDL to validate its ability to detect issues. The developed method can find 99.339 percent of randomly introduced mistakes. This paper’s main objective is to provide an AES implementation that is trustworthy, strong, and resistant to fault injection threats.

[Kolate & Joshi (2021](#ch58.xhtml#ref58_8))proposed DNA-based security techniques as an information carrier. By integrating the advantages of both DNA-based and cryptographic AES, the new data-security approach may be put into practice. This offers many layers of protection. DNA cryptography is presented as an efficient encryption technique, which confirms non-vulnerable communication. Compression methods can be used with DNA cryptography and AES to secure sensitive data, such as military data. DNA cryptography is advantageous and advancing quickly, as evidenced by the employment of the four DNA bases (A, T, G, and C) to encrypt communications and boost performance in terms of parallelism and storage capacity.

[Jang et al., (2022](#ch58.xhtml#ref58_9)) proposed a Quantum computing analysis that enhances the resistance of secret key ciphers against a strong quantum opponent. This key recovery attack applies the Grovers algorithm’s quantum key search on three different AES variants (128, 192, and 256) in order to retrieve the key. As a consequence, it demonstrates improvement in the implementation pool and a decrease in the quantum costs for the AES variants across a variety of metrics.

[Mane & Mulani (2018](#ch58.xhtml#ref58_10))proposed The AES algorithm is implemented quickly and securely on an FPGA (fast programmable gate array).

Advanced encryption algorithms are one type of cryptographic algorithm that is used to improve the security of system data and protect it from unauthorized access. (a matrix-based programming language used to analyze and design the system), and the balance algorithm is designed using Xilinx SysGen, a Simulink add-on that enables the architecture level of FPGA designs using graphical block programming. Hence, at a maximum working frequency of 1102.536 MHz, the system only makes use of 121 slice registers. Moreover, the suggested system has a throughput of 14.1125 GB/s.

## Conclusion

Data breaches and data theft are the major and most important security threats emerging in every organization, which pave the way for cryptography’s implementation and development for securing various resources. Because of its flexibility and exponentially stronger key than DES and Triple-DES, one of the cryptography algorithms called AES is the one that is most commonly employed in a variety of areas. AES can be modified and transformed into a newly proposed algorithm, such as Defense in Depth, a system-level approach, and its polymorphic property transforms AES into a dynamic structure that can be combined as a hybrid structure in the field of AI. AES has also been used in many fields, such as telecommunications, data transactions, quantum analysis, memory computing, information security (DNA-based AES), and so on. This ensures that the AES can be one of the best algorithms for securing data and resources in every field.

# A Survey on Alerting Using Honeyword System

Mr. E. Rajkumar,^([^(46)](#fn46))

## Abstract

A security method called Honeywords is used to identify and stop website password assaults. This method involves including honeywords, or fictitious passwords, along with genuine passwords in a website. A warning is sent to the website administrator about a possible security breach if a hacker accesses the database and tries to utilize a honeyword. This technique is helpful because it makes it harder for hackers to distinguish between legitimate passwords and false ones, decreasing the occurrence of an attack. In order to construct multi-layered protection against password attacks, honeywords can be used in conjunction with other security measures. Overall, honeywords offer a practical solution to strengthen the backend security of a website and safeguard critical user information. Due to the rise in cyber attacks, honey words have become more common as a security solution. Internet security is still seriously threatened by password attacks, but Honeywords can help by strengthening the defenses already in place.

Keywords: Passwords, Honeywords, Legacy UI, Honey encryption, Honey-checker, Salting, Sweetword

## Introduction

For years, passwords have been the standard practice for protecting internet accounts, but they have their own set of issues. Password theft is a significant problem that can occur through phishing or hacking. Once a password has been compromised, it can be used to steal identities or obtain illegal access to confidential data. A promising strategy being investigated by researchers in recent years for safeguarding internet accounts is the use of “honeywords.” Honeywords are fictitious passwords that are made to feel and look authentic but are actually fraudulent. The purpose of this technique is to make it so that a hacker who obtains a password will be unable to determine which one is the actual password and will therefore be I was unable to access the account. The idea of honeywords, how they function, and why they could be an effective tool in the battle against cybercrime are all covered in this article.

Although the usage of honeywords is a relatively new idea, the cybersecurity world has already expressed a lot of interest in it. The fact that honeywords give an extra layer of security without forcing users to remember complicated passwords or go through additional authentication stages is one explanation for this. Moreover, honeywords are a quick and affordable way to increase account security because they can be simply implemented into current authentication systems. The fundamental idea behind Honeywords is straightforward: if a hacker acquires a password database, they won’t be able to distinguish between actual and bogus passwords. They will have to try several passwords before they find the right one, which makes it much more difficult for them to log in to an account. This not only gives the account an additional degree of security but also serves as an early warning system for attacks. Also, users may not be able to tell the difference between genuine and fraudulent passwords, which raises questions about how they may respond to the use of honeywords. In conclusion, honeywords are a cutting-edge method of protecting online accounts that may add an extra layer of protection against hackers. The advantages of honeywords make them a viable instrument in the battle against cybercrime, notwithstanding the difficulties still associated with their application. We’re likely to see further advancements in this area as technology advances because the cybersecurity community is constantly looking for fresh and inventive solutions to protect our online accounts.

This method has drawn interest as a potentially effective means of safeguarding user data and preventing illegal access to backend systems. We will delve more into the idea of honeywords in this post, covering their operation, advantages, and any potential implementation difficulties. We will also look at some actual implementations of Honeywords and provide some helpful advice for website owners who want to use this method to increase security.

## Methods & Techniques

\[[1](#ch59.xhtml#ref59_1)\] This paper intends to provide accurate cryptanalysis of an IoT framework’s keyword system. Although integrating a password as an authentication element in an IoT framework has many benefits, it frequently inherits the security flaws of password-based authentication. Several of these flaws might be fixed by using honeyword-based authentication. While combining the honeyword protocol with the IoT infrastructure, careful design approach is required. This study contributes reference to the next two main goals in this way. This study shows that the researchers are continuously working to create a honeyword-based strategy that satisfies the requirements from both the security and usability viewpoints. Before anyone chooses the way to safeguard an organization’s password file, they must have a greater understanding of its security (and usability) standard.

\[[2](#ch59.xhtml#ref59_2)\] **Security analysis:** The suggested model offers defense against insider attacks in addition to password guessing assaults, which are both taken into account in the conventional aPAKE security model. By recognizing the similarity between the genuine and honey session keys, it can also identify password leaks. Compared to both Honeyword mechanism and aPAKE, this solution can provide more security. In the event of an authentication server compromise, HPAKE’s security is greater than Password-over-TLS utilizing OPAQUE because it can identify password leaks. In terms of defense against insider threats and password-guessing attacks, HPAKE is equal to OPAQUE. Our HPAKE technique uses honey words generated during the registration process to produce the user’s private and public keys. The server then stores both the honey public key and the genuine public key. The key exchange technique is used by the server to generate numerous session keys using the users’ different public keys during authentication. To find password violations, the server then determines whether the client is using the real session key or a honey session key. By decrypting the cipher text of the user’s initial Honeyword private key, our concept uses Honey encryption to produce user-specific Honeyword private keys. Our HPAKE system’s fundamental advantage is its ability to generate multiple session keys on the server while using the same ciphertext for both the real password and the honeywords, obviating the need for numerous OPAQUE output instances.

\[[3](#ch59.xhtml#ref59_3)\] **Legacy-LH password changes:** A important **term** used by the system is “Token,” which describes a group of letters that can be regarded as a single logical unit. A password’s “pattern” is made up of the different token combinations that it contains. The frequency of a token or password pattern in the password database is measured by the number of times it appears there. The system doesn’t keep track of the length of the alphabets and numbers, but it does keep track of the length of special characters in order to produce honeywords that are identical to a user’s actual password. As a result, the pattern representation adds “S” as a subscript to the special character’s length. By integrating specific information from the user’s profile and ensuring that it meets the minimal separation requirement from the actual password, honeywords are produced. The creation of various sets of tokens based on input from the user, such as: B. Strings of letters, Strings of digits, and Special Characters, is one way to generate honeywords. The components of each token set are then merged to create potential honeyword combinations. If a user profile-related substring appears in the password, this strategy is especially helpful. As a result, this method generates honeywords that are challenging to identify from the majority of user passwords.

\[[4](#ch59.xhtml#ref59_4)\] The password manager hashes the user’s entered password and generates a collection of honeywords that closely resemble the original password when a user registers and creates a username and master password. These honey words act as a signal to identify and stop intrusion by outsiders. OTP encryption, which encrypts all user app credentials, adds an additional layer of protection because the password manager holds the passwords for other programs and websites. When logging in, the password manager provides a login screen for the user to enter their details and allows three login attempts. The password manager uses OTP to decrypt the app passwords and grants access if the hashed master password given by the user matches the hashed master password that is already stored. After that, the user is sent to their account page, which contains all of their passwords. The password manager will recognize unauthorized access if a hacker tries to input one of the honeywords and route them to a phone lock password page. This keeps the app passwords OTP protected and secure while deceiving the hacker into thinking they have access to a legitimate account. The user’s account will be disabled and the program will end if they attempt more than three times without entering a valid honeyword. In order to defend against brute force attacks, the encryption technique known as Honey Encryption (HE) creates a fake message that looks real to outsiders who enter the wrong key. The true meaning is carefully hidden. A password manager (PM) is a piece of software that uses a single master password to lock all of the user’s passwords and store them securely. Besides protecting passwords, PM also helps minimize instances where users mistype their password, promoting better password quality

\[[5](#ch59.xhtml#ref59_5)\] **User Registration: In order** to initiate the registration process, you must create a new user account that will serve as a database record describing the means by which you can verify your identity. You must demonstrate that your identity matches your user account in order to be verified. Users must enter specific details while enrolling in addition to their desired username and password.

**Encryption/decryption** Passwords are encrypted into unintelligible text using techniques in order to identify hackers. Afterward, ciphertext creation is done to create ciphertext that will be used in the next step.

**Adding salt ValuesA** further layer of security protection is added by appending certain salt values, often known as irrelevant data. This increases the password’s length, adding another level of security.

Fig. 1\. Working of the honeyword authentication

**Hash Function:** Hashing of the password is done as the input string is initially used as the password. The password is then calculated for length, and the string is then turned around. The reversed text is then transformed into a binary string and, depending on the length of the password, is subsequently padded with extra bits. In order to create a safe and distinctive hash value, this method entails numerous steps of translating and altering the password in different ways.

\[[6](#ch59.xhtml#ref59_6)\] The benefit of the real-password unrelated design method is that it prevents the attacker from quickly determining the real password from a single sweet word. Also, it makes it possible for honeywords to be generated with an equal frequency, making it harder for an attacker to figure out the genuine password. Nevertheless, this approach makes it difficult to use probabilistic password models, and major adjustments must be made during the design and evaluation phases. When the attacker is aware of the user registration sequence, these alterations are considerably more difficult because it complicates the honeyword generating process. We have created four distinct honeyword generation techniques, each with its own special set of protection mechanisms, to solve these difficulties. To determine the most reliable honeyword technique, we extensively analyzed these strategies and compared their efficacy in various attack scenarios. Overall, our method of honeyword production has a lot of advantages over conventional ones. We have made it harder for attackers to guess real passwords even when they have in-depth knowledge of the user registration process by using real-password-unrelated design and creating various honeyword techniques.

## Conclusion

We conclude that the honeywords system has been demonstrated to be a beneficial and successful tool for increasing security measures across a variety of fields. Businesses and organizations frequently use it because of its capacity to recognize and stop cyberattacks like brute force, phishing, and password guessing. The capacity of the Honeywords system to generate dummy passwords and notify security staff instantly when an attempt is made to access them is a key benefit. In high-risk industries like finance, healthcare, and government where data breaches can have serious repercussions, this method is very helpful. Notwithstanding its advantages, the Honeywords system needs to be combined with additional security precautions to offer complete defense against cyberattacks. In general, the honeywords strategy is a hopeful remedy for the data breaches

# A Study on IoT Based Road Safety and Traffic Management

N. Jagadeesh^([^(47)](#fn47))

Email: [kavithad.mca@spiher.ac.in](mailto:kavithad.mca@spiher.ac.in)

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-60](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-60)

## Abstract

The IoT has a bigger important in many fields in the current situation. In which road safety and traffic management is the most needed area for proper management of vehicles on road and also for the safety of the people. As there is less human power these IoT devices are incorporated for providing assistance for human beings with regard to usage. The more the usage, there arises a problem of reliability as these data helps to avoid accidents in road. In this paper, we discuss the various challenges and issues faced when IoT devices are used and also about the solutions to be considered when the issues occur in these devices when used for Road Safety and Traffic Management for providing the utmost safety for the drivers and pedestrians. Keywords: Io T, Road Safety, Pedestrians, Reliability

## Introduction

IoT is a collection of various sensors and components which are incorporated together for the process of making an object or device to work with less human interaction. Many sensors are incorporated to the IoT device in order to perform various tasks. In the case of road safety and traffic management, various sensors like (IR, ultrasonic, and accelerometer) are used for assisting drivers to avoid accidents in the road and help to provide the utmost safety for the pedestrians on the roads.

## IoT in Road Safety

The roads are the backbone for many countries as they connect with many other countries which helps in the development of the country. As there is a need for many there should be proper safety in roads. According to the WHO around 1.35 million people die every year due to road traffic accidents, and up to 50 million more suffer non-fatal injuries \[[1](#ch60.xhtml#ref60_1)\]. So there is a need for better vehicle management guiding the drivers for smooth operation of the vehicles.

*Connected Vehicles*

1.  Assists with the condition of the vehicle.
2.  Informs the drivers in case of overspeeding
3.  In case of medical emergency, details are sent to save lives.

These are being done by the sensors which are being incorporated into the vehicles.

## IoT in Traffic Management

Traffic plays a major role in many cities where the people are halted for many hours and many miles mainly during the peak hours or during festival times. It takes more time for crossing a small area which is a major issue in case of emergencies where ambulances and fire engines are supposed to move on in that area.

## Literature Survey

Fabio Arena and Giovanni Pau-An Overview of Vehicular Communications”, January 2019, Article in Future Internet “. This paper proposes ideas about how communication can be carried out between vehicle to vehicle, vehicle to infrastructure and vehicle to everything. It also gives a glimpse about the Intelligent Transport System how well it can work if the data is reliable.” ([Arena and Pau, 2019](#ch60.xhtml#ref60_2))

R. Sushmitha et al-Smart Roads System”, Vol. 2, Issue 7, July 2021, International Journal of Recent Advances in Multidisciplinary Topics. “This paper gives idea how to use the roads for pedestrian safety.” ([Sushmitha et al., 2021](#ch60.xhtml#ref60_3))

[Ning Lu et al. “Connected Vehicles: Solutions and Challenges,”](#ch60.xhtml#ref60_4) August 2014 IEEE Internet of Things Journal, This paper proposes an idea about wireless communication with vehicles, Infrastructure, etc. There is a need to check how efficient it is when compared to wired communication. In wireless, there arises a problem of too much information providing more workload for the users.” (Lu et al., 2014)

### Juan Guerrero-Ibariez et al.” [Sensor Technologies for Intelligent Transportation Systems,”](#ch60.xhtml#ref60_5) 2018, Multidisciplinary Digital Publishing Institute, This paper provides an overview of various sensors which can be incorporated with vehicles for Intelligent Traffic System” (Guerrero-Ibanez et al., 2018).

[Mubashir Murshed et al. An IoT Based Car Accident Prevention and Detection System with Smart Brake Control”](#ch60.xhtml#ref60_6) International Conference on Applications and Techniques in Information Science (iCATIS2019), 19-23 Jan 2019, Dhaka, Bangladesh “This paper gives information to the users with the email provided as soon as abnormal behavior detected. Even if the driver does not respond the sensors will make the actions to be carried on to the vehicles for effective movement” (Murshed et al., 2019)

[Naresh et al. (2020](#ch60.xhtml#ref60_7)). Smart Traffic management system using IOT “International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology (IJETT-Scopus Indexed) — Special Issues - ICT 2020” This paper proposes about smart traffic management and how to manage traffic in case of emergency vehicles passing through the traffic.

## Existing Issues

The various challenges and Issues being faced by road safety management are

1.  Frequent access:
    
    When there is a frequent movement of vehicles in junctions’ without any proper intimation to other vehicles and persons on the road.
    
2.  Inadequate Footpath:
    
    There is no proper footpath for pedestrians, which makes them to go through on the main road which leads to accidents
    
3.  No proper bus stops:
    
    There are no proper bus stops which makes the people to stand on the roads causing fatalities that result in severe injuries and death.
    
4.  Line marking in roads:
    
    As many roads do not have proper line markings to indicate the separation between both side of roads which causes overtaking of vehicles leading to accidents.
    
5.  Uncontrolled parking:
    
    The drivers parking the vehicles on either side of the road without proper indication lead to the crashing of vehicles which is approaching.
    
6.  No proper sign boards:
    
    With minimum and unfamiliar signboard marking the vehicle drivers and pedestrians face the issue regarding the understanding of the sign boards which proves to be an issue for causing accidents.
    
7.  No proper speed control:
    
    The drivers lack speed control which makes them go through rash driving which leads to crashing with the vehicles and pedestrians.
    
8.  Usage of Alcoholic substances:
    
    The usage of various alcoholic substances during driving makes drivers drive in a rash manner causing accidents \[[8](#ch60.xhtml#ref60_8)\].
    

The various challenges and Issues being faced by traffic management are

1.  Usage of Old traffic signals:
    
    The outdated traffic signals are still being used in various places even if it is worn out causing malfunctioning of the traffic lights.
    
2.  No proper manpower
    
    There is a lack of traffic in charges that are to be available near traffic signals to assist the vehicle commuters for smooth crossing of vehicles in signals.
    
3.  Lack of traffic discipline
    
    Bus stops which are situated near intersections of traffic signals cause’ traffic which proves to be a major concern in traffic management.
    
4.  Less education by drivers
    
    Some drivers are less educated to understand the signs, and boards which are used which makes other drivers suffer in traffic.
    
5.  Traffic conflict between vehicles and pedestrians:
    
    The pedestrians cross the signals without noticing which leads to fatality. The pedestrians do this due to lack of knowledge, when other people cross the roads they also tend to cross without seeing to the signal.
    
6.  Traffic near signals in public places:
    
    As many people are supposed to be in a public place there requires high traffic management by using sensors, traffic personnel etc. Due to lack of all these, there arises traffic and causes lot of congestion
    

## Proposed Solution

Some of the proposed solutions for overcoming road and traffic safety management is

1.  Smart Traffic Lights
    
    These lights will give a clear indication of the signals from a longer distance and indicate the changes that are supposed to happen (changing of lights).
    
2.  Telematics
    
    This is like a real time GPS which is used to know the actual speed, acceleration, parking and other operations on a vehicle.
    
3.  Autonomous vehicles
    
    Many sensors like GPS, Sonar are all installed in these vehicles to understand the surrounding environment and help to guide the driver about ongoing object and upcoming objects.
    
4.  Emergency services
    
    Certain vehicles are incorporated with fatigue sensors which detect abnormal and emergency behaviors among the drivers and inform the emergency centers and to the relation of the drivers regarding their status.
    
5.  Separate Lanes
    
    The usage of different lanes for different vehicles in road as in case of toll booth, where two-wheelers, four-wheelers, and emergency vehicles are given separate lanes. This method helps to reduce traffic.
    
6.  Street Lighting
    
    The usage of sensors for street lights to adjust with that of the normal lighting which is already available. The sensors must act accordingly with the natural light.
    
7.  Signals with audio
    
    The usage of audio in signals to indicate vehicular movement which helps the less educated driver \[[9](#ch60.xhtml#ref60_9)\].
    

## Steps to be implemented for Road Safety and Traffic Management using IoT

1.  Providing individual path for the different types of vehicles
2.  Usage of proper signal facilities in intersection points and injunctions.
3.  Providing basic knowledge about the traffic system to the users.
4.  Improvement in Traffic control management system.
5.  Improvement of Traffic safety management system
6.  Strengthening traffic police and improving their operations.
7.  Providing proper parking facilities to the vehicle and avoiding roadside parking.
8.  Adjustment of roadside light with accordance with the natural lighting.

## Discussion

The smart usage of sensors in Road Safety and Traffic Management provides improvement in these fields. As and when in the starting stages there are chances of many accidents happening due to poor facilities in road safety and traffic management.

As nowadays, all are updated and people are mostly dependent on sensors for their vehicles for parking, and vehicle tracking which proves to be an improvement in the technology. The vehicles at present can be combined with more and more sensors for providing safe vehicle movement on roads.

The vehicles which are connected ones, they communicate with themselves for avoiding a collision.

In the case of people proper educational knowledge to be given during their school days regarding how to move on in roads and also the importance of traffic signals and why it is to be followed.

## Conclusion

The main challenges Issues in Road Safety and Traffic Management is being addressed and how these can be solved by using IoT and sensors has been discussed which provides a clear idea that improvement in technology and other aspects helps to provide vehicles with the utmost protection and knowledge to common people about road safety and traffic management makes them follow the rules.

As many new sensors are found and incorporated into vehicles there are more chances that these will be available at minimum cost and it will be affordable to all in future. The more the technology gets developed the efficiency of these sensors are to be maintained even during the availability of these sensors at lesser amount. If done then the accidents will be minimized on roads and it becomes a safer place for both vehicles and

# Image-Based Steganography for Android: Concealing Secrets in Pixels

Ms. S. Sivasankari,^([^(48)](#fn48))

E-mail: [shankarirathnam@gmail.com](mailto:shankarirathnam@gmail.com), [akashcyber2020@gmail.com](mailto:akashcyber2020@gmail.com), [aakshayapriya27@gmail.com](mailto:aakshayapriya27@gmail.com), [hariharanmadesh1802@gmail.com](mailto:hariharanmadesh1802@gmail.com)

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-61](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-61)

## Abstract

Steganography is a technique used to hide sensitive information in mediums like images, audio, videotapes, etc. Steganography is really a useful concept for maintaining the security principles like confidentiality and authentication. The word is derived from the Greek word \`steganographia.” With this method, concealed data discovery is eliminated. The benefit of employing data encryption is that it allows us to conceal any material behind the original data (stego file). Our Android-image-based Steganography is going to enhance security in secret communication using AES algorithm.

Keywords: steganography techniques, AES algorithm

## Introduction

The common platform for steganography is image data due to high redundancy, resulting in digital image capacity for embedding. In early works in image steganography both in spatial domain and transform domains, non-adaptive methods were proposed.

Advantage of stego image, is using simply encrypted text is that message is kept inside the image and the quality of the image is not so much affected, so the chances of attacks possible on hidden messages become low.

In stego image data in internal image is not visible to any other person without processing an image. Here we implement stego image in Android applications using AES methods.

The software we use XML, java, and android studio.

The hardware we use 13 processor system, 8 GB RAM, 100 GB ROM or higher, Android Phone.

## Related Work

### Literature Review

[Manohar and Kumar (2020](#ch61.xhtml#ref61_2)) proposed a steganography technique for data hiding. Their paper explains that steganography is a technique for secret communication by hiding data in another form, making it undetectable without revealing it.

**[Aloraini et al. (2022](#ch61.xhtml#ref61_9)), [Subramanian et al. (2021](#ch61.xhtml#ref61_11))** has developed a technique for hiding images and text using the Least Significant Bit (LSB) method in image steganography. Their paper describes how digital steganography conceals information within other data to ensure secure transmission.

**[Cogranne et al. (2022](#ch61.xhtml#ref61_7))** proposed a quantized technique. Their paper explains how their approach embeds hidden messages by lowering deformation or analytical discern, improving the security of the omniscience optimal detector.

**[Nahar et al. (2021](#ch61.xhtml#ref61_3))** studied the LSB technique and added Advanced Encryption System (AES) to enhance the security of the stego image. Their work aimed to embed data into a stego image with greater security.

**[Subramanian et al. (2021](#ch61.xhtml#ref61_11))** and his teammates worked on increasing the data capacity for embedding user key values. Their work aimed to improve the data-hiding capacity of steganography techniques to enhance robustness.

**[Yang et al. (2020](#ch61.xhtml#ref61_13))** researched on LSB-based techniques. In their paper, they discussed how to improve the strength of the stego image, fixing higher capacity, and undiscernible of secret gatherings can be achieved.

## Advantages of image steganography

Security: Image steganography provides a high level of security, as it can be used to hide sensitive data within an image, making it difficult for unauthorized users to access or detect it **([Manohar and Kumar 2020](#ch61.xhtml#ref61_2); [Zhou et al., 2020](#ch61.xhtml#ref61_10); [Subramanian et al., 2021](#ch61.xhtml#ref61_11)).**

Undetectability: Since steganography hides data within an image, it is difficult for an observer to detect that there is any hidden data at all. Thus, **[Subramanian et al. (2021](#ch61.xhtml#ref61_11))** steganography provides a high level of secrecy and confidentiality.

Large Capacity: Images have a large storage capacity, so a lot of data can be hidden within them without affecting the image’s visual quality.

## Disadvantage of Image Steganography

Vulnerability to detection: Although steganography is difficult to detect, it is not impossible. Advanced techniques and software tools can be used to detect hidden data within an image **([Saxena and Maheshwari, 2021](#ch61.xhtml#ref61_5)).**

Loss of data: When data is hidden within an image, it may result in a loss of quality in the image. This is because steganography involves making subtle changes to the image, which can result in a degradation of the image’s quality **([Cogranne et al., 2022](#ch61.xhtml#ref61_7)).**

Limited to specific types of files: Steganography is limited to specific files to embed the data.

## Methods Used in

There are various techniques used in image steganography, some of which are:

## Least Significant Bit (LSB) Embedding

This is the most commonly used technique in image steganography. In this method, the secret data is hidden in the LSB of the pixel merit of an image. The least significant bit of a pixel is the bit that has the least effect on the overall value of the pixel ([Zhang et al., 2022](#ch61.xhtml#ref61_1)).

## Spread Spectrum Technique

This technique involves embedding the secret data by modulating the amplitude, frequency or phase of the pixels of an image using a carrier signal ([Tian et al., 2022](#ch61.xhtml#ref61_6)).

## Transform Domain Techniques

This technique involves embedding the secret data by transforming the original image into a different domain, such as the frequency or wavelet domain, and then hiding the secret data in the transformed coefficients.

## Distortion Techniques

This technique involves distorting the image slightly in any ways that the deformity is subtle to the naked eye but can be detected by a steganalysis tool ([Pan et al., 2022](#ch61.xhtml#ref61_8)).

## Randomized techniques

This technique involves using a random generator to select pixels or groups of pixels to embed the secret message within, making it difficult to detect the presence of hidden data.

There are many other techniques used in image steganography, but the ones listed above are the most commonly used. The choice of technique will depend on the level of security required, the size of the message to be hidden, and the type of image being used ([Meng et al., 2009](#ch61.xhtml#ref61_4)).
