## Advanced Encryption Standard Technique (AES)

![Fig. 2. Advanced Encryption Standard Techniques](images/fig61_2_B.jpg)

Fig. 2\. Advanced Encryption Standard Techniques

Widespread use of AES is found in the symmetric key block cypher created by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST ([Nahar et al., 2021](#ch61.xhtml#ref61_3); [Subramanian et al., 2021](#ch61.xhtml#ref61_11)). It works with 128-bit static-size data blocks and encrypts them in a way that makes it difficult for unauthorized parties to decipher.

Data is encoded and decoded using AES and use a secret key (single key). The key range can be 128 bits, 192 bits, or 256 bits, and the encryption is more secure the larger the key size. Using the key and a sequence of mathematical operations on the plaintext, AES encrypts the data. These operations comprise, among others, substitution, permutation, and matrix multiplication.

The design of the works is a symmetric key which means single key is used to conceal both plain text and images ([Subramanian et al., 2021](#ch61.xhtml#ref61_11)).The unencrypted text and key values are 512-bit (64 bytes). To cope with the increasing computational power, we progress a strategy that works with 512 bits in a single block. Our algorithm uses a sub-box and XOR function to provide good reliability and effecting.

We first construct a 44-block matrix and then convert the key into its hexadecimal counterpart in order to do row shifting. Left circular shifts of 0 bits are represented by Row 1, 1 bits by Row 2, 2 bits by Row 3, and 3 bits by Row 4. The matrix is expanded into an 88-block matrix by applying the XOR operation to extra blocks if the key block size is larger than one. The matrix values are then replaced using S-Box after the entire matrix block has been inverted.

The matrix values are first categorized, after which they undergo hexadecimal, row, S-box, and reverse S-box transformations. Then, an s-box is created out of the matrix using row shifting=k and k = k’. The final key values were determined by substituting this significance using S- Box, even though K’ is the polar opposite of K (K’ = K) ([Aloraini et al., 2022](#ch61.xhtml#ref61_9); [Tang et al., 2022](#ch61.xhtml#ref61_14)).

The 512-bit algorithm’s encryption procedure goes like this:

*   Take the text key of any size and plaintext.
*   Create an 8x8 block matrix with 1=0 and j=0, designated as M.
*   Hexadecimalize the message character to get its value.
*   Use XOR to combine the hexadecimal value with the key matrix.
*   Complete Interchange 1 by replacing Columns 1 and 2 with Columns 3, Columns 2, Columns 5, and Columns 6, and Columns 7 and Columns 8, respectively.
*   Switch the matrix’s complete block.

Conduct Interchange 2 by switching rows 1 through 3 by switching rows 2 through 4, switching rows 5 through 7, and switching rows 6 through 8.

Use the Substitution box to do the mix column operation, which is to XOR the constant matrix with the outcome of step 8. (S-box).

*   Use XOR to combine the secret text and step 10’s output.
*   Go through steps 6 through 11 up to four times.

In order to demonstrate how this method works, we organized the secret message “steganography” into an 8\*8 matrix.

## Conclusion

Wegatheredvarious image steganographytechniques and analyzed their advantages and disadvantages. From all the steganography methods, we selected the AES algorithm for its stronger encryption. We implemented image steganography in Android applications using Java programming languages. Our Android-based image steganography system is developed to facilitate secure secret communication without arousing undue curiosity.

# Various Methods of Injection Attacks

Ms. G. Sathyadevi,^([^(49)](#fn49))

Email: [satthyaram@gmail.com](mailto:satthyaram@gmail.com), [sethutals14@gmail.com](mailto:sethutals14@gmail.com), [dharshaanmsd@gmail.com](mailto:dharshaanmsd@gmail.com), [dharun0473@gmail.com](mailto:dharun0473@gmail.com)

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-62](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-62)

## Abstract

False Data Injection attacks cause series threat to web applications. The injection attacks are in the top ranks in dangerous vulnerabilities that can cause potentially severe damage. The proposed protection mechanism is based on an input filter. To prevent the entry of malicious commands and codes, this filter employs a restricted use of common expressions and characters used in SQL queries. The filter works by limiting the entry of fundamental characters, which helps to restrict the input of malicious codes and commands.

As a security scanner for frequent injection attacks, the filter code is employed. Requests are routed by the filter in two steps. The character is first checked against the blacklisted characters after a request to the filter is sent. If the character is invalid, it will be replaced by an empty string. If it is valid, the entered string will be set to its work. By this way, the input of malicious query codes and commands is restricted. Finally, the string entered will be ready for post-processing work. It is an effective way to prevent SQL injection attacks and is a valuable contribution to the community in the ongoing effort to secure web applications.

Keywords: SQL injection, False Data, SQL Queries, Vulnerabilities, Blacklisted Characters, Post Processing.

## Introduction

A major security risk is the SQL injection vulnerability, which attackers can use to run malicious code and access a database without authorization. An attack known as SQL injection involves putting malicious SQL code into a website’s input field so that the backend database of the web application can use it to execute the code. A filter that checks characters submitted into input fields and filters out any that aren’t valid is suggested as a solution to this problem. Characters are categorized as blacklisted or whitelisted by the filter, and any blacklisted characters are replaced with an empty string. By doing this, popular symbols and characters that are frequently used in SQL injection attacks can’t be used to conduct injection attacks.

The proposed work comprises a simple character restriction filter that compares inputted strings to potential risk characters and replaces any matches with an empty string. This filter offers at least a first line of defense against SQL injection flaws. After the filtration process, the string is sent for input validation before being processed by the web application. This step is necessary to ensure that the input is valid and does not contain any malicious code that could bypass the filter. Input validation is an essential step in securing web applications and preventing SQL injection attacks.

Overall, the suggested filter offers a straight forward but efficient way to guard against SQL injection vulnerabilities. Organizations can safeguard their databases from malicious attacks and stop unauthorized access to sensitive information by validating and filtering input. To guard against SQL injection vulnerabilities and ensure the security and safety of their data, organizations must implement strong security measures.

## Abstract

Password protection is the practice of using secret codes or phrases that are known only to the user to secure digital information or accounts. The value of password protection in protecting sensitive information, such as financial information, personal information, or secret documents is frequently discussed. A few of the password security methods suggested include the use of long, complicated passwords, password managers, and multi-factor authentication. It should also be noted that using weak or stolen passwords makes fraud, identity theft, and data breaches more likely. This paper further talks about several methods for regaining forgotten passwords, such as password resets or email or security question confirmation. This paper concludes by highlighting the critical role password protection plays in safeguarding digital information and providing readers with a summary of the key concepts involved.

## Introduction

The most popular user authentication method is passwords, which are frequently used to protect sensitive data. Passwords are essential for ensuring data security as they act as the first line of defense in securing online accounts. Yet, using incorrect passwords makes it easy for hackers to crack them might result in security issues and data breaches. It’s crucial to make sure that passwords are adequately secured and to have efficient recovery methods in place to prevent password loss or theft. Requiring strong passwords, password hashing, and multi-factor authentication are all examples of password protection techniques. Password hashing ensures that the password is not stored, and requirements for password strength promote the usage of complicated, challenging passwords. Rather than being hashed into plaintext instead of being changed into a hashed value, making it difficult to decipher the original password’s plaintext. whereas multi-Factor authentication establishes extra security by requiring users to provide added authentication factors in addition to their passwords, such as a fingerprint or a one-time code generated by a mobile app. Regaining access to a device or account that has been locked or rendered inoperable because of a forgotten or lost password is referred to as password recovery. In digital devices and online services, password recovery techniques are routinely used to stop data loss, reduce service interruptions, and provide users access to their accounts after they have been locked out.

Typically, during password recovery procedures, the user is confirmed using a variety of ways, such as email or the confirmation of personal data. Upon user authentication, a password reset, or recovery option is displayed. This could entail answering security questions, submitting a verification code, or receiving a link to reset your password Techniques for password recovery include those for phone, email, and security question confirmation. To confirm a user’s identity, security questions are frequently used in conjunction with email and phone verification. Email and phone verification can be used to update a password or unlock an account.in ensuring that crucial data and the internet. The accounts are safe. To prevent unauthorized access to sensitive data, it is crucial to be attentive and continually enhance password protection and recovery procedures. One of the underlying problems with password protection is that traditional password-based authentication systems are vulnerable to attacks like brute force attacks, dictionary attacks, and phishing attacks. In recent years, attacks on online websites have increased, often exploiting poor password management on the websites. Registered users are often the victims of these attacks and are required to quickly change their credentials due to a generic leakage compromising their current ones. Even if users choose strong passwords, the websites’ password storage must respect basic security guidelines for it to be effective. Two examples of major data breaches in recent years are LinkedIn and Yahoo.

## Conclusion

Password protection and recovery are essential components of data security in the contemporary digital world. The rise in cyberattacks and data breaches makes it more important than ever to use strong passwords and effective recovery methods. We’ve listed some of the most important problems and suggested solutions for password security and recovery. These include the requirement for strong, one-of-a-kind password creation, regular password changes, and activating two-factor authentication. Moreover, it has shown that password recovery methods like email verification and security questions can be attacked and may require additional security measures to ensure their effectiveness. This paper places a strong focus on the need for ongoing education and knowledge regarding password protection and recovery to help organizations and individuals stay safe and secure.

# Prevention and Detection of Arp Spoofing - A Survey

R. Sivasankari,^([^(52)](#fn52))

E-mail: [shankarirathnam@gmail.com](mailto:shankarirathnam@gmail.com), [rakshith.durai@gmail.com](mailto:rakshith.durai@gmail.com), [rameshmm2502@gmail.com](mailto:rameshmm2502@gmail.com), [gokulavasan123456sssg@gmail.com](mailto:gokulavasan123456sssg@gmail.com)

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-65](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-65)

## Abstract

ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) spoofing is a common attack technique used by malicious actors to intercept and manipulate network traffic. This attack method entails the transmission of falsified ARP messages to other devices within the network, leading them to direct their traffic toward the attacker’s machine instead of the intended recipient. Preventing and detecting ARP spoofing is crucial for maintaining the security and integrity of a network. Without proper protection, attackers can gain unauthorized access to sensitive information, steal data, or launch more sophisticated attacks. Over the past few years, several strategies have been devised to minimize the threat of ARP spoofing attacks. These techniques range from simple methods such as MAC address filtering to more advanced solutions such as cryptographic protocols and machine learning-based algorithms. The purpose of this survey article is to evaluate the existing ways of identifying and combating ARP spoofing attacks. It will examine the advantages and disadvantages of each technique and establish their actual usefulness in real-world settings. By providing a comprehensive overview of the current research in this area, this paper aims to help network administrators and security professionals choose the most appropriate prevention and detection methods for their networks.

Keywords: ARP Spoofing, Man-in-the-Middle attack, MAC address, Internet Protocol.

## Introduction

As our world becomes increasingly connected and reliant on technology, the security of our networks and data in our networks has become more important than ever. This paper will highlight the grave repercussions of network attacks, specifically Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attacks, that lead to identity theft, financial losses, sensitive data exposure, and critical infrastructure damage. One common type of MITM attack is ARP spoofing, which exploits vulnerabilities in the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) to redirect network traffic to an attacker-controlled machine. ARP spoofing is extremely detrimental since it may be used to circumvent basic security measures like firewalls and intrusion detection systems. During ARP spoofing, the hacker injects malicious bogus ARP packets into the network, leading the victim machine’s ARP cache to be updated with the attacker’s MAC address rather than the actual MAC address of the intended destination. The victim device would then forward any network communication destined for the destination to the attacker’s workstation, which can intercept and after the traffic before delivering it to the intended destination. The attacker can also use ARP spoofing to launch other attacks such as session hijacking, DNS spoofing, and network reconnaissance. Several detection and mitigation approaches have been presented in the literature to avoid and limit the danger of ARP spoofing. The purpose of this survey study is to give a complete evaluation of existing research on ARP spoofing detection and mitigation. This paper will examine the key research questions, methods, and findings of the literature in order to identify the major themes and trends in the field. The survey paper will be composed of three sections. The first part will provide you with a quick rundown of the ARP and how ARP spoofing attacks operate. The second section will review the existing detection and prevention techniques for ARP spoofing. This paper will analyze the strengths and limitations of each technique and identify the major trends and challenges in this area. The final section will highlight the gaps and limitations of the existing research and identify areas for future research. This paper will discuss the need for more comprehensive and integrated approaches to detecting and mitigating ARP spoofing, as well as the importance of developing new techniques that are resistant to evolving attack methods. By providing a comprehensive review of the existing research, this survey paper aims to make a significant contribution to the field of network security. It will be a great resource for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers who want to learn more about ARP spoofing and create effective ways for preventing and minimizing this danger.

## Literature Review

\[[**1**](#ch65.xhtml#ref65_1)\] Morsy & Nashat (2022), proposed a novel method called D-ARP for detecting ARP spoofing attacks that happen in Man-in-the-Middle (MITM). D-ARP attempts to create a link between ARP queries and responses by transmitting ARP packets authenticated with a secret key in tandem to original ARP packets. Each host maintains a log file of all signed ARP packets. D-ARP detects ARP spoofing by matching the injected key to identify conflicts or duplicate MAC addresses. To enhance reliability, to find the MAC addresses of MITM attackers, D-ARP uses the Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) server + Nmap capability. In addition, the system includes an admin module for building an authorized list of hosts. According to the results of the experiments, D-ARP has a zero percent chance of false positives and false negatives and is extremely successful at recognizing and combating ARP spoofing assaults. In conclusion, D-ARP provides a reliable and effective way of detecting ARP spoofing assaults. Its capacity to build a link between ARP requests and responses, as well as use additional techniques for spotting attackers, makes it a dependable network security solution.

\[[**2**](#ch65.xhtml#ref65_2)\] The article describes a new approach proposed by Hijazi & Obaidat (2019),involves creating a static IP-MAC database on the server side and using an executable batch file to automate IP-MAC address gathering and registration. The framework for the proposed method consists of seven steps that ensure a thorough and systematic approach to assess the efficacy of the solution. To address ARP security vulnerabilities in LANs, the authors created an ARP on something like proxy server that collects Internet Protocol, Media Access Control address finally device type information for each connected device during actual network testing. The testing process consisted of three phases: IP-MAC gathering, registration, and identification and avoidance method strategy implementation using a type methodology. The testing procedure was divided into three stages: IP-MAC collection, registration, and execution of an identification and avoidance method employing a type methodology. In the proxy serve; the suggested solution generates a static IP-MAC database and detects and prevents ARP attacks. The outcomes of the experiments demonstrate that the suggested algorithm successfully identifies and stops ARP assaults while establishing a safe network environment. The authors created a Visual Basic plan for implementing detection and protection methods for ARP spoofing and poisoning attacks. The tool does this by collecting each device’s IP- MAC and storing it in an executable file. When the batch file is executed on the proxy serve; the IP-MAC is added to the server cache table. The application additionally enables IP-MAC checking by transforming the MAC to IP and contrasting it with a static entry. The program also has the ability to block and erase IP-MAC records in order to prevent illegal connection access. Overall, the proposed approach offers a practical technique to deal with ARP security issues in a client/server scenario.

\[[**3**](#ch65.xhtml#ref65_3)\] Tian et al., (2017) present a solution to the vulnerabilities associated with the address resolution protocol (ARP) and neighbor discovery protocol (NDP) used in IPv4 and IPv6 network communication, respectively. ARP and NDP suffer from spoofing and other security vulnerabilities that have been identified and reported over the years. Previous attempts to secure the protocols involved modifying the basic protocol, which was not always feasible. The authors provide ARPsec, a stable ARP/RARP protocol suite that includes an address-binding repository built with logical reasoning to allow permanent evaluation of the destination machine’s identity. The formal logic is built around a collection of operational rules and features that are designed to offer secure address resolution without modifying the underlying protocol. Where necessary, the authors supplement the logic-prover-derived assurance using the trusted platform module (TPM), a ubiquitous component found in most current computers. TPM-assisted system state attestations are obtained at a low computational cost, and the strategy enhances the authors’ prior work to accommodate IPv6 NDP (ndpsec).

\[[**4**](#ch65.xhtml#ref65_4)\] O. Salem, K. Alsubhi, A. Shaafi, M. Gheryani, A. Mehaoua, and R. Boutaba, provides a framework for mitigating Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) With a few exceptions, assaults in a remote monitoring system where sensor data is mostly normal. The data is analyzed by the Local Processing Unit (LPU) before a warning is triggered to detect important value shifts. The sensor only communicates the signature of the collected data to prevent the MitM from obtaining confidential information. To keep the distance between measurements, the LPU’s change detection mechanism employs data signatures. The proposed method (Salem et al., 2022) uses Locality Sensitive Hashing (LSH) to establish data signatures that are irrevocable and prevent an adversary from deducing or accessing private data. LSH is a high-dimensional vector hashing algorithm that allows related vectors to be mapped to the same hash values. By applying LSH to the collected data, vastly smaller signatures may be formed and communicated from the sensor to the LPU, resulting in significantly reduced packet sizes and, as a result, less energy required for data transmission. To prevent modification attacks, a keyed Hash Message Authentication Code (HMAC) is transmitted also with text. The initial value of the key is derived from the Signal Strength Indication (RSSI), which is widely used in Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) for indoor localization. RSSI is influenced by the distance between connected devices, and the MitM cannot be deployed in the exact same vicinity as sensors.

\[[**5**](#ch65.xhtml#ref65_5)\] Akter et al., (2021) proposed architecture includes three important components. The first component would be an NFC shield with an antenna, followed by an Arduino Uno board with an ATmega328 CPU, and finally by a passive card. The MITM card needs to be inserted between Reader malicious and Card original in our experiment. To partition the space, a sheet of aluminum foil is employed between Reader malicious and Writer malicious to prevent radio signals from clashing. They communicate with one another over a different channel (in our case, wire). Three active components and passive components devices are arranged inside a passive-active- active-passive-active arrangement, with the gadgets providing card-reader-writer-card-reader operations. This paper examines a man-in-the-middle (MITM) attack against contactless payment systems that exploit a weakness in the separation of card authentication and transaction authorization. The MITM attacker is comprised of three components: Reader malicious Writer malicious, and Card malicious. The attacker hijacks interaction between both the original card and reader, alters messages as needed, and transmits them to the Writer malicious component, which writes the information to the Card malicious. The attacker controls the route such that the original reader cannot identify any channel swaps during transmission. Payment information, challenge replies, and personal information can all be altered by the attacker.

\[[**6**](#ch65.xhtml#ref65_6)\] Aldabbas & Amin (2021)proposed a mechanism for automatically detecting and mitigating ARP attacks in an IoT environment utilizing a pc or laptop executing custom code. The SDN controller retains data on network topology along with the Controller ARP Table (CAT). To analyze malicious traffic, network topology data is gathered from the controller and the dynamic host configuration protocol (DHCP) server during machine design. Once ARP information originates upon this controller, it is handled by a different machine; ports are then locked, so no further action occurs on the controller. This novel system is made up of three major parts. The proposed approach’s first components gather network topology information from the whole network. The remainder is concerned with configuring forwarding rules on connected devices to route all ARP traffic to a separate workstation. The final component includes traffic analysis and ARP spoofing avoidance. Several experiments are carried out to evaluate the effectiveness of the suggested system using a specialized simulation for SDN-based IoT. Experiments were carried out on an Ubuntu Virtual Machine having six cores and eight gigabytes of RAM and a hypervisor server with sixteen gigabytes of RAM. Mininet seems to be a popular SDN-based simulation tool. This application is used to establish virtualizing setups for different Pox SDN controller examinations. To mitigate the attack scenario, the proposed server machine acts as a bridge to both SDN controller, also to connected nodes. Inquiries for address translation are sent to this server, which analyses traffic on the network using a specialized way of identifying the attack state. When a network is attacked, appropriate safeguards are implemented, and the hacker’s position as in network is determined. Many tests are conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of the suggested system, and it is determined that the technique performs better in terms of attack detection and mitigation.

## Discussion

The study of Morsy & Nashat (2022)offers an unusual way to detect ARP spoofing assaults. According to the authors, their technique identifies and blocks these assaults with no false positives or negatives. D-ARP establishes a link between ARP queries and answers by sending a signed ARP packet in tandem with the original ARP packets. D-ARP detects ARP spoofing by comparing the injected key to locate conflicts or duplicate MAC addresses, and hosts log all signed ARP packets. A DHCP server and Nmap are also used to discover the MAC addresses of victims, as well as an admin module for constructing an authorized list of hosts. Yet, this work may benefit from a more thorough assessment of the inadequacies of the proposed strategy. For example, the authors make no mention of the impact of D-ARP on network performance or the risk of false positives and negatives in scenarios with complex network topologies. Also, the authors should investigate the potential of attackers evading the described method by deploying more advanced ARP spoofing techniques. Other tools for identifying attackers, such as DHCP and Nmap, improve the method’s reliability even more. Overall, the article suggests a potential new way for detecting ARP spoofing attacks, but further research is needed to evaluate its effectiveness in different network situations and against more advanced attack tactics.

Hijazi & Obaidat (2019) propose addressing ARP security vulnerabilities in a client/server situation by constructing a static IP-MAC database on the proxy server and automating IP-MAC address collecting and registration with an executable batch file. The proposed method’s architecture (Hijazi & Obaidat, 2019) comprises seven phases that ensure a complete and methodical approach to evaluating the efficacy of the solution. The testing procedure was divided into three stages: IP-MAC collection, registration, and execution of a detection and prevention method employing a type mechanism. Experiment results show that the suggested solution successfully identifies and prevents ARP attacks while providing a safe network environment. The Visual Basic plan created for deploying detection as well as mitigation approaches for ARP spoofing and poisoning threats has an easy-to-use interface that allows for automatic gathering of IP-MAC, registration of IP-MAC in the server cache table, and IP-MAC entry verification and change. The suggested method offers an in-depth solution for ensuring network security against ARP spoofing and poisoning attacks, making it a practical and dependable method for network administrators to administer the network. While the suggested solution is highly successful in identifying and stopping ARP assaults, there may be scalability constraints for bigger networks that might be studied further in future studies.

Tian et al., (2017) provide us with a solution to the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) and Neighbor Discovery Protocol (NDP) vulnerabilities in IPv4 and IPv6 network communication, respectively. The study offers an innovative and effective solution to the ARP and NDP protocol problems that do not need protocol change. For current computer systems, the employment of formal logic with TPM gives excellent security assurances that are both cost-effective and practical. The article focuses on a serious security issue that has been detected and publicized throughout time. ARP and NDP are widely used in contemporary networking, but they are vulnerable to spoofing and other security flaws, making them a potential target for attackers. Attempts to protect the protocols in the past required altering the underlying protocol, which was not always possible. The authors suggest a stable ARP/RARP protocol suite that includes an address-binding repository built with formal logic to enable long-term evaluation of the destination machine’s identity. This method provides secure address resolution without modifying the underlying protocol. Arpsec, according to the authors, costs 7% to 15.4% higher than the standard Linux ARP implementation. The overhead is equivalent to that of a standard Linux NDP implementation, hence ARPsec represents the initial step for potentially trustworthy and encrypted underlying network in both IP versions 4 and 6. The study’s findings show that the technique is feasible, paving the door for further research and development of secure networking protocols. Overall, this study makes an important addition to network security by suggesting a novel and practical solution to the vulnerabilities associated with the ARP and NDP protocols. For current computer systems, the employment of formal logic with TPM gives excellent security assurances that are both cost-effective and practical. The study’s findings illustrate the approach’s practicality and open the way for future research and development of secure networking protocols. As a result, this article would be appropriate for inclusion in a survey paper on network security.

Salem et al. (2022) provide a strategy for combating Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) assaults in a remote monitoring system in their study. Locality Sensitive Hashing (LSH) is used in the proposed system to establish irreversible data signatures that prohibit an attacker from deducing or accessing private data. The study highlights three key contributions: lowering data transmission energy consumption, limiting effective MitM attacks, and preventing modification and replay assaults. The suggested paradigm applies to remote monitoring systems, where data privacy and security are crucial. The employment of LSH and HMAC by the authors addresses the issues of data secrecy and integrity, respectively. LSH provides irreversible data signatures that lower data transmission packet sizes and energy usage, whilst HMAC assures message authentication and prevents message modification attacks. The use of RSSI as the first key value for HMAC is a feasible technique that makes use of current technology while reducing the possibility of MitM attacks. The suggested architecture can solve issues about security and privacy in remote monitoring systems, notably in the healthcare arena. The authors conduct a thorough assessment of the suggested approach’s efficacy in preventing MitM and modification/replay attacks.

To combat man-in-the-middle (MITM) against contactless payment systems, the study (Akter et al., 2021)offered an architecture that includes an NFC shield, an Arduino Uno board, and a passive card. Researchers found a flaw in the separation of card validation and payment authorization, allowing an attacker to hijack the interaction between the original card and reader, change messages as needed, and transfer them to the malicious writer component. The attacker used the route to prevent the original reader from detecting any channel swaps during transmission, allowing them to change payment information, challenge responses, and personal information. To counteract this attack, the suggested technique included establishing a maximum reading time and a threshold value, as well as measuring the difference between the current reading time and the maximum reading time to detect anomalies when the reader and the card are communicating. As compared to previously proposed protection mechanisms, this approach requires no extra hardware and delivers a more efficient and cost- effective solution. The research also proved the suggested mechanism’s usefulness in identifying MITM attacks with 100% accuracy. The suggested architecture and technique contribute significantly to the field of security in contactless payment systems. The study provides a viable and cost-effective way to minimize MITM attacks by detecting a fault in the present system and offering a remedy that does not require any new hardware.

Aldabbas & Amin (2021) suggested a system for automatically identifying and mitigating Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) threats. The system is built on a Software-Defined Networking (SDN) controller that holds network topology information as well as the Controller ARP Table (CAT). The suggested solution consists of three major components: acquiring network topology information, implementing flow rules on network devices, and traffic analysis and ARP spoofing mitigation modules. Numerous tests were carried out in order to assess the efficacy of the suggested system using a specialized simulation for SDN-based IoT. The experiments comprised introducing an attacker with the IP address 10.0.0.11 and implementing the well-known operating system known as “Kali Linux” to cause ARP spoofing and some bogus packets to destabilize the overall system topology controller. Many factors, including attack detection time, CPU overhead, attack mitigation time, and system throughput, were calculated to assess the performance of the suggested strategy. By analyzing suspicious network traffic, the suggested approach in this study also reduces the incidence of Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) assaults. Because the system inspects ARP data independently at each server, ARP assaults are detected automatically, and attack protection methods are engaged very rapidly. Inquiries about address translation are routed to this server, which analyses traffic on the network that used a specialized approach to determine the attack status. This study’s proposed technique is innovative and shows promising results in identifying and mitigating ARP assaults in IoT systems. The suggested system outperforms existing systems in various ways, including quicker attack detection and mitigation times and the eradication of DDoS attacks.

## Conclusion

Therefore, ARP spoofing is a critical security concern that demands network administrators and security specialists to maintain constant attention and awareness. Our review of the current literature on this topic reveals that attackers frequently utilize ARP spoofing to intercept and alter network traffic, and the potential implications of a successful assault can be severe. This type of attack can jeopardize the integrity and security of sensitive data, such as login passwords, financial information, and personal identifying information. While there are options for taking steps to reduce the risk of ARP spoofings, such as implementing network-level security protocols such as ARP spoofing detection and prevention mechanisms, it is critical to remain proactive and aware of the latest security threats and network security best practices. As technology advances, so do the methods used by attackers, and security measures must develop to keep up. This includes the deployment of intrusion detection and prevention technologies as well as secure coding methods. Finally, everyone must realize the importance of network security and take the necessary precautions to safeguard our data and systems against ARP spoofing and other security risks. This proposal can reduce the danger of ARP spoofing and other cyberattacks by being educated about the current security risks and implementing best practices for network security. This will defend our information and infrastructure.

# A Survey on Enhancing Password Guessing and Dictionary List Creation Techniques Using OSINT

Mr. S. Giridharan,^([^(53)](#fn53))

E-mail: [mailtoogiri@gmail.com](mailto:mailtoogiri@gmail.com), [smkaravindan@gmail.com](mailto:smkaravindan@gmail.com), [rrsk261002@gmail.com](mailto:rrsk261002@gmail.com), [gurubalaji2002@gmail.com](mailto:gurubalaji2002@gmail.com)

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-66](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-66)

## Abstract

Password cracking is the process of recovering a password from an encrypted or hashed form. Attackers often make use of open-source intelligence to aid in their password-cracking efforts. This information can include usernames, email addresses, and personal information such as birth dates or hobbies. By using this information, attackers can create custom wordlists and employ various cracking techniques, such as dictionary attacks, brute force attacks, and social engineering attacks. This abstract provides an overview of the password cracking process using web crawling and highlights the importance of implementing strong password policies and educating users on the risks of password reuse and weak passwords. Additionally, website owners should take measures to secure their databases and limit the amount of personal information that is accessible to attackers. By understanding the methods used by attackers, individuals, and organizations can take proactive steps to protect themselves against password- cracking attempts.

Keywords: Web crawling, Custom wordlist, Open Source Intelligence (OSINT), Social engmeermg

## Introduction

Passwords are the cornerstone of network security and protect against unauthorized access to sensitive information. However, as the number of websites, apps, and devices that require passwords continues to grow, it can be difficult to keep track of them all. Unfortunately, this has resulted in many users using simple and easy-to-guess passwords, leaving them vulnerable to hacking attempts. One of the methods used by hackers to gain access to user accounts is password cracking. This process uses special software to guess the user’s password by trying different combinations of characters until the correct one is found. To be successful, hackers often collect information from websites to help them compile a list of possible passwords. The first step in cracking a password is to gather information about the user. This information may be obtained from various sources including social media profiles, online forums, and other publicly available information. Once a hacker has gathered enough information, he can use a technique called brute force password cracking to guess a user’s password. In brute force attacks, all possible combinations of characters are tried until the correct password is found. This can be a time-consuming process but is often successful if the password is weak or easy to guess. Another password cracking technique is dictionary attacks. In this method, the hacker uses a precompiled list of common passwords or words from a dictionary to guess the user’s password. This is often more successful than brute force attacks because many users use common passwords such as “12356” or “password.”

## Literature Review

\[[**1**](#ch66.xhtml#ref66_1)\] It proposes a new approach for generating password dictionaries, which can be used for cracking passwords based on contextual information. The proposed methodology takes into account the common patterns and structures used in passwords, as well as the specific context in which the password was created. This approach is more effective than traditional dictionary generation methods that do not consider contextual information. To test their approach, the authors conducted experiments using real-world password datasets. The results showed that their methodology outperformed traditional dictionary-based password cracking.

\[[**2**](#ch66.xhtml#ref66_2)\] It explores the effect of using “leet” or “1337” substitutions in passwords on their strength and security. Leet is a technique where letters are replaced with numbers or symbols that resemble them, such as “3” for “E” or “@” for “A.” The authors conducted a study using a large dataset of leaked passwords and found that leet substitutions are commonly used by users to create passwords, with the most popular substitution being “3” for “E.” However, they also found that such substitutions do not significantly improve the strength of passwords, and can even make them weaker if the substitution is too predictable. The paper concludes that while leet substitutions may make passwords more memorable for users, they do not significantly improve password security and can even decrease it if the substitution is too predictable.

\[[**3**](#ch66.xhtml#ref66_3)\] It proposes a novel method for constructing a sentiment dictionary using web crawling techniques. The sentiment dictionary can be used for sentiment analysis, which is a vital component in many natural language processing applications. The proposed method focuses on three main aspects of sentiment analysis: (1) collecting a diverse set of opinionated text from the web, (2) filtering out irrelevant text, and (3) labeling the remaining text with sentiment scores. The method uses a multi-stage approach that includes crawling the web, filtering out irrelevant web pages, extracting opinionated text, and labeling the text with sentiment scores. The sentiment scores are calculated using a supervised learning approach based on a set of seed words. Overall, the paper presents a novel and effective method for sentiment dictionary construction that can be used to improve the accuracy of sentiment analysis in various natural language processing applications.

\[[**4**](#ch66.xhtml#ref66_4)\] It proposes a novel approach for attacking machine learning-based systems used in cybersecurity applications. The authors highlight the growing use of machine learning algorithms in intrusion detection systems, and the need to evaluate their robustness against potential attacks. The proposed approach is a brute-force black-box method that involves generating a large number of adversarial samples and testing them against the target machine-learning model. The method is based on the assumption that the attacker does not know the target model’s parameters or training data. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach on two popular intrusion detection systems, Snort and Suricata. The results show that the proposed approach can successfully attack the models, even when they are trained with state- of-the-art techniques for robustness. Overall, the paper provides valuable insights into the vulnerabilities of machine learning-based systems used in cybersecurity.

\[[**5**](#ch66.xhtml#ref66_5)\] It presents a method to crack the password protection of PDF 2.0 documents using GPU acceleration. The authors use a tool called Hashcat to perform password cracking and find that the use of GPUs significantly speeds up the process compared to using CPUs. The authors first discuss the PDF 2.0 specification and the various types of password protection it supports, including encryption and access permissions. They then describe the Hashcat tool and its use for password cracking. The authors find that using GPUs can greatly reduce the time required to crack PDF 2.0 passwords. They test various password lengths and complexity levels and find that longer and more complex passwords take longer to crack, but still benefit from GPU acceleration. The authors also compare the performance of different GPU models and find that newer models with higher memory bandwidth perform better. The paper concludes by highlighting the importance of strong password protection and the need for users to use longer and more complex passwords to prevent password-cracking attacks.

## Methods and Techniques

\[[**1**](#ch66.xhtml#ref66_1)\] The techniques and algorithms used in the paper:

Corpus collection: A corpus of text is collected from a variety of sources, including online forums, social media, and news articles. This corpus is used to generate candidate passwords.

Password generation: The candidate passwords are generated by applying various transformations to the words and phrases in the corpus. These transformations include capitalization, substitution, and concatenation.

Contextual filtering: The generated passwords are filtered using contextual information, such as the target user’s name, age, gender, and location. This helps to generate passwords that are more likely to be used by the target user.

Frequency analysis: The frequency of each generated password is analyzed to determine its popularity and likelihood of being used as a password.

N-gram analysis: The generated passwords are analyzed using N-gram analysis to identify common patterns and sequences.

Markov chain analysis: A Markov chain is used to model the likelihood of a user choosing a particular password given their previous password choices.

Password cracking: The generated dictionaries are used to crack passwords using various cracking techniques, including brute force, dictionary-based attacks, and hybrid attacks. A comprehensive diagram of the proposed process is shown in [Fig. 1](#ch66.xhtml#fig66_1), DBPedia is a Python library that employs rdflib4, an RDF library, to merge graph data from diverse schemas. RDF is a data model that merges information on the web, and its length and scope can be adjusted during generation. It can be limited to one layer, called “contextual dictionary 1” (CD\_1), or increased to two layers (CD\_2), three layers (CD\_3 ), and so on. Each additional layer significantly increases the quantity of data, creating a trade-off between speed, dictionary length, and success rate. Some of the links in a Wikipedia or DBPedia entry are generic and unrelated to the topic. They are excluded from the generated dictionaries, and the wordlist obtained is compared to the target after processing.

![Fig. 1. A methodology diagram for creating a dictionary from website/DBpedia](images/fig66_1_B.jpg)

[Fig. 1\. A methodology diagram for creating a dictionary from website/DBpedia](#ch66.xhtml#R_fig66_1)

\[[**2**](#ch66.xhtml#ref66_2)\] It presents several methods, techniques, and algorithms used to analyze and evaluate the security of passwords that use leet substitutions. One of the main methods used in the paper is data collection. The authors collected a large dataset of passwords from various sources, including leaked password lists and user surveys. They also used a password cracking tool to generate a set of candidate passwords based on common patterns and leet substitutions.

The authors then used several techniques and algorithms to analyze the strength of the passwords in their dataset. One technique was to calculate the entropy of the passwords, which measures the amount of uncertainty or randomness in a password. The authors also used a tool called John the Ripper to perform brute-force and dictionary-based attacks on the passwords, which allowed them to evaluate the effectiveness of different leet substitutions in increasing password strength. Another algorithm used in the paper was a Markov model, which the authors used to generate random passwords based on the frequency of character combinations in their dataset. They then used this algorithm to analyze the impact of leet substitutions on password strength by generating a set of candidate passwords with and without leet substitutions and measuring their strength.

\[[**3**](#ch66.xhtml#ref66_3)\] It proposes a novel approach for sentiment-aware web crawling and constructing sentiment dictionaries. In this approach, the authors utilize three main techniques: Seed-based Crawling, Sentiment Classification, and Mutual Reinforcement Learning. Seed-based Crawling: The first technique used in this approach is seed-based crawling. The authors propose an initial set of seed URLs that are likely to contain sentiment-related content. The web crawler then follows the links on these seed URLs to crawl sentiment-related web pages. This approach saves time and computational resources by focusing on a smaller subset of web pages that are more likely to contain relevant content.

Sentiment Classification: The authors use a machine learning algorithm to classify web pages into positive, negative, or neutral sentiment categories. They use a combination of lexical and syntactic features to train the classifier, including the presence of sentiment-related words, the frequency of punctuation marks, and the length of sentences. The sentiment classification allows the system to accurately identify and classify sentiment-related web pages.

Mutual Reinforcement Learning: The authors propose a novel approach where the sentiment classification algorithm and the web crawler reinforce each other’s performance. The web crawler in turn, feeds back information about the sentiment-related content it finds back to the sentiment classification algorithm. It helps improve the accuracy and efficiency of the sentiment-aware web crawling system.

[Figure 2](#ch66.xhtml#fig66_2) illustrates the overall flow chart of the proposed approach, The need for a sentiment- aware web crawling method is highlighted to periodically collect new sentiment words, as opposed to the current web crawling method for building a sentiment dictionary. This method can save database space and time in constructing the sentiment dictionary. To accomplish this, a new bucket-sorted hash join scheme is introduced to achieve a faster hashing mechanism compared to the existing hash join scheme. This approach is applied to create the database.

![Fig. 2. Sentiment-aware web crawler](images/fig66_2_B.jpg)

[Fig. 2\. Sentiment-aware web crawler](#ch66.xhtml#R_fig66_2)

\[[**4**](#ch66.xhtml#ref66_4)\] It proposes a technique for attacking machine learning-based cybersecurity systems using a brute-force black-box approach. The paper focuses on attacks on systems that use binary classifiers for decision-making. The proposed method involves three steps: data generation, model inversion, and adversarial attack. The first step in the method is data generation. The attacker generates a large amount of data that includes both positive and negative samples. The positive samples are designed to be similar to the target class, while the negative samples are designed to be dissimilar. The surrogate model is used to invert the target model and generate a representation of the decision boundary. The attacker generates adversarial samples that are designed to be misclassified by the target model. The adversarial samples are created by perturbing the input data in a way that is not noticeable to humans but changes the decision of the classifier. The perturbations are based on the decision boundary generated in the second step. The algorithm used in this method is a combination of techniques from machine learning and optimization. The surrogate model is trained using a machine learning algorithm, and the inversion of the target model is done using an optimization algorithm. The adversarial attack is also an optimization problem that is solved using a gradient-based method.

\[[**5**](#ch66.xhtml#ref66_5)\] It describes a novel method of using GPUs to accelerate the password-cracking process and improve its efficiency. The technique used in the paper involves a combination of dictionary attacks and brute-force attacks to crack the password of a PDF document. The authors proposed a multi-tiered approach that allows for the efficient use of GPU resources. They first start with dictionary-based attacks, which use a pre- computed list of words and their variations, to increase the probability of success. If the dictionary attack fails, the brute-force attack is then launched. This approach involves trying every possible combination of characters until the correct password is found. To optimize this process, the paper proposes the use of an incremental search, where the algorithm starts with shorter password lengths and gradually increases the length until a match is found. It is based on the MD5 hash algorithm, which is commonly used to store password hashes. The kernel function is optimized for parallel execution and makes use of the shared memory on the GPU to reduce the number of memory accesses.

## Conclusion

In conclusion, password cracking is a serious security concern that website owners need to take seriously. In this paper, we analyzed the password cracking methods by gathering information from web scrapping and using GPU that will increase the probability to bypass the security. Once the information has been obtained it can be used to launch a password-cracking attack. It involves the use of various techniques to gain unauthorized access to user accounts by guessing or discovering their passwords. Attackers can gather information from websites using various methods, including social engineering, phishing, and data breaches. Once they have obtained this information, they can use it to launch password-cracking attacks. The contribution of this paper lies in its innovative approach to dictionary generation for password cracking, which considers the contextual information that is often associated with password creation. These provided methodologies have the potential to be useful for security professionals and law enforcement agencies in the fight against cybercrime, as it provides a more accurate and efficient means of cracking passwords. Overall, this paper provides valuable information about the development of novel techniques for password cracking and highlights the importance of considering contextual information in the generation of password dictionaries.

# Survey on Multi-Factor Authentication in Cloud Computing

Ms. K. R. Nandhashree,^([^(54)](#fn54))

Email: [nandhashree29@gmail.com](mailto:nandhashree29@gmail.com), [jeevam701269@gmail.com](mailto:jeevam701269@gmail.com), [harish12groot@gmail.com](mailto:harish12groot@gmail.com), [karthi.vmpak@gmail.com](mailto:karthi.vmpak@gmail.com)

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-67](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-67)

## Abstract

The proliferation of cloud applications and cloud services to enterprises and personal usage is high these days. It is known to attract unwanted attention from hackers who are focusing their efforts on the cloud’s data. There are a lot of methods varying from phishing which can readily disclose one’s credentials. These traditional ways of authenticating users to a certain app or service are not enough for security. In this review paper, the survey of different techniques and methods of multi-factor authentication that have been implemented in various works in past decades; then we analyze the findings and future direction of the modalities involved. Concerning various papers and articles on authentication methods we came to a solution where intercepting a text message is more difficult than passwords and social accounts. A full-stack web application that is built and hosted on the cloud and is authenticated with various methods is claimed to be a more secure model. This serves as an alternative solution for better security and authentication for all enterprises, organizations, and even for personal applications that are built on the cloud.

Keywords: Web, Cloud, Authentication, Frameworks, Multifactor

## Introduction

Nowadays, sensitive information is stored online by both companies and users, rendering digital security vital. Online accounts are used by everyone to engage with the programs, services, and information that are kept online. A breach or misuse of this internet data could have detrimental real-world consequences, including identity theft, disruption of the company, and loss of privacy. Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is a solution to all this. Digital assets are protected by passwords, but they are insufficient. Cybercriminals with experience constantly search for passwords. One password can be used to access multiple accounts for which the user may have to use multiple passwords. Even if the password has been stolen, multi-factor authentication adds an extra layer of protection to keep unauthorized users from accessing these accounts. Multi-factor authentication is used by businesses to verify user identities. The primary advantage of MFA is that it boosts the security of your organization by mandating that users authenticate themselves using a secure user ID & Passwords. Although login credentials are necessary, they can be compromised through Trial and error methods or theft by unauthorized parties. Adhering to an MFA protocol that involves factors such as biometrics or physical token keys assures that the user data will remain secure from cyber threats.

## Multi-Factor Authentication

Whenever we sign into our online accounts, the procedure we refer to as authentication is necessary to demonstrate that we are the true account owners. These authentications are often accomplished using a straightforward username and password. Yet sadly, as new technologies proliferate around the globe, these usernames and passwords are so simple to find and guess. Also, people frequently forget their passwords, so the majority merely use the same password or pick an easy one for each account they have on various websites. Nevertheless, things become more fascinating when multi-factor authentication techniques are enabled. The process always begins with the standard password, but is subsequently followed by a variety of authentication techniques, including biometrics, one-time passwords (OTP), face recognition, knowledge-based, and possession-based techniques. This is not the end of it. These days, there are many different ways to secure one’s account.

## Exploratory Study

### Various Algorithms used for MFA

In this section a survey on the algorithms used for MFA is described. Based upon the modality of authentication technique the authors have used different algorithms.

### REAL-OR-RANDOM (ROR)

Yeongjae et al. have used the Burrows - Abadi - Needham (BAN) logic to evaluate the viability of the authentication systems without flaws. This paradigm in ([Cho et al., 2022](#ch67.xhtml#ref67_1)) demonstrates the nature of the security of the session keys which would be using Automated Validation of Internet Security Protocols and Applications (AVISPA). This method protects the systems from replay and Man - In - the - Middle (MITM) attacks and relevant protocols are compared in terms of security functionality, computation cost, and communication overhead protocols. This algorithm is backed by Elliptic Curve cryptography and Fuzzy Extractor as they contribute to the small key size as well as ensuring a high-security level. This paves way for the authentication and agreement phase with smart cards as the authentication method.

### Rabin Cryptosystem

FanWu et al. proposed a method to protect the identity of the user, who is authenticating into the system. This is over weighted than other methods in the previous papers. Most methods won’t involve any password (or) token, but this method follows token-based authentication for all the WSN networks in the IoT systems. All these schemes meet the requirements and common attacks are proved to be invalid after simulating the model with NS-3. This model is similar to the process of checking bio-metrics, but more of a virtual token that acts like the entry to the actual account after successful authentication.

### Zero - Round Trip - Time Authentication:

[Mitev et al. (2022](#ch67.xhtml#ref67_3)) proposed a protocol, which involves two main factors for authentication - Physical Layer properties which depend on the physical layer properties of wireless communication such as channel characteristics and signal strength to authenticate the user and the Digital Signature layer which uses a digital signature to provide an additional layer of authentication in which the user has to possess a private key and a public key pair to sign and verify all messages exchanged with the access point. This method is similar to the work in [Cho et al. (2022](#ch67.xhtml#ref67_1)) which focuses on wireless communication where the layers of the signal are verified by an access point. Also, this protects from MITM attacks like the BAN method.

### Pseudo-Identity Authentication

Devanapalli et al. developed a Pseudo - Identity method using a chaotic-map-based algorithm. This is based on the three methods including passwords and challenge-response. The extended version of this method depends totally on randomness and complexity rather than the traditional chaotic maps. This algorithm’s working has been proposed by the Automated Validation of Internet Security Protocols and Applications (AVISPA) tool and proved its effectiveness against security attacks.

### Key Agreement

Qi Jiang et al. proposed a method where the user’s private key and the Cloud Assisted Autonomous Vehicle’s (CAAV’s) public key are used in establishing a secure communication channel between the user and the CAAV - Cloud Assisted Autonomous Vehicles. Since this project is based mostly on autonomous vehicles connected to the cloud, the protocol was built hybrid in nature with efficient authentication using biometrics and homomorphic encryption.

### CT-AKA Protocol

Qi Jiang et al. also developed CT-AKA (Certificate —Less Two—Party Authenticated Key Agreement) protocol which generates a cryptographic hash of the biometric data and stores that. The procedure involves system setup, AV registration, user registration, user authentication, password and biometrics change, and smart card revocation which are the six processes that make up CT-AKA. CAV (The Cloud—Assisted Autonomous Vehicle) system is booted up by the cloud during configuration, and system parameters are released. A secret key for each AV is created and distributed by the cloud during the AV registration process. In addition to this, the protocol uses a key agreement mechanism to securely establish a session key between the user and the cloud server which in turn is used for their communication.

The OTP authentication method is a general authentication gateway that is present nearly in every web - application we use today. ### Biometrics

Biometrics is one of the MFA techniques where one’s biometric information is used for authenticating the user into the application or network. The papers ([Ometov and Bezzateev, 2017](#ch67.xhtml#ref67_6); [Ibrokhimov et al., 2019](#ch67.xhtml#ref67_7); [Sinigaglia et al., 2020](#ch67.xhtml#ref67_9)) have used this modality of authentication which is common and also secured. One’s biometrics cannot be replaced but can still be cloned using the new technologies available. The paper Kalsoom [Fatima et al. (2019](#ch67.xhtml#ref67_10)), discusses the use of facial recognition and iris scans including voice recognition with voice prints. In paper [Jiang et al. (2020](#ch67.xhtml#ref67_5)), biometric authentication includes the use of a shared secret key for authentication between the vehicle and the cloud server.

### Certificates and Token-Based Authentications

The new method implemented here is token-based authentication and certificate-based authentication. Though this method is explained in the paper [Ometov and Bezzateev (2017](#ch67.xhtml#ref67_6)), they have provided this certain authentication only to IoT devices. Also, the authentication is lightweight but is stopped by the lack of a standardized authentication framework.

### Knowledge-Based and Possession-Based Authentications

This method is used in paper [Albalawi et al. (2019](#ch67.xhtml#ref67_8)) to ensure fast and reliable authentication with technologies like blockchain which helps in bringing more standardized protocols for the safety of data. This method is backed by machine learning, where most of these authentication factors are used inside a vehicle. This not only secures the data but also prevents users from performing any illegitimate activities.

### Behavior Detection

Aleksandr et al. developed a behavior detection method where the cloud system understands the user’s behavior by pre-built inputs or machine learning. These are deployed in models where user interaction is needed the most. This is used in V2X applications and helps solve most authentication challenges. This method involves analyzing the user’s behavior patterns to determine whether the current user is the legitimate owner of the device or not. With the help of sensors, users’ typing rhythm, mouse movements, and even the way they hold their device can determine if the behavior matches the expected behavior of the legitimate user.

## Conclusion

These days, login into accounts requires a laborious authentication process, which makes it easier for attackers to target accounts that aren’t secured. As a result, users must employ MFA approaches and put up with the wait time to be authenticated to an account. Each time a user attempts to access their account, MFA will reduce the time spent by employing an alternate authentication method. It requires less time to process and must be guarded.

# Survey on Improvement in Efficiency of Steganography

Mrs. C. Jeeva, P. Nijin, S. Atchaya Kumar,and S. Mano Subash
