# Autonomous Assistance for Alzheimer's Patients

R. Julian Menezes,[^(60)](#fn60)

E-mail: [julianmr@hindustanunic.ac.in](mailto:julianmr@hindustanunic.ac.in); [nithinkumar.c44@gmail.com](mailto:nithinkumar.c44@gmail.com); [rishwanthpraveen@gmail.com](mailto:rishwanthpraveen@gmail.com); [slakshmi@hindustanuniv.ac.in](mailto:slakshmi@hindustanuniv.ac.in)

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-75](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-75)

## Abstract

Alzheimer’s disease (Ad) is a disease that becomes more and more inhibiting of memory with a progressive course over time it also affects thinking and causes visual impairment. Visual impairment is a customary symptom of AD, and recent studies have shown that visual interventions may improve the functioning of AD patients. This paper aims to use image processing techniques to detect AD at an early stage using Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) of the brain. The proposed technique also includes camera-based detection for visually impaired or AD individuals to recognize text, objects, and known people in real-time using face recognition and sign language. Optical Character Recognition (OCR) method is used to transform pictures into text, and ML is used to detect known faces, objects, and sign language. The output will be expressed in the form of an audio stream with the help of text-to-speech.

Keywords: Face detection, Ocr, Sign detection, Tesseract, MRI, API, AD

## Introduction

Visually impaired individuals face many challenges in their daily lives, including difficulties in reading printed text, recognizing faces, and identifying objects. Assistive technology has the prospective ability to alleviate challenges and enhance the standard of living for individuals with visual impairments. The number of people with near or distant vision impairments worldwide is estimated to be at least 2.2 billion. One billion or almost half - of these cases are yet to be treated for vision impairments. Recent advancements in OCR and face recognition technologies have made it possible to develop camera-based systems that can accurately recognize text, faces, and objects. However, these systems have not yet been fully explored for their potential to assist visually impaired individuals. Several studies have developed OCR and face recognition systems for the visually impaired, but these systems have limitations such as not being able to recognize text in real-time, and not being able to recognize faces and objects. We additionally add sign-to-speech as an additive functionality in the integrated system that will help other people understand the sign language being expressed by the affected

[Evans et al. (2007](#ch75.xhtml#ref75_1)) conducted a study in which 13900 individuals resulted showing that the presence of depression was rife between individuals who were visually impaired to those who are not visually impaired. This suggests that there may be a link between visual impairment and depression. Likely individuals with visual impairment may be to a greater extent prone to experiencing difficulties in functioning their daily lives. These difficulties can hurt an individual’s mental well-being, leading to depression which could lead to social isolation, which is another risk factor for depression. In conclusion, this research highlights the importance of recognizing the potential impact of visual impairment on mental health and the need for interventions that can help alleviate the burden of depression in this population.

[Mashiata et al. (2022](#ch75.xhtml#ref75_2)) conducted an all-inclusive sweeping review of the status quo and anticipated prospects of assistive technology catered to visually impaired individuals. The review aimed to provide an overview of the various assistive devices that are currently available, as well as their features and limitations. Various types of assistive devices are being used for visually impaired individuals, including capturing devices, working hours, response times, coverage areas, and feedback. The devices reviewed include those that use image processing, computer vision, and machine learning techniques to assist users with visual impairments. The review also discussed the features of the assistive devices, such as the type of sensors used, their working hours, response time, coverage area, and feedback mechanisms. The devices were also evaluated on their ability to assist users in different scenarios, such as indoor and outdoor environments. However, the review concluded that at the time of the review, there was no single device that met all the requirements for designing assistive technology for visually impaired individuals. In conclusion, the review highlights the need for continued research and development in assistive technology for visually impaired individuals to create devices that can meet the needs of all users. The review suggests that it is important to consider the trade-offs between different features when designing assistive technology for visually impaired individuals, in order to provide the best possible assistance to users in different scenarios. For this reason, we aim to provide a fully provisioned system for persons with visually impaired that will contain 5 modules which are MRI Alzheimer’s detection, OCR, Sign to Speech, Object detection, and face detection that will help the visually impaired to perform basic functions

Three pre-trained networks were shortlisted to detect Alzheimer’s in an MRI image VGG-16, Resnet50, SE Resnet50 of which Resnet seemed to be more accurate than the others [Theckedath and Sedamkar (2020](#ch75.xhtml#ref75_3)). The Haar cascade classifier is used due to its quick result, low computational costs, and reliability ([Hyun et al., 2021](#ch75.xhtml#ref75_5)). The Haar cascade for face detection then uses the LBPH (local binary pattern histogram) algorithm for face recognition due to its known performance and ability to recognize the face from the frontal, rear, or side view ([Hwang et al., 2019](#ch75.xhtml#ref75_6)). The sign-to-speech module will be carried out using a regular CNN with tuned pre-trained models ([Ahmed et al., 2022](#ch75.xhtml#ref75_7)). Pytesseract the wrapper for google ocr and Python will be used for the OCR module ([Tafti et al., 2016](#ch75.xhtml#ref75_8); [Hegghammer, 2022](#ch75.xhtml#ref75_9)). Object detection is carried out using the Caffe model ([Ikeda et al., 2019](#ch75.xhtml#ref75_10)). The output is in the form of an audio stream which is converted with the help of GTTS (Google text to speech) [Kaur and Singh (2022](#ch75.xhtml#ref75_11)).

## Related Works

In the field of assistive technology for the visually impaired, there have been several studies and projects related to camera-based text recognition and object identification that has ranged over a long period of time with significant developments. Martinek et al. (2019) presented an OCR system that can perform two crucial tasks: analyzing the layout of a page, including identifying text blocks and lines and recognizing text using OCR. [Hyun et al., (2021](#ch75.xhtml#ref75_5)) An architecture for face detection using a Haar classifier was proposed that aims to enhance the computational speed of the system. This is achieved by eliminating unnecessary iterations during the classification process hence increasing the processing speed by 4.46%, which can be beneficial for real-time applications such as security systems and video surveillance. Additionally, the use of Haar classifiers in this architecture is a conventional system for detecting faces in images, making it a reliable and robust solution (Wu and Zhang, 2021) an experiment with a 99.85 accuracy rate achieved by the improved facenet in the experiment which demonstrates the ability to effectively recognize faces in real-time. A face detection and recognition system that uses this technology can detect and recognize faces with high accuracy.

Sustainability is a key concern in face detection systems, as they often rely on small processing units.

[Holanda et al., (2018](#ch75.xhtml#ref75_15)) proposed a reading system was proposed that utilizes a portable device and combines ML techniques, segmentation, and feature extraction to achieve an accuracy of 99.86% and a specificity of 99.3%. The system integrates a central moments extractor with a multi-layer perceptron.

[Wang et al., (2022](#ch75.xhtml#ref75_16)) 400 training images and 100 gaze attention maps were classified using a classification algorithm that has Resnet 50 as a backbone. The first initial epochs don’t show considerable improvement but after 10 epochs there was significant improvement Resnet 50 proved to be a conventional system to classify medical images.

## Proposed Methodology

Our objective is to develop a Dual Aid system that comprises two main components: the Doctor’s Aid and the Patient’s Aid. The Doctor’s Aid module is designed to offer doctors a preliminary understanding and a starting point for analyzing MRI scans of patients with Alzheimer’s disease. This model can be deployed on a server to provide local access within the hospital’s network. Considering that visual impairment is a common symptom of Alzheimer’s disease, the Patient’s Aid is divided into four sub-modules that can help patients with Alzheimer’s perform basic activities. These sub-modules include face detection for identifying family members, object detection for recognizing common objects in the environment, OCR for reading large print signs, and sign-to-speech, which allows patients who communicate via sign language to converse directly with their doctors.

### *Doctors Aid*

We propose an ensemble method that concatenates Resnet 50 and Xception that will perform a multiclass classification of four categories of **MRI** images, namely Mild Demented, Moderate Demented, Very Mild Demented, and Non-Demented.

#### Resnet50 and Xception

The reason for choosing this approach is that ResNet50 and Xception have complementary strengths - ResNet50 is proficient at capturing long-range dependencies, while Xception excels at capturing local features. Since the details in **MRI** images are often subtle, combining both these architectures allowed us to capture both local and global features accurately. We selected ResNet50 for its complexity, having 50 layers, which makes it more effective at capturing complex patterns present in MRI images, crucial for dementia classification. Furthermore, ResNet50 is a conventional backbone algorithm for classifying medical images, making it a preferred choice. We leveraged the pre-trained weights of ResNet50 from ImageNet dataset to bring prior knowledge to the task of dementia classification. Similarly, Xception, known to work well with ImageNet weights, was combined with ResNet50. The availability of a wide range of resources for both ResNet50 and Xception made it feasible to use them together to form an Ensemble method. Resnet 50 is an adaptation of the Resnet model having 50 layers which consist of 48 convolutional layers with 1 Average pool and 1 Max pool layer. Furthermore, Xception uses skip or residual connections to facilitate the flow of information from earlier layers to later layers, allowing the network to preserve significant information throughout the training process. This is accomplished by adding shortcut connections between the layers of the network, allowing for direct communication between them.

#### Patients Aid

The primary module of the patient’s aid is the face detection module where the Haar cascade classifier is used due to its quick result, low computational costs, and reliability. The Haar cascade for face detection then uses the LBPH (local binary pattern histogram) algorithm for face recognition due to its known performance and ability to recognize the face from the frontal, rear or side view. Optical character recognition also known as OCR will be carried out by pytesseract that will help the patients read big signs. For object detection we are using the Caffe model that can detect multiple objects in a screen Sign to speech will be carried out with a Pretrained CNN Sequential model. These algorithms have been selected upon extensive literature survey so that the selected algorithms work properly in all conditions where speed or accuracy is not compromised for reliance.

## Simulation and Analysis

We performed simulations to investigate the behavior of different algorithms with different optimizers. We experimented with several algorithms and optimizers, and after analyzing the results, we shortlisted two algorithms: Xception and Resnet 50. Xception is a variant of the Inception network, while Resnet 50 is a variant of the Resnet network. Furthermore, we shortlisted three known optimizers for these algorithms: Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) optimizer, Adaptive Moment Estimation (Adam) optimizer, and Root Mean Square Propagation (Rrnsprop) optimizer. These optimizers are widely used in deep learning for optimizing the parameters of neural networks. The shortlisting process was based on the performance of the algorithms with the different optimizers, computational efficiency, or other relevant factors. The shortlisted algorithms and optimizers were hence chosen to be further analyzed and compared to determine the best combination for a specific task.

As observed for the given dataset Resnet 50 performed better with the Sgd optimizer giving us a more stable test accuracy and also higher highs and less lower lows as compared to Adam optimizer. Similar observations were observed for Xception paired with Sgd and Adams optimizers It was additionally noticed that Xception wasn’t able to get trained effectively during initial epochs and there was an accuracy drop of around 10-12% in the testing accuracy. Resnet 50 and Xception concatenated with SGD optimizer performs with increased stability through the epochs. Extra Augmented data was added to the ensemble model. All the simulations were carried out for 10 epochs with a learning rate of 0.001. Rms prop doesn’t seem to be a competent optimizer for this ensemble method as we can see there is a difference of about 15 % and fluctuation in the test accuracy.

The Patient’s Aid module was able to perform the respective functions during testing which was run on a simulative software that had 5 buttons that have different functions

Fig. 3. Patient's Aid User Interface

## Conclusion

In conclusion, an effective framework has been built for a multiclass classification where an ensemble method of concatenating the Xcpetion and Resnet 50 algorithm paired with the Sgd optimizer has proved to be a viable method to classify the available MRI axial cut images. However, we need to extend the functionality of this framework to include the coronal and sagittal brain slices and add other data modalities such as FDG-Positron Emission Tomography (PET), FDG-Positron Emission Tomography (PET), Structural Magnetic resonance Imaging (SMRI), Computer Tomography (CT) and Functional Magnetic Resonance (Fmri). The face detection module, Sign to speech, object detection, and OCR module are good solutions that can help the visually impaired to do basic functionalities which were achieved in a simulative process

# Developing an Internet of Things based soil moisture prediction

S. Shenbagavadivu,^([^(61)](#fn61))

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-76](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-76)

## Abstract

Farming is the country’s distinct sector of the economy. Agriculture’s primary issues include groundwater, fertilize; and conservation tillage. The freshwater resources, which are already stressed, are being used extravagantly in many countries. The water utilization for agricultural irrigation can be optimized using the Internet of Things and machine learning approaches. In an IoT-driven smart irrigation framework, a Floret impregnation- Artificial Neural Network (FI-ANN) has been used to forecast the quantity of soil moisture in a field. Future soil moisture is predicted using field data from the deployed sensors (air temperature, air humidity, soil moisture, soil temperature, radiation), as well as online weather forecast information. According to experimental findings, an average RMSE is 0.0019. The effectiveness of various ML methods for predicting future soil moisture is examined, and the GBRT results are quite promising.

Keywords: Internet of things, Soil moisture, Agricultural irrigation, Machine learning, Floret impregnation-artificial neural network

## Introduction

Cultivation plays a critical role in the progress of every country. It has made a significant commitment to improving the nation’s economy. The assessment of authentic soil is a crucial measure for aiding growth in the agricultural turn of events. Soil testing is a key barrier to improving agricultural output. Currently, continuous soil testing is done manually, which is exceedingly night before going to bed and prone to human mistakes. In agriculture, forecasting soil type is crucial for enhancing yield output. To minimize manual measurement of soil borders, a variety of sensors including soil moisture, ambient temperature, and soil additives such as nitrogen, phosphoric, and potassium are utilized to identify soil boundaries (NPK). In accordance with the soil barrier values, the type of soil is predicted. To avoid the present soil testing procedure, ranchers might use the proposed technique to incorporate essential composts for growing. Ranchers require more current agricultural and technological ideas to aid them in increasing productivity. By employing an IoT-based agriculture framework, soil kinds are sensed and appropriate yields are recognized. Agriculture is dependent on topographical areas and climatic conditions in designated places. It really assists ranchers in expanding the development of any produce. Tailored crop proposal framework based on topography. It gets the contribution from the client and gives customized suggestions pertinent to their area and their past development. ## Result and Discussion

With the field-sent sensor hub, the sensors’ information is accumulated hourly for 37 straight days. The analysis takes into account the minimum amount of soil moisture for the day and daily averages of air temperature, humidity, UV radiation, and soil temperature. The data also comes from a weather forecasting website that is used to predict soil moisture levels for the coming days.

The data are sent to the local host computer via a web service. The newly received data is then analyzed using the machine learning algorithms that were discussed earlier. Scikit-learn, Pandas, and Matplotlib, all Python-based analysis tools, are utilized.

The forecast of a field’s soil moisture over the next few days can help with planning and provisioning for appropriate irrigation, as previously stated. Learning about the environmental conditions and factors (such as temperature, humidity, and UV) for the upcoming day can be made easier with the help of online weather forecast information. Prediction models based on machine learning can be made from the sensor data that has been collected over time. These models can be used to estimate soil moisture for the next day based on the weather and environment that is expected.

This study discusses two approaches for predicting soil moisture. In the first method, in addition to the other weather-projection characteristics (air temperature, humidity, and UV), the anticipated soil temperature is used to predict the subsequent days’ soil moisture. The soil temperature is ignored by the second method for predicting soil moisture.

In [Table 1](#ch76.xhtml#tab76_1), the RMSE of the applicable machine learning approaches are compared to determine their accuracy. The results demonstrate that when temperature is one of the parameters used to estimate soil moisture, the GBRT performs better.

## Research Methodology

Predictive models developed may be adapted for both agricultural irrigation and urbanized areas. The creation of a smart irrigation system changes a farmer’s life. This study presents an intelligent irrigation architecture based on For anticipating moisture content, a hybrid technique based on IoT and artificial training is used. Since soil moisture is a key factor in determining how much water should be utilized for irrigation, ML approaches are used to estimate soil moisture for the following days using data from field sensors and weather forecasts. When the results of several ML approaches are analyzed, the findings of the GBRT-based approach are highly positive. In many water-stressed countries like India, such techniques might help to maximize the use of irreplaceable fresh water supplies for agriculture.

# Mitigation of Threats in Cloud Using Ensemble Hybrid Machine Learning

S. Divya^([^(62)](#fn62))

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-77](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-77)

## Abstract

Researchers have utilized a broad variety of machine learning techniques throughout the past few years in order to identify network attacks without having extensive prior knowledge about the characteristics of these attacks. Due to the complexity of the model, however, traditional machine learning methods are unable to generate one-of-a-kind feature descriptors. Consequently, this limitation applies to the entire field. The difficulty in characterizing the attack detection challenge is directly correlated to this fact. In this paper, various supervised deep learning models are combined to form an ensemble framework to detect and mitigate the attacks in cloud. The supervised deep learning models include generative adversarial networks, autoencoders, convolutional neural network, and recurrent neural network. These unsupervised ensemble models act as a base classifier and the output is obtained from the meta classifier to classify the attacks. The results of simulation show’s that the proposed method has higher rate of classification accuracy than the existing ensemble models.

Keywords: Threats Mitigation, Cloud, Machine Learning

## Introduction

The benefits drawn from a wide range of sources are made available to a large number of users of networked computers thanks to the continuous growth and widespread acceptance of the Internet. On the other hand, as the number of people who are dependent on the networks continues to climb, the importance of taking precautions to keep them secure will only become more pressing. The goal of network security is to prevent unauthorized users from gaining access to resources like computers, networks, programs, data, and so on and making modifications to them ([Ahsan et al., 2022](#ch77.xhtml#ref77_1)).

However, when more and more systems related to finance, e-commerce, and the military go online, they become easier targets for network attacks, which puts them in great danger and exposes them to catastrophic damage. This places them in a position where they could be severely damaged ([Berghout et al., 2022](#ch77.xhtml#ref77_2)). It is vital to have effective tactics for identifying threats, repelling them, and preserving the safety of networks. Additionally, it is essential to have such strategies. An extra layer of complexity arises from the fact that various forms of attack typically call for a variety of responses. Therefore, figuring out how to recognize new and previously unknown forms of network attack is the most important task facing those who work in the field of network security ([Singh et al., 2021](#ch77.xhtml#ref77_3)).

Deep learning approaches, so-called because of the general design of deep layers used to tackle complex problems, represent a major development in the capacity of machine learning to mimic the structure of the human brain with the architecture of neural networks. Deep learning approaches are so-called because of the general design of deep layers used to tackle complex problems ([Daghigh et al., 2021](#ch77.xhtml#ref77_4)). The general design of the deep learning algorithms that are used to tackle complex issues is where the term deep learning derives from. One of the most notable initiatives for the game of Go to use the capabilities of a common deep-learning structure ([Unal et al., 2022](#ch77.xhtml#ref77_5)).

The objective is to give academics interested in applying deep learning methods to the study of network security a fundamental understanding of deep learning so they can get started. A substantial amount of work has been done that, in essence, focuses on the application of deep learning approaches to detect attacks. The term “deep learning techniques” refers to this [Gupta et al. (2022](#ch77.xhtml#ref77_6)).

Our research is based on the conclusions of several prior literature evaluations ([Sharma and Singh, 2022](#ch77.xhtml#ref77_7); [Alsoufi et al., 2021](#ch77.xhtml#ref77_8); [Arul et al., 2021](#ch77.xhtml#ref77_9); [Gheibi et al., 2021](#ch77.xhtml#ref77_10)) that look into the potential of deep learning to address the problem of attack detection. These evaluations look into the possibility of using deep learning to the problem of attack detection. These reviews look into the several applications that deep learning could have.

With the support of IoT security approaches that have been trained with deep learning, we are able to obtain a clear understanding of how various hacks are carried out and how to defend against them. A method that detects breaches by utilizing deep learning and analyzing the similarities and differences across four very big data sets.

In order to accomplish the goal of explaining the deep learning algorithms and the applications to which they are most suited, this step was taken. This one, in particular, focuses on the specifics of attack detection, such as malware analysis, spam detection, and intrusion detection, amongst other issues that are linked to attack detection. In contrast to broader, more comprehensive overviews, this one is more focused.

In this paper, we develop a supervised machine learning framework that enables better detection of issues and threats in cloud computing services. The supervised machine learning framework uses an ensemble framework to detect the issues and threats for detection and mitigation in cloud.

## Related Works

Convolutional neural networks have been the focus of a great deal of intriguing studies and applications in recent years, notably in the area of network security ([Sun et al., 2022](#ch77.xhtml#ref77_11)). The authors employ recursive and convolutional network layers to build a neural network that can mimic a malware detection system. This work is meant to lead to the acquisition of classification qualities. The method suggested combines two different types of feature extraction approaches to produce a hierarchical feature extraction architecture: the convolutional operation in the convolutional layer and the sequence modeling in the recursive network layer. The most desirable features of the two different styles of are combined in this architecture.

The input for their network is the original short strings, and it extracts features to classify the strings using character-level embeddings. The eXpose neural network (XNN) is a method that the authors in [Aziz et al. (2022](#ch77.xhtml#ref77_12)) present as a mechanism for identifying attack signals in advance. When compared to methods that serve as baselines and are based on the manual extraction of features, the design of eXpose self-extracted features emerges as the undeniable victor. It is stated that the wide diversity and high level of complexity of their initial inputs make algorithm processing difficult. In spite of this, it reduces the false alarm rate in contrast to these baselines, which suggests that the automatic feature extraction process in CNN is not robust enough and not fair enough without the addition of additional or even noisy input.

It is extremely necessary to have the ability to identify malicious web shells in order to guarantee the network continuing safety. The authors in [Sayadi et al. (2021](#ch77.xhtml#ref77_13)) provide a word2vec format as well as a CNN-based hazardous detection method for the analysis of HTTP request data. Because this is the very first time that word2vec and CNN have been attempted to be integrated in the context of malicious detection, this body of work carries a great deal of significance. They begin by discussing the word2vec software, which is distinguished by the fact that it makes use of feature representations of HTTP-obtained words. The web request is then characterized as a matrix of a size that has been calculated in advance by using the features that have been strung together. A model has been eventually built for the classification of shells, and it makes use of a CNN framework. Although many various kinds of experiments are carried out, the suggested method outperforms the relevant conventional classifiers in every single set of tests that are carried out.

A classification approach for end-to-end encrypted communication that is based on a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (CNN) is described in [Qazi et al. (2022](#ch77.xhtml#ref77_14)). This approach unifies the processes of feature extraction, feature selection, and classifier application under a single framework with the intention of attaining robust performance in attack detection using the CNN architecture. Additionally, it shows how the authors intend to employ 1D-CNN as the learning algorithm for the network. This enables the network to automatically learn the association between automatically extracted features and outputs that are associated with anticipated labels. This is made possible by the fact that the network is given this information.

An AE and DNN based hybrid deep learning technique was employed in [Khan (2021](#ch77.xhtml#ref77_15)) to identify malicious code. To be more specific, they make use of AE in order to move their emphasis from the excessive detail that was contained in the initial data to the most important components of the data. This is accomplished by shifting their focus from excessive information to the most crucial components of the data. Using a DBN- based learning model that includes multilayer RBM and a layer of BPNN in order to find the malicious code is the next step in the process. This step is necessary in order to move on to the next stage of the process. They were able to fine-tune the entire network to build the most effective hybrid model once they found out that each RBM layer had been trained unsupervised and that each BP layer had been trained supervised. This information allowed them to develop the most accurate results possible. We were able to achieve this by providing each BP layer with supervised instruction. Experiments have shown that their hybrid network is superior to DBN-based networks in terms of its ability to accurately detect threats. These DBN-based networks were previously employed.

The authors in [Tran et al. (2022](#ch77.xhtml#ref77_16)) outline an innovative technique for analyzing traffic that is centered around CNN. A two-dimensional representation of the data on network traffic is presented by this method. These researchers demonstrated their findings by utilizing the dataset provided by the USTC-TRC2016 flow competition. Specifically, they used it to show that their method achieves an average classification accuracy of 99%.

The authors in [Hou et al. (2021](#ch77.xhtml#ref77_17)) use an ensemble network to categorize the many forms of attack that have been documented. To be more specific, the neural network learns the knowledge necessary to classify things by applying a collection of classifiers. These classifiers help the neural network obtain the knowledge it needs to classify things. After that, it compiles the results of all of these classifiers into a single set in order to make accurate predictions. In order to increase performance when differentiating regular behaviors from abnormal ones, the technique that is being suggested incorporates not just an AE but also a BNN, a DNN, and an extreme learning machine. It has been demonstrated that the performance of employing a multitude of classifiers for the detection task is superior to the performance of employing just one classifier for the task. The results of their suggested ensemble technique are exciting in the right direction.

An ensemble structure is presented in [Omer et al. (2021](#ch77.xhtml#ref77_18)) as a technique of strengthening the stability of neural networks for the detection of malware. This is accomplished through the use of many networks working together. This structure is based on the principle that superior results can be achieved by integrating a large number of different classification methods. During the training phase, a collection of neural networks is built, and the individual classifiers are responsible for the maintenance and upkeep of their own statistics. This may involve the conversion of input data as well as the preservation of semantic context. A vote is taken from a range of classifiers to determine which samples will be labeled during the testing phase of the project. When applied to the task of finding a solution to the problem provided by the AICS 2019, their proposed ensemble structure demonstrates great levels of both accuracy and recall.

## Feature Selection

The CFS that is discussed in this research has the potential to not only improve the selection of features but also the precision with which they are classified. This method examines the selected subset of features to determine how relevant and redundant they are in relation to the search space that has been provided. This assists in locating the most optimal solution feasible.

## Correlation-Based Feature Selection

Correlation-based feature selection refers to the algorithms that choose features based on evaluations that are based on correlations. These algorithms are also sometimes referred to as CFS algorithms. Repeating characteristics, on the other hand, are chosen for inclusion because they are linked to a number of other characteristics in the same category.

This method prioritizes subsets whose characteristics are strongly related to the class while being relatively unrelated to the characteristics of other subsets. In order for a feature to be included, it must be able to make predictions about classes that cannot be made using any other features that are already accessible in the instance space. The following is an illustration of one function that may be utilized to compare the characteristics of CFS subgroups:

  
$$M\_{s} = \\frac{kr\_{cf}}{\\sqrt{k + k(k - 1) + r\_{f}}}$$  

On the basis of the equation presented above, we are able to draw certain inferences regarding the following three variables:

> *M*[s] - feature subset evaluation,
> 
> *r*[cf] - mean correlation degree between
> 
> *r*[f] - average inter-correlation degree between.

The value of the CFS is determined by analyzing the correlations that exist between its various subsets of attributes. Finding the feature set that has the highest value *r*[cf] enables a large reduction *r*[f] in the overall size of the datasets that are used for training and testing purposes. This is possible because of finding the feature set that has the greatest value.

## Belife Network

One can classify deep belief networks into two groups: those that use backpropagation neural networks (BPNN or BP) with a single layer and restricted Boltzmann machines (RBM) with many layers of unsupervised learning networks. These two kinds of networks both train their models using constrained Boltzmann machines (DBN). The open and hidden layers of neurons make up this neural network, which is structured as an undirected graph model.

A neural network whose generation structure is selected at random is known as a random bit machine. Training that is done on a layer-by-layer basis is beneficial for DBN because it makes use of the components that are inherent to RBM. The distribution of DBN is represented as below:

  
*J*(*θ*[*k* + 1]) = *J*(*θ*[*k*]) + *α*[*k*]∇*J*(*θ*[*k*])*d*[*k*] + *o*(*θ*[*k*])  

DBN was utilized by the researchers in this investigation in order to identify malicious software. The researchers trained a multilayer generative model using unsupervised learning in order to counteract the tendency of DBNs toward overfitting

## Unsupervised Generative Adversarial Network

One of the most promising unsupervised learning systems that has been proposed in recent years is called the generative adversarial network (GAN). This system makes use of the property of finding intrinsic patterns in data in order to develop new examples, and it is one of the systems that has been suggested in recent years. The concept of a game in which there is neither a winner nor a loser was a significant motivation for the development of GAN. It plays a never-ending game within the setting of a deep neural network called who will generate and who will discriminate, which is necessary for it to get to the stage where it can learn a distributed representation of real-world data.

This is essential for it to get to the point where it can learn a distributed representation of real-world data. On the other hand, the objective is to ascertain whether or not a particular data set is the product of genuine data by simulating, modeling, and learning the distributional characteristics of real data. These two objectives are opposed to the objective of the task, which is to establish whether or not a particular data set is the product of actual data collection. Both their capacity for production and their capacity to differentiate between different objects can benefit from the ongoing rivalry between these internal models.

## Supervised *Cnn*

The convolutional computation and the depth structure that they use make convolutional neural networks, more commonly referred to as CNNs, a technology that is emblematic of deep learning and is used extensively in this field. CNNs are also referred to by their more common name, convolutional neural networks. In particular, CNN makes advantage of a multilayer perception variant design, which calls for the user to perform essentially no preprocessing at all.

In addition to the input and output layers, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) contain a number of other levels that are not visible to the user. The convolution layer, the pooling layer, and the complete connection layer are all components of these layers. CNN has a number of benefits that other categorization systems do not possess. To make features, it does not require any prior information and does not require as much preprocessing as other methods do. These are two of the most essential benefits.

## Supervised Recurrent Neutral Network

RNNs are a special kind of neural network structure that is endowed with a memory function in order to store information that was acquired in the past. This function was developed solely to be utilized with input that varies over the course of time. RNNs are particularly well suited for application with this kind of data. This choice in design is consistent with the hypothesis that human cognition is based on previous experience and memory. This hypothesis helps to explain why RNN performs so well when it is presented with time-series data.

RNNs still face substantial fundamental design issues, such as gradient disappearance and gradient explosion, which prevent them from remembering or modeling long-term relationships. This is one of the reasons why RNNs are not widely used. The first of these issues is referred to as gradient vanishing, and the second of these issues is referred to as gradient explosion. As a result of this, researchers have developed LSTM and GRU with gates and memory cells. Both of these types of networks are able to recall long-term relationships by successfully navigating essential elements of the flow of information.

## Conclusions

In this paper, the ensemble architecture allows us to utilize supervised machine learning methods for improved problem and threat detection in cloud computing services. Using a supervised machine learning framework, vulnerabilities and risks in the cloud can be discovered and mitigated by employing an ensemble architecture. Using the meta-classifier output from the ensemble base classifier can help reduce the impact of attacks. The resilience of the model against different types of attacks is examined through the simulation. Simulations show that the proposed solution is superior to the status quo in terms of problem detection and assault prevention.

# Detection of Insects, Birds, and Wild Animals in Farming Land Using Regional Convolutional Neural Network

Mrs. N. Rajeswari,^([^(63)](#fn63))

E-mail: [csrajee2007@gmail.com](http://www.csrajee2007@gmail.com); [kavithad.mca@spiher.ac.in](http://www.kavithad.mca@spiher.ac.in)

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-78](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-78)

## Abstract

In this paper, we aim to find the objects that create disturbances for farming in its area and this includes insects, birds, and wild animals. The suggested technique is created such that it facilitates the detection of these things and it performs theft monitoring in the farming area. This research work would involve a sensor used to detect obstacles like an animal or bird, temperature, and humidity of the farming area, and the information will pass to the mobile application using IoT. Obstacle detection can be proposed with the help Regional Convolution Neural Network.

Keywords: Detection, Farming Land, Wild Animals, Regional Convolutional Neural Network

## Introduction

The first people to domesticate land and raise crops marked a significant turning point in the development of human history. Farming practices have been subjected to a considerable evolution over the past century because of improvements in agricultural technology and the expansion of global agricultural markets ([Ramos et al., 2022](#ch78.xhtml#ref78_1)).

These days, one of the most essential things for a farm to undertake is to take precautions to protect both its agricultural products and its livestock. Wild animals are responsible for a significant amount of the agricultural crop loss that occurs across most of India ([Petrović et al., 2022](#ch78.xhtml#ref78_2)).

The amount of food that can be gathered will drastically decrease because of animal interference on land used for agriculture. Because of this, a great number of farmers will experience huge financial losses. During field research, it was shown that wild animals were responsible for the loss of an average of 36% of the crop. As a possible solution to this issue, we suggest the creation of a robotic system that would prevent wild animals from entering farms ([Faruque et al., 2022](#ch78.xhtml#ref78_3)).

To overcome this issue, it is necessary to develop a region-based deep learning model that should detect the obstacles in the farming landscape ([Naveen et al., 2022](#ch78.xhtml#ref78_5)).

In this paper, the objects like insects, birds, or wild animals are detected using Regional Convolution Neural Network. The proposed method enables the detection of objects and it performs theft monitoring in the farming area. This research work would involve a sensor used to detect obstacles like animals or birds, temperature, and humidity of the farming area, and the information will pass to the mobile application using IoT.

## Regional Convolutional Neural Network

With R-CNN, we can locate localized areas that provoke specific emotions. The defined local regions contain not just items and/or sections of objects, but also contexts that have been specially specified for those objects. In other words, defined local regions are a combination of the two.

The region proposal network, a neural network implementation, is created by combining all three of these processes into a single architecture. The construction of candidate boxes, the extraction of features, and the classification of the features that were extracted are the steps that make up these steps.

The RPN can complete the training in its entirety as well as the detection procedure in its whole. The RPN can process images of any size and generate a list of potential candidate boxes. The degree to which a candidate box matches the target box will be considered when determining a score for that box competition.

The output convolutional feature map from the previous layer is available to both the large and the small networks, but only the small network may slide over it. A low-dimensional vector is produced as the output of the sliding-window layer. This vector is then fed into two layers that are connected and have levels that are like one another. To carry out regression and classification, these layers make use of a rectangular frame.

Faster R-CNN proposes a novel approach to anchoring, according to their findings. At each position along the sliding window, [Fig. 2](#ch78.xhtml#fig78_2). offers a graphical illustration of how the rectangular frame regression layer generates 4*k* outputs, also known as the coordinate values of K boxes. The classification layer for rectangular frames contains a total of 2*k* outputs that are ready for usage.

![Fig. 2. Region proposal network](images/fig78_2_B.jpg)

[Fig. 2. Region proposal network](#ch78.xhtml#R_fig78_2)

The placement of the center of the sliding window that is currently active is determined by the geometric center that lies at the *k* box (*x*[1], *y*[1], *x*[2], *y*[2]). Even when employing three distinct sizes and three different ratios, For each possible point in the sliding window, k = 9 anchors are still employed, same like in faster R-CNN. This is the case even when *k =* 9 anchors are being used.

Each anchor is assigned either a target, also known as a positive label, or a non-target, depending on what kind of assignment they receive (also known as a neutral label). The multitasking loss strategy used by the Fast R-CNN network is incorporated into the architecture of the Faster R-CNN network.

## Convergence Feature Sharing

The RPN network and the Fast R-CNN network can be trained jointly rather than separately thanks to a recently developed piece of technology from the Faster R-CNN system. This is made possible by the RPN network. The flexibility to switch back and forth between two distinct optimization strategies is the engine that powers this four-stage method.

1.  Step 1 A pre-trained model is used during the first stage of the process to create initial values for the network parameters, and the RPN network is then subjected to fine-tuning.
2.  Step 2 In the second stage of the process, the initialized RPN network is used to extract the suggested region for training the Fast R-CNN network. The RPN network is utilized in this stage.
3.  Step 3 Re-initialize the RPN utilizing the Fast R-CNN N/W that was built in Step 2 with the main goal of optimizing the RPN unique layer.
4.  Step 4 Modify to the settings for the convolutional layer.
5.  Step 5 The fifth and final stage consists of applying the RPN extracted region proposal to the Fast R-CNN to make any necessary improvements.

## Non-Maximum Suppression

It is possible to measure the degree to which two rectangular boxes overlap one another by utilizing a ratio known as the intersection-over-union (IoU) ratio. This ratio may be found in the below equation

(18)  
IoU(A, B) = (A∩^()B)/(A∪^()B)  

A technique known as non-maximum suppression (NMS), after locating the highest possible values, hides them all by a predetermined standard operating procedure. To get rid of unnecessary windows, the NMS is usually utilized in the process of target detection.

# A Trifold Authentication Using Elliptical Cryptography in Cloud Computing

K. Komathi^([^(64)](#fn64))

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-79](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-79)

## Abstract

Processing in the cloud and storing data in the cloud are gaining a growing number of users as a direct result of developments in networking technology and the continuously rising demand for more computing power and storage space. In other words, the demand for more computing power and storage space is driving the adoption of cloud computing. Recent attacks have shown that personal information can be disclosed, computing tasks can be maliciously altered and cloud services can be disabled for users. In this paper, we develop a trifold authentication scheme to secure the data via proper authentication in cloud. This model uses hash chains to achieve the above aim. The simulation is conducted to test the efficacy of the authentication in cloud. The results show that the proposed method has a reduced rate of complexity than the existing methods.

Keywords: Cloud, Authentication, Elliptical curve cryptography

## Introduction

Through the usage of cloud computing, consumers and organizations are liberated from the obligations of data storage and computation that have historically been their responsibility ([Tiwari and Gangadharan, 2021](#ch79.xhtml#ref79_1)). Users and organizations alike are now able to store data and carry out computations on computers located in remote locations thanks to the advent of cloud computing ([Anuradha et al., 2021](#ch79.xhtml#ref79_2)).

Users that sign up for the public cloud get access to the platform that is provided by the cloud service provider once they have completed the registration process. Users can save information in the cloud, which may later be accessed by other users and shared. Because it is stored in the cloud, your data is accessible whenever you need it and from any location you choose ([AlAhmad et al., 2021](#ch79.xhtml#ref79_3)).

Cloud storage has a lot of advantages, but it also has a lot of drawbacks because of the open nature of the platform and the absence of any security measures. Cloud storage is vulnerable to a wide variety of threats ([Rangwani and Om, 2021](#ch79.xhtml#ref79_4)). Many of the items that we save in the cloud, such as our profiles on various social networking platforms and our medical records, could be considered to be information that is either secret or private. It is of the utmost importance to make certain that these data are kept private and that implementation of safe data exchange is carried out ([Safkhani et al., 2021](#ch79.xhtml#ref79_5)).

Because the vast majority of cloud service providers have not yet installed necessary security controls, user data is freely viewable and can be accessed in a variety of ways. In order to achieve their goal of increasing revenues, they will even resort to utilizing the personal information of users. In addition to this, the attacker has the capability of accessing and stealing the private information of users that have been saved in the cloud ([Fatima and Ahmad, 2021](#ch79.xhtml#ref79_6); [Olakanmi and Odeyemi, 2021](#ch79.xhtml#ref79_7); Padmaj a and Seshadri, 2021).

The privacy of their information that has been outsourced must be protected at all times. Users also have the choice of making their information accessible to friends or to the person who initially launched the inquiry into the information. It is essential to have an access control system that is not only reliable but also adaptable. In this paper, we develop a trifold authentication scheme to secure the data via proper authentication in cloud.

## Related works

[Wang et al. (2009](#ch79.xhtml#ref79_9)) advocated that cryptography should be used to enable changeable access control by encrypting each data block with a unique key. They did this by using cryptography. Cryptography was utilized in order to complete this task. In this approach, symmetric cryptography employing the shared secret key is applied, which enables the supply of mutual authentication.

When it comes to cloud computing, data privacy, and security are two of the most important concerns. [Chen and Zhao (2012](#ch79.xhtml#ref79_10)) carried out an in-depth analysis of these issues over the whole of the data life cycle, analyzed the effectiveness of various potential solutions, and outlined potential avenues for further research. The safety of storing data on the cloud and collaborating on that data is the primary topic of investigation in this study. The following is a synopsis of a few relevant research, with the primary attention being placed on the application of symmetric encryption, identity-based encryption, and attribute-based encryption in cloud storage systems.

However, because this method depends on the data owner delivering the paired keys to both the service provider and the end users, it takes a considerable amount of storage space. It is now possible to encrypt and decrypt user private information that is saved in the cloud thanks to a solution that was released by [Ramesh et al. (2017](#ch79.xhtml#ref79_11)) and is based on the secure e-stream cipher ChaCha20. This makes it possible for user information to be protected from prying eyes.

[Li et al. (2009](#ch79.xhtml#ref79_9)) presented a novel strategy for the authentication of cloud computing that was founded on the identity-based hierarchical architecture (IHA). This strategy was revolutionary because it took advantage of the benefits offered by cloud computing. Interdomain identity-based proxy re-encryption is a method that was developed by [Tang et al. (2008](#ch79.xhtml#ref79_14)) to securely transfer sensitive information between users who are located in different domains.

[Wang et al. (2009](#ch79.xhtml#ref79_9)) introduced a revolutionary IBPRE+ intending to make it easier and more secure for users of social cloud environments to share information. The method makes use of a delegator to generate re-encryption keys, which can be less taxing on the computer resources of the person who owns the data.

[Tang et al. (2008](#ch79.xhtml#ref79_14)) established the collusion attack against Tang approach, and they proposed a different method of data storage based on identities that is resistant to collusion attacks and can handle both local and remote inquiries. This method of data storage is based on identities. This type of data storage makes use of identities, and it is capable of responding to inquiries made both locally and remotely.

[Ruj et al. (2012](#ch79.xhtml#ref79_15)) presented a method for authenticated access control that is decentralized and intended for use with cloud storage. This technique does not necessitate the knowledge of user identities to carry out authentication, which means that the privacy of users is preserved. Later, they presented a new anonymous authentication system for cloud storage that was a decentralized access control mechanism. The data were encrypted utilizing an approach known as attribute-based encryption (ABE), and authentication was carried out utilizing an approach known as attribute- based signature (ABS), both of which are detailed in [Maji et al. (2008](#ch79.xhtml#ref79_16)).

## Proposed Method

Each server in a single-server system must be registered by a mobile user in order for the latter to access the services. The mobile user has to keep several SCs and credentials after being registered on multiple SSS servers, which may be annoying for a mobile user.

Non-centralized design increases the risk of intruders, which has an impact on the whole routing process. In current cloud security measures, malicious nodes are removed from the network in order to prevent intrusions. As a result of these rogue nodes, the network as a whole suffers from severe packet loss, which exacerbates the problem of congestion.

[Figure 1](#ch79.xhtml#fig79_1) provides an overview of our data storage platform that is hosted in the cloud at a high level. The *semi-trusted third party* (STTP), cloud storage servers, data owners, and requesters are the four different entities that make up the model. The STTP is responsible for the oversight of the users and servers that make up the cloud storage service and is responsible for supervising them. A user cipher text is saved and backed up on servers that are part of a cloud storage service. This ensures that the user data is secure as illustrated in [Fig. 1](#ch79.xhtml#fig79_1).

![Fig. 1. The system model](images/fig79_1_C.jpg)

[Fig. 1. The system model](#ch79.xhtml#R_fig79_1)

The owner of the data stores encrypted copies of the data on servers that are located in other locations. This reduces the burden that is imposed on the local storage while simultaneously easing the process of accessing the data and enabling the data to be shared at any time and from any location. Those who send in requests do so intending to expose additional people to the material that is kept in the cloud.

A user management center, a key management center, and a data processing center are the three fundamental components that make up the STTP. The user management center is the most crucial of these three components. The User Management Center is the organization that is in charge of resolving any issues that may arise if a current user is deleted or a new user is registered.

The user list (UL) and the revocation list (RL) in the cloud storage system are regularly kept up to date by the system with the most recent list of allowed users and the public keys associated with their accounts. These lists are referred to as user lists and revocation lists, respectively. It is the responsibility of the key management hub to generate a partial private key for each unique user. The plaintext version of the cipher is stored on the servers that are used to store data in the cloud. These servers can provide the ciphertext to the data processing center when it is requested.

Only the STTP is given direct authorization to access the cloud storage servers in our cloud storage model, which keeps the servers secure and prevents unauthorized users from accessing their data. A cloud storage platform will often have its servers dispersed across a number of distinct physical locations.

## Conclusions

In this paper, a reliable protocol that can be used for cloud-based authentication systems is developed. The proposed technique includes the following stages: initializing the system, generating and verifying signatures, registering, logging in and authenticating, and changing the password. Two of the most essential features of the proposed framework are the generation of a dynamic session key and the facilitation of mutual authentication between the gateway node, the distant user, and the sensor node. Both of these features are essential for the operation of the framework. According to the findings of our study, the proposed method is successful against a wide variety of different types of attacks, while simultaneously keeping the promises of safe mutual authentication, complete anonymity, and perfect forward secrecy. We provided evidence to show that the level of security provided by our proposed solution is superior to the level of security provided by the standard that is already in place.

# Binary Classification of Medical Chest X-Ray Using Gaussian Naive Bayes in Machine Learning

S. Shanthi,^([^(65)](#fn65))

E-mail: [sshanthi4961@gmail.com](mailto:sshanthi4961@gmail.com), [manimayur@gmail.com](mailto:manimayur@gmail.com), [dr.murugan.m@gmail.com](mailto:dr.murugan.m@gmail.com)

DOI: [10.1201/9781003430452-80](https://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9781003430452-80)

## Abstract

Artificial Intelligence plays a major role in computer field as it handles large amount of data and prediction is faster and more accurate. Machine learning techniques and deep learning techniques are branches of artificial intelligence with deep learning as a subfamily of Machine learning. Machine learning techniques and deep learning help in the extraction of data to promote the biomedical field ([Tiwari et al., 2018](#ch80.xhtml#ref80_1)). Machine learning became popular and accomplished much better on unstructured data ([Abound & Akpan, 2021](#ch80.xhtml#ref80_2)). As the data increases enormously, the popularity of Machine learning grows. With rapid growth in medical data, classification of medical images plays a vital role in clinical care. The objective of classification is to find the target class ([Perez-Careta et al., 2022](#ch80.xhtml#ref80_3)). The target class should be accurate. Conventional method is time-consuming and need extra endeavor to find the target class.

Keywords: Naive Bayes, Gaussian Naive Bayes, Wiener Filter

## Introduction

Machine learning learns patterns from the past to automate the model and predict the output. Machine learning become a widely used approach as it produces a more prominent result in complex tasks than human performance ([Janiesch et al., 2021](#ch80.xhtml#ref80_4); [Alzubaidi et al., 2021](#ch80.xhtml#ref80_5)). The main goal of Machine learning is to build a model to perform various tasks like object classification, and detection. Handling large amount of complex data and amazing improvement in hardware engineering (ex: High Performance computing technology) increases the popularity of learning. Lung and Lung classification for disease prediction is an important topic for research in recent times The size of the medical image datasets also increases as it is used in hospitals, diagnostic centres etc. [Yadav & Jadhav (2019](#ch80.xhtml#ref80_6)) analysis x-ray for determining pneumonia, with that of the healthy person. This analysis is needed, as determining the affected person with pneumonia is expensive and need a radiologist proficient. To overcome this cumbersome task of classification, this research is about the Gaussian Naive Bayes Algorithm and the chest image processing analysis.

## Related Works

Naive Bayes classifier is used and uses median filter to filter the noise in X-ray images ([Bustomi et al., 2018](#ch80.xhtml#ref80_7)). Classification of image classification is based on the Soft set. Soft set classifier is carried by mean values of the quantities of the classes and classification is carried out by labeling the unknown data ([Lashari & Ibrahim, 2013](#ch80.xhtml#ref80_8)). KNN classification and feature extraction is carried out for the medical classification. Classification on Small-class and imbalanced image data is performed using deep KNN ([Zhuang et al., 2020](#ch80.xhtml#ref80_9)). Ultrasound images are analyzed using various algorithms and show that the Support vector outperforms the other algorithms ([Naziya & Jadhav, 2019](#ch80.xhtml#ref80_10)). Image classification is executed by Bag of Features approach which focuses on vector representation. This is done by Support vector machine and by KNN and their accuracy are calculated. This representation is used find the class of the image ([Loussaief & Abdelkrim, 2018](#ch80.xhtml#ref80_11)). The aim is to find the infected and not infected tuberculosis patient by SVM classifier data. The performance result is 94.7% ([Yahyaoui et al., 2017](#ch80.xhtml#ref80_12)). Lung disease classification is accomplished using very less datasets of images ([Krzhizhanovskaya et al., 2020](#ch80.xhtml#ref80_13)). In [Abu et al, (2019](#ch80.xhtml#ref80_14)) tensor flow framework is used for the classification of various flower images. Using deep neural network, the images are classified and the accuracy obtained is 90%. Yu Zeng et al. carries out random forest and decision tree algorithm and show the noise is reduced. The paper aims on the various input features that is used in medical data. The accuracy obtained from this algorithm is 86% ([Zeng & Cheng, 2021](#ch80.xhtml#ref80_15)). Multivariate Bernoulli Naive Bayes is compared with Multinomial Naive Bayes to categorize of sentiment analysis for a less dataset. [Singh et al, (2019](#ch80.xhtml#ref80_16))gives a comparison between these two algorithms and suggests that Bernoulli Naive Bayes algorithm gives a better result.

## Naive Bayes Classification

Naive Bayes is a simple and powerful algorithm for classifying images, documents, spam filtration, etc. The name “Naive” means integrating attributes that are independent to each other. This means that changes in one attribute in one model will not affect the other one. It is a probabilistic framework and we involve in finding the probability of some features given ([Viet et al, 2021](#ch80.xhtml#ref80_17)). Before the Gaussian Naive Bayes we need to know what conditional probability is and for Probability of X with respect to condition Y.

(1)  
$$P\\left\\lbrack \\frac{X}{Y} \\right\\rbrack = \\frac{P\\lbrack XANDY\\rbrack}{P\\lbrack Y\\rbrack}$$  

The Probability X happens after event Y has occurred already. is the probability of occurrence of both A and B. Bayes classifier states that

(2)  
$$\\text{P}\\left\\lbrack \\frac{\\text{V}}{\\text{U}\_{\\text{i}}} \\right\\rbrack = \\text{P}\\left\\lbrack \\frac{\\text{v}\_{1}}{\\text{U}\_{\\text{j}}} \\right\\rbrack \\ast \\text{P}\\left\\lbrack \\frac{\\text{v}\_{2}}{\\text{U}\_{\\text{j}}} \\right\\rbrack \\ast .. \\ast \\cdot \\text{P}\\left\\lbrack \\frac{\\text{V}\_{n}}{\\text{Uj}\_{\\text{j}}} \\right\\rbrack$$  

$P\\left\\lbrack \\frac{Vj}{Ui} \\right\\rbrack - >$ Posterior probability of the hypothesis is true.

$P\\left\\lbrack \\frac{Ui}{Vj} \\right\\rbrack - >$ Likelihood probability of hypothesis is true

*P* \[*Vj*\] -> Class Prior probability of the hypothesis

*P*\[*Ui*\]-> Evidence probability is true. Naive Bayes classifier presume the independent features

(3)  
$$\\text{P}\\left\\lbrack \\frac{\\text{V}}{\\text{U}\_{\\text{i}}} \\right\\rbrack = \\text{P}\\left\\lbrack \\frac{\\text{V}\_{1}}{\\text{U}\_{\\text{j}}} \\right\\rbrack \\ast \\text{P}\\left\\lbrack \\frac{\\text{V}\_{2}}{\\text{U}\_{\\text{j}}} \\right\\rbrack \\ast .. \\ast \\cdot \\text{P}\\left\\lbrack \\frac{\\text{V}\_{1}}{\\text{U}\_{\\text{n}}} \\right\\rbrack$$  

$P\\left\\lbrack \\frac{V}{U\_{1}} \\right\\rbrack - >$ The class Ui generating the instance V

$P\\left\\lbrack \\frac{V1}{Uj} \\right\\rbrack - >$ The probability of class Uj generating the observed value for feature1,

$P\\left\\lbrack \\frac{V2}{Uj} \\right\\rbrack - >$ The probability of class Uj generating the observed value for feature2,

$P\\left\\lbrack \\frac{Vn}{Uj} \\right\\rbrack - >$ The probability of class Uj generating the observed value for feature n.

1.  Bernoulli Naive Bayes Classifier: Bernoulli Naive Bayes works well with discrete data and it is based on Bernoulli distribution ([Ismail et al., 2016](#ch80.xhtml#ref80_18)). When the predictor is binary then Bernoulli Naive Bayes classifier is used.
    
    The Bernoulli Naive Bayes decision rule is given by
    
      
    *P*(*X*[*k*] ∣ *Y*) = *P*(*k* ∣ *Y*)*X*[*k*] + (1 − *P*(*k* ∣ *Y*))(1 − *X*[*k*])  
    
2.  Gaussian Naive Bayes

The best way to handle continuous data is the Gaussian Naive Bayes ([Kamel et al., 2019](#ch80.xhtml#ref80_19)). Naive Bayes is used when the data is discrete. Naive Bayes is a generative model and Gaussian Naive Bayes follows the Gaussian distribution (Normal Distribution). Gaussian distribution is widely used in statistical analysis and in machine learning. Gaussian distribution is a continuous probability distribution function ([Shen & Fang, 2020](#ch80.xhtml#ref80_20)).

The probability density function likelihood of the data is assumed to be

(5)  
$$P\\left\\lbrack \\frac{Xi}{Y = k} \\right\\rbrack = \\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2\\pi\\sigma\\text{k}^{2}}}e^{({- \\frac{xi - \\mu\\text{k}}{2\\sigma\\text{k}^{2}}})}$$  

Where

*   *Xi* is the continuous variable
*   *Y = k* is class k of Y.
*   σ is the variance of the variable X
*   p is defined as mean of the variable Xi for Y

Gaussian Naive Bayes Algorithm:

Input: A set of Medical chest X-ray

Output: Classified data and finding the accuracy

1.  Step 1 Collecting the dataset
2.  Step 2 Collected data is pre-processed. The image may contain noise which should be removed before the classification
3.  Step 2.1 The noise is removed by the Wiener filter method
4.  Step 3 GNBM is created using python
5.  Step 4 Split the dataset into training and testing data. Training data is 70% and testing data is 30%
6.  Step 5 Testing the data and predicting the class. Examine the training data of the GNBA and predict the class.
7.  Step 6 Assess the performance metrics of the data and store the data

## Implementation

Step 1: Medical data acquisition

Materials: Data is obtained from an Adapted version of Paul Mooney’s Chest X-Ray Images (Pneumonia) dataset.

Step 2: Processing: The first step in image classification is processing ([Arya & Semwal, 2017](#ch80.xhtml#ref80_21)) the image may contain noise that should be removed before the classification. Poisson noise, white noise, Gaussian noise, etc. are some of the noise that may be present in an image. To remove this noise, filters are used. Three types of filters are

1.  Wiener filter or linear filter
2.  Averaging filter or Mean filter
3.  Median filter

Step 2.1: i) Averaging filter: Averaging filter ([Shetti & Patil, 2017](#ch80.xhtml#ref80_22)) replaces each pixel element with the average of the pixel elements. This filter is simple and smoothes images by decreasing the intensity between two pixels. This is often used to reduce noise.

ii) Median Filter or Non-Linear Filter: It removes noise by preserving the edges. Each pixel element is replaced by the median of the intensity of the pixel element within the region.

Merits: Sharp details are retained. sensitivity to the outliers is less than the average filter. Effectively removes the outliers.

Demerits: Does not remove all kinds of noise

(iii) Wiener filter: It is a type 0 linear filter. The Wiener filter adopts to the image deviation. If the variance is small, wiener accomplish a very good smoothing and if the variance is large then it accomplishes it very less smoothing. It renders a better solution for determining computation difficulty in stationary signals. It provides a very good outcome in noise removal form the chest x-ray images. Comparing Median filters and Averaging filters, Wiener filters provides a very good result for filtering noise from chest X-ray.

In this paper, we use Wiener Filter ([Fig. 3](#ch80.xhtml#fig80_3)) to filter out noise

Step 5: For predicting the class, import the Gaussian Naive Bayes. Fit the model by passing the training and testing data.

Step 6: Performance Metrics and Result:

The performance metrics are accuracy, Precision, and Recall. These metrics are calculated from the confusion matrix classification of the class. This shows how Gaussian Naive Bayes from sklearn predicts the class using the test data.

Accuracy: Accuracy value is given as total number of True positive values obtained plus the True Negative value obtained divided by total samples obtained.

(6)  
$$\\text{Accuracy} = \\frac{\\text{TPV} + \\text{TNV}}{\\text{TPV} + \\text{FPV} + \\text{TNV} + \\text{FNV}}$$  

The accuracy by using Gaussian Naive Bayes Algorithm is 96.90.

Precision: Precision is defined as the total positive values obtained divided by the total positive values obtained (True Positive + False Positive)

(7)  
$$\\text{Precision} = \\frac{TPV}{TPV + FPV}$$  

The precision shows well with 96.1 than the Naive Bayes Classifier and Bernoulli Naive Bayes.

Recall or sensitivity: Recall is positive prediction divided by the total samples in the prediction.

(8)  
$$\\text{Sensivity} = \\frac{\\text{True~Positive}}{\\text{True~Positive} + \\text{False~Negative}}$$

## Conclusion

This idea is based on machine learning techniques for classifying medical health images. To classify the medical images, the proposed classification works efficiently. For the classification of Chest X-ray Gaussian Naive Bayes algorithm is used. Wiener filter method is applied to remove the noise and the GNBA model is implemented for Binary classification of Normal and Pneumonia chest data. The algorithm is simple and shows better performance metrics than the other algorithms.
